On Guard Before a Catastrophe

XXII. Do the leading elements know where we stand in the world? And if so — what way out are they seeking?
In society and in private conversations, at meetings and in institutions, people report on the terrible Jewish situation in Poland, which is growing from day to day more serious, more dangerous and more catastrophic. There is endless polemicising, discussions are held — and all without a goal, without awareness [?], without concrete proposals that might make it possible to change, to ease the grey life of the Jewish middle class in the country.
That is how it is: on the one hand we do not know how to continue the further course of the life-process. Earnings grow smaller and rarer from day to day. Systematically, and with enormous speed, we are being pushed out of almost all the branches of existence from which the Jew drew his livelihood for years, and in which he was regarded as unique in his generation, as a specialist in his field, as an achiever [?] and a man of brains whom no one could match.
Now all this has gone bankrupt: no matter in which field we have standing, we are not allowed to exist in our trades and branches, however capable we may be of working them.
There is a course [?] to push the Jew out of everywhere and from every side, without mercy. No reasons need be given at all. The name "Jew" is enough — it already says everything. So let us not persuade ourselves that we will no longer achieve anything [?] on account of our abilities, for, first, they are forcibly devalued, and second, we are pushed out by force from everywhere; and whatever else, strong we certainly are not, and with our weakened "might" we will certainly achieve nothing.
Why deceive ourselves, why play hide-and-seek, why shut our eyes to clear reality, when by doing so we commit a crime against ourselves and weaken still further these already sufficiently weakened forces of ours?
On the other hand, we cannot even stay standing on our goose-legs [?], for, although they have every chance of collapsing by themselves, they are being pushed to it with hasty momentum.
Under the prevailing conditions, where all kinds of individuals in various guises lie in wait for the Jew and would gladly drive him out and annihilate him, that is still not all. People keep crying that we are shunned [?] everywhere and not allowed near anything, any enterprise; systematically the ground is cut from under our feet, so that the prospects for the present are utterly pessimistic — yet even this is too little.
We cannot keep up with the tax screw that oppresses the middle class, and nevertheless they keep devising how to throw still more obligations on the already sufficiently burdened citizen. They keep planning new taxes, as though the existing ones came easily.
Not a few citizens are completely out of the running; they owe taxes that cannot be collected. They have been broken and have collapsed, and the government has lost them as payers for the "and present future" [sic; presumably: the present and the future].
It goes without saying that this is a loss for the state, for every citizen must contribute taxes to the government treasury; if not, it suffers damage and constant loss.
The government, however, wants to know nothing of this; it wants its quota, and if payers have dropped out, the quota must flow in from those who still pay — that is, from those who have not yet completely collapsed. And here the question arises: how long will they be able to hold out? And one thing more: those who pay, those who exist, those who struggle — they are visited constantly, to check whether they were not perhaps left in arrears [?] from before, or whether they did not pay less last year. No one at all stops to consider that such a payer must not be overburdened all at once, so that he should not thereby be made to slip and fall [?]. One must not forget that in such an unfortunate case no one benefits from him any more: for the government he is a "dead man", and he no longer employs anyone either. And the question arises: does it pay, from a business and economic standpoint, to adopt such harmful measures?
We are not a few — people who somehow or other [?] managed to reach some trade, and they cannot attain their goal, because they are burdened with debts to the Treasury (Skarb), and the end is that they are broken still further and consequently have nothing with which to get through the day. Such laggards are everywhere, and it would certainly pay the government to come to terms with them, so that it could win them back as living taxpayers.
Be that as it may, the situation is bitter both for the laggards and for those who tremble lest they too should have to come down to the same dreadful level.
True, not a little has already been written and said about this danger, but it must be stated that nothing more has been done about it, and that is certainly too little, too shallow, too delicate.
It is generally known that it is not easy to change the system that weighs upon the middle class — which, by the way, is recruited for the most part from our strata — but to stand aside at a distance, say that things are bad and bitter, and help groan along is far from just, for by that one certainly achieves nothing.
The Jewish people is utterly downcast; the circumstances in which we find ourselves ruin us to the highest degree. There is no courage, there is no strength for productive public work — but that does not mean that we may thereby end our public work.
One must summon one's strength and start helping to improve and ease Jewish existence, which finds itself in a state such as perhaps never before. We have already grown so accustomed to the bad that we will soon stop feeling altogether, and then, God forbid, there will be no one and nothing to save, no one and nothing to bring to a decent and humane condition.
Those who summon their strength and have the courage to look real reality in the face see that the situation is terrible, that it has truly reached the culminating point, that "the waters have come up to the soul" (Psalm 69:2), and that it is almost impossible to go on dragging the yoke like this without a term and without any guarantee [?] of a better tomorrow.
History has shown not only us Jews but all other peoples too that it did not grow light before it had first grown thoroughly dark — and it has not deceived us. With us, then, it is already thoroughly dark, terribly black; so when will a crumb of light appear, when will the sun shine for us?
But it would be nonsense in our times to rely on miracles; one must not stare at the sky and wait for consolation, for one must remember that by then [?] the soul — which we must guard like the apple of our eye — may, God forbid, expire.
Let us give ourselves a clear account of the situation; let people among us wake up and guard our vital interests; let our representatives — whoever and whatever they may be — remember that they must not remain indifferent to the masses, who are constantly sinking and are threatened with the danger of drowning.
At so grave a moment people must come to save the people, to pull it out of every danger.
At the present moment the people must be saved — spiritually and economically, physically and morally.
But when, and by whom, will it be saved from this terrible swamp of annihilation?
Chana Pesele Is Already Cleaning!...

[Humour — pre-Passover feuilleton.] Pre-Passover troubles of a married man.
By J. Oberżanek [?]
Chana Pesele is cleaning, and when my Chana Pesele cleans — woe and alas to me.
When Chana Pesele cleans she gets nervous, and when my Chana Pesele gets nervous everything goes „do góry nogami“ [Polish: upside down]: the home is no home, the children are no children, the husband is no husband, the chairs are turned over with their legs in the air, the bedding lies in the sideboard, the clothes in the kitchen and the dishes — in the bedroom, the windows are flung open[?]
— my Chana Pesele is cleaning..
Terror seizes me when the days before Passover come; before Passover I can find no place for myself: don't stand here and don't sit there, don't walk here and don't stand there; for sleep I sleep on the bare boards, and for food I eat a krechets [a flat round matzah] with sour milk; two whole weeks I wander about, I have neither day nor night, I wander about like a homeless lodger.
When the days before Passover come I pray to the Master of the Universe: great God, perform a miracle and send a flood upon the world, let it thunder and lighten, let it snow, let it hail, make a hurricane [„hu-ragan“] and an earthquake. A world upheaval. After all, You can do anything; with You everything is possible. Perform a miracle and make such[?] a „pogoda“ [Polish: weather] that no one can open a window, that no one can air out and clean — what does it matter to You, Master of the Universe, that I should have two weeks of rest, that I should have a quiet eve of Passover — have mercy on a married man!..
Well, and what does God do? He does exactly the opposite — He sends out a warm sun, warm weather, a brightness pours over God's little world — it is spring!..
My Chana Pesele feels the sun, and the house becomes a hell, a fair, a market, a tararam [uproar], a hubbub, noise and tumult; and as I appear on the threshold, my Chana Pesele meets me all worked up:
— Here already? Why were you in such a hurry? You want to eat lunch — stones!
I knew then that things were bitter, that if I said a word the scrubbing-brush would go „chad[?] rubo“[?]... and if I did not at once do a „chatil[?] vaharogo“[?], the dishes[?] would soon go into the [—][?] — so at once I turned the shaft right round [i.e. turned back].
My yidene [„my Jewess“ = my wife] sees that I really am leaving, she fills with anger and serenades[?] me with her Passover-eve repartee:
— What's this running off? What do you think, I'll work on my own[?] and you'll go off for a stroll — here you'll stay!
— What will I do here? — I asked my yidene.
— What do you mean, what will you do? — What all the men do in the week before Passover.
— What do all the men do in the week before Passover?
— They help their wives clean.
So I saw that my yidene was right: why should she work on her own[?] while I go for a stroll? I put on my wife's dressing-gown, tied my head up in a towel and set to the work.
First of all I tackled the windows, and one-two.. the first pane cracked after one wipe and a „trach“ — the second pane cracked; it did not take long and all the windows were „cleaned out“ — not a single pane was left...
After the windows I tackled the bedding — one pull and one beating... and the feathers flew like snow.
After the bedding I tackled the dishes; it did not take long — and no more dishes.
After the dishes I tackled the laundry: I filled the tub [balia] with water, poured and poured — and the tub was empty.
I stand by the tub and cannot understand the riddle; it is really the story of the burning bush [which burned but was not consumed].. I pour and pour and the tub is still empty.
The riddle was answered for me by the neighbour who lives behind me.
As I stand by the empty tub, my neighbour bursts in screaming „gevalt“:
— What is going on here at your place? There's a flood in my home, everything is swimming! The whole household has become a ruin-heap!
— What do you mean, I say — you're swimming? And what has that got to do with me?
My wife heard the dialogue between me and my neighbour, and came running with a „vayitsaku“ [„and they cried out“]:
— Idiot, shlimazl, good-for-nothing[?], you aren't even capable of tying a tail to a cat.
— What happened? — I did not understand what the women wanted of me.
— You beast — you didn't put the plug in! — my yidene gives me to understand.
Well, go know that a tub has a plug, and that if you don't put the plug in, the water pours down[?] to the neighbour and all the furniture, lock, stock and barrel [„mit hak un pak“], floats like Noah's ark..
After the tub I tackled the attic.
In the attic a war had just broken out between three women. The warring parties were tearing at each other's hair. Three sheitels [wigs] lay on the ground, the voices reached right up to heaven:
— A plague they'll hang today!
— Today I'll hang [the washing]!
— They won't live to hang today.
My yidene stretched out a washing line and the other one threw the line back down.
But I am a man after all — I seized the „okazja“ [Polish: opportunity], and while they were tearing at each other's hair, I hung up the washing.
Well, then there was a „wedding“: just to spite me the three women made peace, and before I could look round, my washing was lying on the ground.
That is how I helped this year with the Passover cleaning, and as you see I did it very „szykownie“ [Polish: stylishly] and „zgrabnie“ [Polish: deftly]; and if you, gentlemen, want a restful eve of Passover — help your wives clean for Passover,
Spring in Italy

[Travel letter — Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany; from our Zurich correspondent.]
(Travel letter).
From our Zurich correspondent Shloyme Frohman.

I am travelling on the international train Leipzig–Innsbruck–Rome through the Austrian Alps and the Brenner Pass. At Innsbruck a Hamburg theatre ballet boards the train; it tours [?] around Europe in order to prove to people in other countries the original "German art". The ballet consists of a director or manager and 12 young girls. The troupe is now going to Rome, where there is currently a boom ["high conjuncture"] and a "hausse" [?] for sentimental merchandise. As is well known, Mussolini preaches and propagates with all his strength the first commandment of Fascist Italy: "Marry young" [misprinted "yug" for "yung"]. Naturally, he does not mean by this only the words themselves [lit. "the haggadah"]; thus at every occasion of a state speech he blurts out all the secrets of the cheder, and then he babbles something about: "the role of numerous human material in future events"; "war is just as much a necessity, and just as dear to mankind, as the birth pangs of a child are to the mother". As one sees, then, these are very noble thoughts. But the masses, and chiefly the youth, suffer most from the circumstances of the time. For that very reason, however, youth has become a person of standing [meyukhes], a very important [vazhne] meyukhes, and at every opportunity one hears nothing but: "Youth, oh my crown and my treasure"... One is surely not obliged to draw an analogy [gezeyre-shove], or even to investigate and inquire what else the trickster still has up his sleeve; in short, the youth in Italy is getting married!... And not only the youth of Italy, but also the youth of the whole world. And in order to symbolise the marriage propaganda systematically, and so that the external noise-making apparatus and the hoo-ha-tararam, which is a main factor and a life-artery in a Fascist state, should also function well, — the Italian government has introduced something very important: all newly married couples in the world can travel on the Italian railways to Rome and back free of charge, apart from the other discounts that await [?] them in Rome during the seven days of the wedding feast [shivas yemey hamishte]. On a fixed day of the week all the marriage candidates march in military order across the main squares of Rome.

So I am now travelling on the international train through the Italian "Riviera", which is — as the Italians say — the paradise of Europe, and I will not forget to stop off [?] in Venice and Naples, and only then go on to Rome, where the world of feeling now blossoms in all its splendour and where the sentimentality industry, which is a significant economic factor in the national economy of Italy, is not now going through any crisis at all.

Among the young girls, or "girls", of a German theatre ballet there are two girls with quite black hair, a Semitic head structure and typically Jewish eyes, who make themselves particularly noticeable by wearing a necklace with a swastika on their breast.

The Germans have a bit of a Jewish trait: sitting together, one soon begins to talk, to tell each other stories, or — as the German word goes — to "quatschen" [chatter].

We carry on a conversation. I tell how, a day earlier, a German from Munich poured his heart out to me in Zurich: how he only now feels well and good and has become a bit of a human being again, being a few days in Switzerland, where he no longer has to join in and imitate the whole emptiness of always holding his hand up and shouting "Heil Hitler", when after all at every "Heil Hitler greeting" he would like to land [?] Hitler 2 slaps, even if he could not [printed "bekont" for "gekont"] get up alive again afterwards.

All the German women and men nod their heads enthusiastically. A sign [?] that they like such words, which they presumably have not heard in Germany for a long time; only the two girls with the black hair and the swastika on their breast remain cold, and one of them immediately starts answering me: "The one from Munich talked like that, but he is not a 'good German' in Munich". And the second black-haired girl adds: "Do you know, sir, that our greatest, glorious leader Adolf Hitler has saved world civilisation?"

The whole story is somewhat puzzling to me. I do not understand how in a chance Nazi-Hitlerite company there turn up precisely two such black-haired pious swastika-wearers.

I call the director aside and he whispers into my ear: "The two pious swastika girls are 2 Jewish girls. After the Aryan paragraph came into force, all members of the theatre ballet had to prove the 'kashrut' [printed "pshores"] of their parents up to the third generation; the two black girls were threatened with losing their posts, so he, the director, interceded for them and succeeded in 'proving' that up to the third generation they are 'pure Aryans'. The final arbiter [poysek akhron, ?] of the Nazi kashrut department ruled on this: since they are Aryans and yet do not have a quite Aryan appearance, they must therefore outwardly behave quite consistently in a German and National-Socialist manner and in this way openly demonstrate their Volkstum." He, the director, tells me this because he now knows that I too am a "Jew", and I will surely not inform on my "fellow believers".

— Jewish people, how poor and tragic your fate must be, when your children have already come to this.

We are already travelling on Italian soil. On both sides of the rails Italian road workers stand in groups, huddled together, shovels in their hands, to sweep away the snow (we are now in South Tyrol, a mountain region where snow is no rarity even in summer), and they keep on singing out loud merry Italian songs, "hee-ha-hoo, ee-hoo-ha, the world belongs to us". One could still be mistaken and think that here, to make the distinction [lehavdl], were only Kraków Hasidim. I learn afterwards that this is a Mussolinian contrivance. The world, the foreign travellers, should immediately, in the very first minute they cross Italian territory, convince themselves of the prosperity and the zest for life in "the new Fascist Italy", in the "golden Fascist era". For this purpose they simply hired all the Italian musicians [bal-menagnim], and set them up on every border with shovels in their hands. Overnight they thus became street sweepers and received the order: "Sing as much and as long as you can", "More singing than sweeping!"

We travel on. At every station Italians board with quite different faces: worn-out, overworked and melancholy faces. Now and then, now and then, one also notices the proud, laughing face of an "official" Fascist in his black uniform and a cap with a large ostrich feather on his head; for him, the official Fascist, things are going, it seems, very well in Italy. Not for nothing do people say that in Germany and in Italy there are today only 2 classes left: state-holders [Statthalter, governors] and mouth-holders [those who hold their tongues — a pun].

I try to start a conversation with an old man with the Fascist badge on his coat. He looks at me sharply until he gains [?] confidence in me, and answers my questions.
— Are you a Fascist?
— Yes, of course, all Italians are Fascists; foreign countries envy us and want to imitate us. But not everyone can do what we Italians can. With us there is no longer poor or rich, — all are equal. There exists only, as our Duce has already said, a difference in competence. One has the competence to be a banker and the other a tram conductor, — but all are equally happy...
— That is all well and good. But you have no freedom of the press in Italy, and not even freedom of opinion.
— What do we need freedom for, we have order! The Duce gave an order that all streets in Italy must be clean — and today you will not find a dirty street in Italy any more. The Duce gave an order that begging is no longer permitted — and no more [printed "I" for "you"] will beggars tug at your coat-tails in the street as before. Do you already know the newest saying of our Duce?
— What?
— "I assure you, Italians, if in 10 years Europe is still not Fascist, it will at least already be fascisised"...

— Milan, get off! — shouts the conductor. On the platform a woman runs after me and, half crying, asks me where Corso Littorio [printed "Karuza-litaria"] Street is. I give her to understand that I am a stranger and do not know any street in Milan. The woman thereupon casts a glance around on all sides and, having made sure that nobody is looking, stretches out her hand, weeping: "Signore, mi dia i soldi" [printed "Siniare, mi diai di salde"] (Sir, give me a few groszy).

In the great hall of the hotel hangs a big picture of the "Duce" Benito [printed "Benita"] Mussolini and a big picture of the Italian king Victor Emmanuel, with an inscription in kiddush-levone letters [i.e. huge letters]: "The new era in Fascist Italy".

Spring in Italy...
Milan, 22 March 1935.
Heard and Seen

By Ben Amotz.
Feitel the Shammes Becomes "Cultured"...
...I found him, Feitel, the Sosnowiec synagogue shammes, sitting over a Polish textbook. He was so absorbed in the "lesson" that he did not hear at all that a "stranger" was in his house.
At first I suspected him of not being in his right mind, for how can it be, and where does it come from, that a Jew of sixty, a [?] of the old generation, should in his old age take up "education" of all things? But hearing how Reb Feitel "struggles" [?] over every word of the A-B-C, how he exerts himself like the best pupil, I approached him with great respect, bowed and —
— "Przepraszam!" [Excuse me]
— You can speak Yiddish with me — Reb Feitel says to me with a smiling face — why are you so impressed that I am learning to read and write Polish?
— Przepraszam! I like it very much [?] that such a Jew, at his age, no evil eye, has a desire [?] for secular education, but...
— Ah, I understand already, you are surely wondering why I have not done this until now? Then, if you please, sit down and I will explain it to you.
— Bardzo dziękuję! [Thank you very much] But I beg you, Reb Feitel Krojn, tell it to me in Yiddish, because I want to understand it well.
— Are you mad or out of your mind — Reb Feitel gets angry — what language then should I speak to you in? I am not, after all, a członek [member] of the kehilla's "Rada Komisaryczna" [appointed commissarial council]...
— You don't know me from today or from yesterday. I am a Jew without any tricks, towards God and towards people; for decades I have served in holiness, and until today I never felt how bad it is when one is not "educated"; besides, what good would it have done me? If I don't sign any bills of exchange, why do I need to know Polish?
But, as King Solomon says, what reason does not bring, time brings — and the time has come: "there arose a new king" — there arose some "new, fashionable" dozores [kehilla board members], who behave exactly like Joseph with his brothers. When the brothers came to Joseph, he spoke Egyptian with them; but as soon as Joseph came to the brothers, he already spoke with them in the holy tongue...
Today's "Rada Komisaryczna Kahalna w Sosnowcu" also keeps to the same system. When they come into the synagogue, they speak mame-loshn [Yiddish], interwoven with Bible verses. But when they hold a session at the kehilla about shochetim, rabbis or the cemetery, then none of the "councillors" [?] will, God forbid, let slip any "żargonowe wyrazy" [jargon words]...
— Well, now you understand why in my old age I must learn languages? Look here, they handed me a bundle of "wezwania" [summonses] for the kehilla-tax payers about paying the tax; if at least the addresses were in Yiddish — no, not that either. So I must wander the streets and every time ask a passer-by to read me a couple of addresses. Oh, excuse me, panie [sir], I have already lost so much time; I have to "skończyć" [finish] the lesson.
— "Be—ge—ke—tse"...
Bowing [?], I gave praise to the Almighty for the great kindness of having blessed the town of Sosnowiec with a cultured council, thanks to which
— "Feitel the shammes becomes cultured"...
I'm "Provided For" with a Livelihood...
The door of the editorial office opens hastily and in falls a "two-faced" Jew, that is: one half of his face laughs and the other — cries. I have come here — he says — to announce the news that I, Menachem Mendel from the "Grablia" [?], am now provided for with a livelihood. You must "put" it in the paper.
Seeing that we take him for a candidate [?] for the [?], he takes a bundle of papers out of his pocket, lays them on the table and says:
— "Read them through, and you will understand."
We read the "papers", but it is hard to make sense of them. Even the only "lively" paper, on which it is written that the magistrate has put up for auction the Jew's property, consisting of 2 candlesticks worth 2 gilden [złoty], a glass "service" for 75 gr. [groszy] and a washstand for 2 gilden, does not yet explain the connection — that thanks to these papers the Jew is "provided for" with a livelihood...
Then one of the "opiekuns" [guardians] of social welfare comes to our aid, thanks to whom we become convinced that Menachem Mendel knows what he is saying; he is indeed
— "provided for with a livelihood"...
— How so? A simple calculation. The Jew was fined by the magistrate to pay 9 gilden or 3 days' arrest. Since the Jew does not have the 9 gilden, he went to jail and served out the penalty.
Then came the third party, the law, and demands the "board" [cost of keep] that Menachem Mendel from the "Grablia" received in jail...
And since Menachem Mendel will not manage to pay for the "board", he will have no choice but to "sit it out", then again it will come to paying, again he will sit, and so the wheel will turn: the larger the debt, the more days Menachem Mendel will sit.
— Yes, yes, it is just as the gentleman tells you. A worry has gone [?] off my head. I no longer wonder how I will make Passover — the magistrate already "takes care" of me.
— I'm provided for with a livelihood...
Black Clouds

By S. Rotenberg.
Ever since Hitler, immediately after coming to power, began to root out Jews, socialists and communists, the diplomats cared very little about this "humanitarian cleansing". After all, there exists some international principle of not interfering in other people's internal affairs. Let a permanent "night of the long knives" reign there, let them violate and murder innocent people there. As long as[?] such a "trifle" does not threaten one's own house, the matter is in perfect order. And that is precisely why none of the European states ever dared to intervene over the sadistic barbarism in Nazi-land. For the gentlemen diplomats the main thing, after all, is to preserve "peace", and it is worth it that the Nazi "Moloch" should devour a few tens of thousands of its own victims, as long as its attention is diverted from the surrounding neighbours.
But after the visit of the English ministers in Berlin, it must have become clear even to the diplomatic conjurers that the Hitlerite beast had merely sharpened its teeth on Jews and Marxists, in order to be able to use them at the proper moment against the whole world.
Hitler has openly and cynically declared that he will arm without limits on land, sea and air, and that he will take back the German territories and colonies that were torn away. Such a "love" declaration means not only tearing up the Treaty of Versailles and spitting on the League of Nations, but it is a shameful provocation to war.
Hitler belongs[?], without a doubt, to the type of tyrant-psychopaths known in history for their bloody deeds. For only a mentally sick despot can demand of a great power such as the Soviet Union that it should transfer its army to the Far East and that its western borders should remain undefended and thus exposed to the "mercy" of the Nazi gladiators.
No more and no less: the preachers of idolatrous barbarism, those pirates who organise gangster and kidnapper gangs that rob people and murder them — these outcasts want to become the bearers of civilisation in Europe.
As we write these lines we do not yet know the result of the negotiations between the English minister Eden and the Soviet government. One thing, however, is certain: if Europe does not want to be devoured by the Nazi hydra, there is only one effective means — a military convention of all the great powers in Europe, the Soviet Union included. All the statesmen of Europe must[?] remember that just as in ancient Rome the censor Cato ended his speech at every session of the Senate with the words "Carthage must be destroyed", so they must always keep before their eyes the slogan: "Hitler-land (not Germany) must disappear". Otherwise Europe faces the danger of a new Hunnish invasion, of a bloody swastika crusade against the whole of human culture and civilisation.
* * *
There are still naive people who believe that fascism (need not necessarily be bound up with antisemitism. As an example they pointed to Italy, where a fascist regime par excellence reigns, and yet not the slightest sign of an antisemitic movement is to be seen there.
These people will now be sorely disappointed, because the "humanitarian" Italian fascism too has shown its [true?] face.
Last week the official organ of the Fascist Party in Italy, "Il Regime Fascista", came out with a venomous, Jew-devouring article, entirely in Hitler's style. In it every "logical argument" for removing the Jews from social, economic and political life finds expression. That these are not mere phrases is proved by the fact that recently the Jewish finance minister, Mr. Guido Jung, was indeed removed from his post, without any special official reason.
It is only a question of time: sooner or later fascist regimes are bound to pounce on the Jews, because this is an ultra-chauvinist movement that tolerates no "aliens".
* * *
We cannot, God forbid, suspect the decisive factors in Poland today of being philosemitically inclined. On the contrary, all the deeds done so far with regard to the Jews bear witness that we are dealing here with a systematically calculated plan to eliminate the Jews from political and social life. True, this is not done with any outward effect, with pomp as under Hitler[?], but in a diplomatic manner, "gentlemanly" and "parliamentary", so as to keep up appearances outwardly.
But what such a spectacle should look like in its full splendour and glitter, without a fig leaf, was shown by the Endeks [National Democrats] in the Łódź city council. Such anti-Jewish laws and clauses were adopted there that one need not be ashamed of them at all in the "Third Reich".
It is indeed a great riddle how Łódź, which has a glorious, revolutionary past behind it, could become an Endek fortress? Some devilish[?] trick must surely have been played there; otherwise such a paradox is quite unthinkable.
Unfortunately we face a sad fact which shows clearly that our home-grown Hitlerites lag in no respect behind their teacher, and moreover display[?] all the "virtues" and "talents" to surpass him.
* * *
Black clouds cover the sky; a dark night of cannibalistic hatred of man and murder-psychosis reigns. Yet one must not despair, for history teaches us that precisely in times of twilight in society new teachings and ideas were born, developed and later became mighty, leading mankind to a better and more beautiful life.
The downfall of tsarist Russia can serve as a classic proof of this eternal[?] historical truth.
Spring in Będzin (A Sketch)

[Będzin — sketch.]
Lucky at least that spring has not gone on strike this year in Będzin. It does its work faithfully, brightens and whitens our little streets, as if someone were whitewashing a house on the eve of Passover... and a lovely warmth in the street — oh, how good! One could already boldly throw off the winter coat, if only the suit were in order...
The same goes for the galoshes. Many people, you will see, still drag the galoshes about on themselves, although the pavements gleam white and are dry as a bone. The reason is quite simple: during the winter the shoes were brought to such a dangerous state that their owners now have to walk on their socks... To buy a pair of new shoes is beyond their means right now, so the shame is covered with the galoshes...
The girls and the women, on the other hand, have already managed to treat themselves to such small fashionable spring hats, and they wear them on the very top of the head with such pride, just as if they with their hats had brought spring down into God's world... Who knows how many tears a girl shed before she begged the few gulden [złoty] for the hat out of her poor father?... But hush, quiet... nothing! Now they strut along the sun-warmed Małachowska Street [ul. Małachowskiego] and cast glances at the strolling students, who have come home for Passover from Kraków, Warsaw and a number of other university towns, where the Jew is beaten or simply hated..
Nevertheless they are merry, the student crowd; the whole street is full of their youthful chatter and laughter; they rejoice in their home town, in the familiar shops, which have decked out their shop windows for the holiday with every good thing — with coloured fabrics, shirts, kerchiefs — and all of it shimmers and shines in the pouring sun, begging to be greeted with „Tiskhadesh“ [wear it in good health]...
— One could live — the crowd laughs — only they don't let you!...
Opposite, on the other, shady pavement, Jews are milling about, talking, gesturing with their hands out of the wish to work out some little business deal.
— There goes my student! — a father points out with relish his own, his son, and the wrinkled face lights up with fatherly happiness. But soon the Jew turns sad again, lowers his head with a Menachem-Mendel-like resignation, and ponders, it seems, how to bring Passover into the house...
A. Brzeziński.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion

[Oneg Shabbat — weekly Torah portion.]
Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on the portion of this week
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parshat Tazria
The portion.
—o—
a) „If a woman conceive“ (12:2)
„Rabbi Simlai said: just as man was created after every beast, animal and bird in the work of Creation — so his law was set out after the law of beast, animal and bird“. Rashi.
Every animal, beast and bird is the embodiment of a good or a bad trait. A cat is the embodiment of modesty, a raven — of cruelty, and so on. Man was created after all the beasts, animals and birds, and contained within himself all their good and bad traits together, which he must refine and elevate... „Sade[?] Tevuot“.
—o—
b) „As in the days of the separation for her infirmity shall she be unclean“ (ibid.)
„All our honour [is credited] among the nations, and our abomination is like the impurity of a niddah“.
If a Jew invents something, it is credited to science and the Jewish origin of the inventor is completely concealed; but if a Jew commits the slightest offence, his whole people is at once defamed, a „drop of blood the size of a mustard seed“ is blown up and proclaimed at the top of one's voice.. „Knesset Yisrael“.
—o—
c) „And on the eighth day he shall be circumcised“ (ibid., 3)
„We are counted as sheep for the slaughter — this is circumcision, which was given on the eighth day“. Gittin 57.
Right from birth the Jew is accustomed to self-sacrifice, to being ready to give his blood... „This is circumcision“ — the meaning of circumcision is „we are counted as sheep for the slaughter“, for as a Jew the tender circumcised infant is already prepared[?] as a sacrifice. And this is the intention of Tanya Rabbati, §95: „Whoever brings[?] his son to circumcision is as if the High Priest offered his meal-offering“ — the young Jew is already a sacrifice.
And therefore the Gemara hints: „this is circumcision, which was given on the e i g h t h day“, because the verse „For Your sake we are killed all the day, we are counted as sheep for the slaughter“ stamps[?] martyrs... „Divrei Yitzchak“.
• • •
„As he entered into the covenant, so may he enter into Torah, the wedding canopy and good deeds“.
About the good deeds of his children a Jew worries only once: at the first commandment, at the circumcision... After that he already forgets about the child's religious upbringing. Therefore we say „As he entered into the covenant, so may he enter into Torah, the wedding canopy and good deeds“ — that later too the father should take an interest in the child's good deeds... „Tokhachat Chaim“.
—o—
d) „And it be in the skin of his flesh like the plague of leprosy“ (13:2)
„And it be in the skin of his flesh like the plague of leprosy“ — since in this world the priest sees the plagues, but in the time to come the Holy One, blessed be He, said: I will purify you“.
„In this world the priest sees the plagues“. Only the priest knows a person's plague; the person himself does not know it, for if a person knew his own plague, he would heal it at once and it would not have come out into the open. But in the time to come: „I will purify you“ — God will illuminate your soul, and then you will see your plagues yourselves and will not need to turn to a priest to see them. And if you yourselves see your inner plagues, you will as a matter of course already be healed... The Maggid of Dubno.
—o—
e) „And it have turned the hair white“ (ibid., 10)
White is always a sign of purity, cleanness, grace; only with plagues is white hair a sign of impurity, because it means that the „plague already has grey hair“, as the saying goes — it is an old leprosy, and then it is much harder to heal.. Rabbi Yonatan Eybeschütz.
—o—
f) „And there be quick raw flesh in the rising“ (ibid.)
This too is a sign of impurity: when from above the plague is healed, smooth, and under the healthy flesh there is the bright spot — these are those hypocrites who present themselves as upright and are in truth rotten inside... „Kli Yakar“.
—o—
g) „It is all turned white: he is clean“ (ibid., 13)
„The son of David will not come until the whole kingdom turns to heresy, as it is said: it is all turned white, he is clean“. Sanhedrin 97.
If „it is all turned white“ — the whole world will be turned to heresy, will become nothing but impurity — „he is clean“: the end must already come, for if all are guilty the son of David must come. Worse is when the impurity is still not so conspicuous... Ibid.
• • •
„Out of the north the evil shall break forth“ [tzafun — also „hidden“].
From those in whom the evil is tzafun, hidden — from them the evil breaks forth; they are the most dangerous people... „Sha'ar Bat Rabim“.
• • •
„The son of David comes only in a generation that is wholly guilty or in a generation that is wholly innocent“.
It does not mean that the generation will be either wholly guilty or wholly innocent, but that each person for himself will be either wholly innocent or wholly guilty — not a mixture of both... „Meimei ha-Da'at“[?].
—o—
h) „When a man or woman hath a plague upon h i m“ (ibid., 29)
„When a man or woman hath upon them“ — so it should have been according to the language of the verse. But here the verse speaks only of the man, therefore „hath upon h i m“, and „or woman“ means that the woman too is one of the plagues, in the sense of „a bad wife is leprosy to her husband“.
R' Yitzchak Skrzyner[?]. „Burekh halme“[?].
The Mamzer (29)

[Serialized novel — "The Mamzer"; installment 29, chapter 2.]
Adv. S. Geliszpawski [?].

A gripping tragic novel of a prodigy (ilui).

Chapter 2.

In the yeshiva sits the rebbe, Reb Yochanan, and recounts in a chant the torments in the World to Come for the wicked and the heretics.

— There are demons there with thousands of eyes, which torture the sinful man by their mere gaze..

— Ai, ai, ai — he sings along — and there are fires there called darkness; the smallest little fire there, in the next world, scalds [?] sixty times more fiercely than the greatest fire in this world — and all for the bit of pleasure a man craves in this world.

At a lectern, set apart from everyone, stands Moshele too.

For six years now he has been here, Moshele Rozen [?], with his mother, in this forsaken little town.

Soon after the divorce they came here. Chanele set herself up here with a little spice shop. She is content: her Moshele is growing into a prodigy, the one and only in the yeshiva; all the fathers and mothers hold him up as a blessing for their own children; her only consolation in life is now Moshele.

She has already somewhat forgotten her sufferings; she does not want to remember at all. She thanks God every day when she closes the shop and goes into the house to prepare food for Moshele, who comes home late from the study house. She thanks God that He brought her here, to this little town, where nobody knows about her and about Moshele's misfortune.

She has a good name in the town. Just as in Knin [?], here too she runs to poor sick people and brings them help; whenever a misfortune happens, people turn to Chanele, and she refuses no one, and if she can she also gives an interest-free loan (gemilut chesed).

Only Moshele alone has not forgotten his misfortune: every day, every hour he remembers that he is a mamzer, but he seeks to plead the cause even of a mamzer. He argues it out with the Master of the Universe and tries to interpret the verse "A mamzer shall not enter the congregation of the Lord" [Deut. 23:3] so that this is not what the Torah means; on the contrary, the Gemara says: better a mamzer who is a scholar than a High Priest who is an ignoramus.

And as he stands so deep in his thoughts, another student comes up to him — Motele is his name — and interrupts his thoughts with a question:

— Moshele, I want to ask you a difficulty (kashya).

Moshele starts up from his sunken thoughts.

— Ask — he says — I'm listening.

— I have already — says Motele — asked many of the boys, and they don't answer me to the point. So I've come to you, so that you should make it clear to me.

— Let me hear the kashya already — says Moshele impatiently.

— King Solomon — says Motele in a Gemara chant — says in Ecclesiastes: I have seen servants riding on horses and princes walking on foot [Eccl. 10:7]. How does King Solomon, the wisest of the wise, come to say such a foolish thing? How can it be that lords should walk on foot and servants ride on horses?

— What did the friends answer you? — says Moshele.

— What do I know — nonsense. One says that it is an allusion to our present time, to the revolutions.

A light smile appears on Moshele's face.

— Do you want to know — he says — the logical interpretation of the verse? I don't know whether it is logical, but I interpret it the way I understand it. The order of the world among the lords [the squires, "pritzim"] is this: when they are young they love to live it up. The father is rich, there is money without limit, so one lives and enjoys oneself; nobody thinks about marrying, and they remain bachelors until thirty. But there is, after all, the Evil Inclination, which talks them into sin — so they pick out a pretty maidservant from those in the manor and live with her, and when the time comes that the maid is to give birth to a child, the squire gives her a few hundred rubles and drives her out. Whose blood flows in the child? The squire's; that is, the maid gives birth to a squire. But what becomes of that child, in whom the noble blood flows? He becomes a shepherd. And the squire again picks out a second, a third, and all of them have children by him.

But when the squire is already getting old, forty, he begins to think about marrying, and if marry — he wants a young lady of the nobility. And one finds a young, beautiful, poor noblewoman who marries him. You understand, of course, that the forty-year-old squire, who has already lived with several maidservants, is already a worn-out man. His wife, whose blood boils in her veins, picks out a handsome servant from those in the manor, lives with him and has a child by him — who is born a servant. That is to say, the children the maidservant bore to the squire, who are real lords, walk on foot like servants. Do you understand now?

— Bless you, Moshele, this I do understand now; this does make sense to the mind.

Three knocks of the beadle with a wooden hammer on the door announce to the yeshiva boys that lunch is ready.

There is a rush to the door, and in the yeshiva the crooked columns of dust grow thicker, settling on the closed Gemaras and holy books.

In the afternoon the head of the yeshiva, Reb Leibl, calls Moshele to him and cross-examines him: why does he interpret verses according to a heretical plain meaning?

— God forbid, Rebbe, that is not what I am saying. I am only saying that we do not interpret it correctly, because fundamentally, Rebbe, you must after all agree that a man does not lift [—] a finger unless it has been decreed on high; nothing, not even a little blade of grass, is created without the Master of the Universe, all the more so a living soul; and that this is so — we say every day the prayer "Who formed man" (asher yatzar et ha-adam) — that He alone created man.

— Agreed, agreed — says Reb Dudl with closed eyes, listening intently to Moshele's words.

— And if this is so — Moshele goes on with fervour — if He creates everything, man as well, then He created the mamzer too, and only with His consent did he come into the world. Did the mamzer, then, want to be born? No — a man is born by force; and if that is so, if he did not want to be created and born, and all this was done without his will, why should he stand lower than his fellow man?

— What is the mamzer guilty of, if he came into the world because of the sin of two people? Why should he be guilty? Why should he deserve [?] to be thrust out of our society and not be allowed to marry a Jewish daughter — and do you really believe that God commanded this?

For a short while it was quiet in the room. Reb Dudl had sat the whole time with closed eyes, his head propped on his right hand, breathing heavily.

— Rebbe — Moshele stands up and lays a Gemara down beside him — Rebbe, here you have before you a Gemara which says that if a son strikes his father he deserves the death penalty, and the same Gemara at once raises a difficulty on the spot: and what if the one struck is not his father — perhaps she sinned with another man and he was born of him? And if so, why should he deserve the death penalty? Rebbe, where is the certainty? The certainty?..

— And why, when one makes a "Mi shebeirach" for a sick person, does one mention specifically the mother's name and not the father's — why is that so? Is there then a suspicion that he is not the son of so-and-so? That means there is no certainty at all.

— Here you want to take me as a son-in-law. How do you know, Rebbe, that I am not a mamzer? Perhaps I am not allowed to marry your daughter at all?

— Easy now — Reb Dudl tears himself from his seat — don't talk nonsense, I beg you, as your rebbe: throw away all these inquiries, they lead to no good. Live as God commanded, as all of us live. What for set yourself against a whole world? One must go with the current and not against it, because that is a danger.

— You are mistaken, Rebbe — says Moshele — on the contrary, going with the current is sometimes a greater danger than going against it. Take, for example, the boatman. If he lets himself rely on the current of the water, the water can carry him off God knows where. But he who steers against the current avoids every little hill, every stone, and is careful that the boat should not carry him off to where there is danger for him. So, one need not always go with the current.

— But Moshele, have pity on your mother — how broken her heart will be when she learns that Reb Leibl has driven you out of the yeshiva; how great her sufferings will be.

— You are right, Rebbe, my mother will suffer from it, but I am already suffering; my heart is already broken, my heart already aches and will ache for a long time yet — he said, broken, and went out of the room.

And Moshele did not throw away his thoughts, did not give up waging a struggle for the truth. Day and night he sat over holy books and Gemaras, searching and gathering everything that had a bearing on the verse in the Torah where a mamzer is spoken of.

And there were different kinds of boys in the yeshiva. There were those who agreed with Moshele, who secretly searched and pondered together with him over the verse "A mamzer shall not enter the congregation of the Lord" and proved that Moshele was right.

And again there were those who avoided him and carried various denunciations about Moshele to Reb Leibl, until he forbade him to come to the yeshiva.

But Moshele did not lose heart; with more courage he threw himself into study, avoiding people — except the town teacher, with whom he used to study secular subjects in the forest.

Many boys considered the expulsion of Moshele from the yeshiva an injustice. People were angry at Reb Leibl and did not even want to come to the lesson. Reb Dudl, too, did not agree and looked askance at it.

“The Cooking Ladle” — I Still Have Time Until Passover.

[“Der Kokh-Lefl” — humour and satire column; Passover, the economic crisis, small traders.]
Humour and satire. Compiled by Amotzlo.
Who reckons with the calendar today? Who cares about dates and deadlines?
Promissory notes get prolonged, taxes get prolonged, rent gets prolonged, even states have to resort to prolongations — so why should I, Berl the small trader, keep the deadline of Passover? So what [“mele”] if the calendar writes that on the night of the fourteenth of Nisan it is Passover! The calendar was printed back in the good years, but today who can put up with such whims and make Passover precisely on the 14th of Nisan?!
So I actually pushed through a unanimous resolution among my household that we take a prolongation: Passover is postponed in our house to Shavuot.
Did I have any other choice?
Just listen:
I applied for a loan at the co-operative[?] loan fund; whole piles of applications are lying there, and if [printed “also”] I get my loan by Shavuot, they will be quite fine people.
Once the American uncle used to help me out with Passover. Just yesterday I got a friendly little letter[?] from him, that he very much regrets that this year he has to break the “tradition” and not send anything for Passover. In America — he writes — there is a severe crisis today, and as the astrologers predict, the crisis will end at the latest around Shavuot. He therefore hopes that he will send me the Passover money for Shavuot.
Seeing that I would no longer be able to make Passover with honour [printed “barukh kavod”], I cast off the shame and went to ask for kimcha de-Pischa [Passover flour relief]; at the kehilla [misprinted “kekhke”] they tell me that I came too late, the kimcha campaign is going very slowly, and besides, to satisfy everyone they would have had to collect money until Shavuot.
If everyone has prolonged for me until Shavuot, why shouldn't I prolong until Shavuot? What do I really care if Passover will be at Shavuot, Shavuot at Sukkot and Sukkot at Passover?
So what — the calendar writes.
Yosef.
Chatzkele[?] “Kol-Bonik” Has the Floor

[“Der Kokh-Lefl” — satire in the popular dialect of the Podzamcze poor; Będzin, Passover.]
In short [“aklal”], it's already the eve of Passover with us; also[?] on the “Zhimne” [Zimna?] D. things are already moving: they scrub and they tidy, they stuff the straw sacks, the rag-man [szmaciarz] collects the rags and gives glasses and “matzibara klapers” [?matzo implements] in exchange. It's lively now on the “Zhimna”.
And what do you see at the “ristocrats” [aristocrats] on Passover eve? Nothing. With them, with the “ristocracy”, it's always the same [“galik”]: at Sukkot they carouse in the rooms, on Yom Kippur [“Yankiper”] they stuff themselves like bears, and before Passover it's with them like before Shavuot [“Shvies”] — they don't tidy, don't scrub, don't fill the mattresses [sienniki], don't whitewash the stove [“koymim”], don't clear out the cupboard, don't strew yellow sand on the floor [podłoga] — important [ważni] people they are. Though you may [?]... — long live the Podzamcze lane!
Just one thing I want to tell you: don't go to the kehilla [“kile”] for another Passover campaign; those who [?“kumtshin”] the [?“peterelen”] won't give you anything[?]; “strength” to our enemies! About what the Podzamcze lane got from the kehilla for Passover, the schmaltz-bellies in the [?] “lastige yebitses” with the “garflin” [?] said: they shall have charoset [“khroyses”], and maror upon maror, and borscht upon borscht.
Don't worry[?] at all, lads [“Yasn”?]: we on the “Zhimne” will also have for Passover, and even more than the rich [“gnidim”], and do you know what we will have?
— Plagues [“makkes”].
I've finished [“khob geshkontshet”, from Polish skończyć].

What Is Happening in Zagłębie? — Będzin: The Discount Bank Must Be Preserved

[Local section header; Będzin — economy, credit institutions.]
What is happening in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 2 Nisan 5695 — piątek 5 kwietnia 1935 [Friday, 5 April 1935].)
Będzin
The Discount Bank must be preserved
with its present public character, the general meeting resolves.
In the hall of "Piast" the annual general meeting of the Discount Bank took place on Sunday afternoon; the bank is, as is known, the remnant of the Cooperative Bank in our town.
The chairman, Mr. A. Liwer, opens the meeting and hands the chair over to Mr. Sz. Fridler. As assessors: Iser Kryclar, Józef Kurc and secretary J. Granek.
The report on the bank's activity so far is delivered by Mr. Liwer. Speaking about the further existence of the bank, Mr. Liwer declares that 3 persons are offering to put up a sum of 15,000 zł., on condition that they are elected to the board.
Mr. Józef Rus comes out against Mr. Liwer's concept. These persons — says Mr. R. — are not small traders, and consequently they will not have the interest of the small merchants at heart, for whom the bank must exist.
A discussion develops on the question, after which Mr. Liwer's proposal is rejected. The latter then announces that he casts off the responsibility and no longer wants to manage the bank. Mr. G. Landner, too, declares that he will not accept the mandate on the board.
Mr. Landner then proposes to cover the loss with the share capital. After the discussion on this proposal, Mr. Gutensztajn's amendment is adopted, that the loss should be covered with 50 percent of the share capital.
After the budget for the year 1935 is adopted, the following board and council are elected by acclamation: Jakub Gelbard, Józef Rus, Jehoszua Klajman, Hercke Kornbrot and Szaul Fridler. Deputies: Jakub Winer and Szymon Kruk.
To the supervisory council: Herman Strachlic, Pinchas Jakubowski, Josel Szwajcer, Dawid Gutensztajn, Dawid Gitler, Szlomo Rajchman and Herszel Staszycki[?]. Deputies: Herszel Zylbersztajn, Wolf Merin and K. Wajde[?].

A Day Before the Divorce, the Wife Died...

[Będzin — human interest.]
He is 70[?] and she is 70.
In the good years the childless couple made a living from a shop, conducted themselves as God commanded, and he devoted his free hours to communal work, founded institutions and in time became a real public figure ("klal-mentsh").
Suddenly bitter years began for the couple: the wife fell ill with a chronic disease, the little shop went downhill, the landlord already had an eviction order for the flat, and there was no other choice but for the couple to separate: "she" was taken into an old-age home ("Moshav Zkenim"), and "he" stayed with a relative in Sosnowiec.
After a few months "he" realised that such a life had no purpose for him and decided to divorce.
The divorce was set for Sunday at the local rabbinate, but on Saturday night "he" received the news that "she" had died...
“The shochtim will slaughter and Gershon will do the inspection”...

[Będzin — ritual slaughter and kashrut.] “The shochtim will slaughter and Gershon will do the inspection”...
On Tuesday the following characteristic incident took place at the local slaughterhouse:
One of the shochtim (ritual slaughterers), who was engaged in the bedikah (inspection), found a serious sirkha (lung adhesion) on the lung of Gershon Waks’s beast and said:
“It is no good,” said the shochet, “according to Torah law (d"t) this sirkha cannot be removed.” The other shochtim expressed the same opinion. It turned out, however, that removing the sirkha was not such a difficult matter, for in the presence of the shochtim the same butcher, Gershon Waks, removed the sirkha, and then the shochtim said that the beast was kosher...
“Such a case,” several of the butchers explain to us, “has never yet happened at the local slaughterhouse. We,” they say, “are now of the opinion that there is no need at all to engage a fourth shochet any more, since for the slaughtering alone 3 shochtim are enough — so ‘the shochtim will slaughter and Gershon will do the inspection’...”

Dispute between the bakers and the rabbinate — over the fee for koshering the ovens.

[Będzin — rabbinate, matzo baking.] Dispute between the bakers and the rabbinate
over the fee for koshering the ovens.
In every town and shtetl matzos are already being baked; the only exception is Będzin, where the tradition of starting to bake on Rosh Chodesh Nisan is still kept.
This year, however, the traditional date has been delayed because of the dispute between the bakers and the rabbinate.
The dispute consists in this: the rabbinate demands 35 zł. for koshering an oven and for maintaining the... chief supervisors (“oyber ne’emonim”).
The bakers want to give only 20 zł. and do not want to recognise the chief supervisors.
In this connection a delegation of the bakers turned to the rabbinate with the request that the burden of the chief supervisors be lifted from them.
The intervention brought no result whatsoever, because the rabbinate will not give up its decision. “If you cannot pay the price demanded,” one of the rabbinate declared, “then don’t bake.”
Legionnaires’ rally in Czeladź — a splendid gift [?] from the Jewish community to the voivode.

A splendid gift [?] from the Jewish community to the voivode.
On Sunday a regional rally of Legionnaire delegates from the Będzin, Zawiercie, Częstochowa and Olkusz districts (powiats) was held in Czeladź.
The rally, which had a festive character, was attended by the Kielce voivode Dr. Dziadosz, starostas and other high state officials.
The opening took place in the market square of Czeladź, where a triumphal arch had been erected.
The reception committee sent Rabbi Lewental an invitation for the local Jewish inhabitants, and the following were delegated: Rabbi Lewental, Chaim Szwajcer, Herman Rechnic and Elimelech Binensztok.
The Czeladź mayor Dorabczyński [?] welcomes the Mr. Voivode, presenting him with bread and salt. The tray is made of coal.

On this occasion the rabbi presents the voivode with a magnificent Eretz Israel album as a gift from the Jewish community of Czeladź, for which the voivode expresses warm thanks to the Jewish delegation.
After the speeches and the adoption of a series of resolutions, telegrams of greeting were sent to the President of the State, Marshal Piłsudski and Premier Sławek.

“The more they multiplied and the more they spread”... — Triplets born on the way to Eretz Israel.

Triplets born on the way to Eretz Israel.
The hundreds of olim (immigrants to Palestine) who travelled last Tuesday by the express train to Trieste had a rare attraction.
On this train travelled the G. family from the shtetl of Kłobuck. As Mrs. G. was expecting to give birth any day, the family had taken a whole compartment for themselves.

And indeed it did not take long: while the express was between Dąbrowa and Sosnowiec, Mrs. G. gave birth to triplets...
The mother and the three new olim to Eretz Israel are feeling lively and well.
“The ‘Pani’ sent him for the laundry”...

[Life in Kielce] Desperate Cries for Help from Two Thousand Poor Families for Passover Relief!

[Kielce — Kehilla and relief; Passover.]
Life in Kielce.
(Date boxes: Friday, 2 Nisan 5695 — piątek 5 kwietnia 1935 [Friday, 5 April 1935].)
Desperate cries for help from two thousand poor families for Passover relief!
As we have already written, the Kielce kehilla has taken it upon itself to carry out the kimcha (Passover flour) campaign.
For this purpose the kehilla board turned with a request to the kehilla taxpayers ("etat-payers"), that each of them give a contribution[?] ("kanta") according to the 1935 tax assessment (the "etat").
This is the only source from which the kehilla can put together the sum needed for the Passover campaign, for which about five thousand Jewish souls are waiting, among them Jews who last year were givers and today have become receivers.
The kehilla must also provide Passover food for the Jewish soldiers, the HeChalutz kibbutzim in Kielce, the orphans of the local orphanage, the old-age home, the poor Jewish children in the public schools, the military and civilian prisoners, etc.
For all this the kehilla needs a minimum sum of 10—12 thousand złoty. Otherwise there is a danger that hundreds of Jewish families will, God forbid, eat chametz on Passover; and this absolutely necessary sum the kehilla can obtain only from the taxpayers.
To our greatest regret, the greater part of the taxpayers has not found it necessary to respond to the kehilla's request and does not wish to take an interest in the kimcha campaign, traditional for generations.
Such disregard must not and will[?] in no way be tolerated. All well-off taxpayers, and also those who are not taxpayers, if they have any possibility at all of helping the Passover campaign, must show their help at once. There is no time for deliberating — it is late enough already!
Already the desperate S.O.S. cries of the five thousand Jewish souls of our town resound loudly in the Jewish street in Kielce, calling on all of us not to forget them on our festival of freedom, Passover!
A Gift from Kielce Jews to a Parish

[Kielce — Jews and neighbours; court.]
In our town and in the whole surrounding area people are talking about the following curious fact.
The inhabitant of the village of Prushilik[?] beyond Kielce, Mr. Janas, donated a plot to the local church parish. The local priest did not hurry to carry out the notarial formalities, but relied on the word of the plot's owner.
A good while passed, the wheel turned for Janas, he became poor, and he sold the donated plot to three Jews from Volhynia[?].
When it became known in the village that the plot which was to have been for the parish had passed into the hands of Jewish property-owners, an antisemitic agitation began under the slogan that "the Jews took the plot by fraudulent means".
Besides this, a petition was filed in the name of the local priest at the Kielce district court to annul the purchase of the plot.
The trial, which was set for 22 March, aroused tremendous interest in Jewish and public circles, so that the courtroom was packed full with curious people from the whole area. But before the court proceedings began, the defender of the Jewish property-owners, the advocate Mr. Fenigsztajn, made a statement which caused a surprising sensation in the courtroom: namely, the advocate declared that the Jewish owners were giving the plot away as a gift to a parish.
After the sensational statement the priest took the floor and expressed warm thanks to the Jewish property-owners for their noble deed.
Man Gone Mad Tries to Strangle 2 Jewish Women

After 20 Years, "Risen in the Resurrection of the Dead"...
A Hasidic Jew Demands Money for Tombstones for His Living Family

[Siewierz — family fraud.] The little town of Siewierz (Będzin district) is in an uproar; people have forgotten their everyday worries and are talking about the interesting story in which the leading role is played by the Hasidic Jew, gabbai of the local Chevra Kadisha, who "possesses" eagle's wings...
The story goes like this:
20 years ago the Waksman family of Siewierz emigrated to America. Mrs. Waksman left behind in Siewierz 2 brothers and a younger sister.
All this time the W. family maintained family relations with the brother and brother-in-law, the Hasidic Jew with the eagle's wings, who was the supposed news-bearer for the whole family. Apart from him none of the other brothers, nor the sister, had the address of the sister in America.
Once, when the sister pressed her brother in Siewierz to tell her the truth whether he knew anything of how their sister in America was doing, he explained to her in the mournful tune of "Eicha" that his wife had had a telephone conversation from Będzin to America and learned that "the whole Waksman family had been burned and not a trace of them remained, God preserve us"...
The sister in America, too, who in every letter enclosed a "pidyon"... asked her brother in Siewierz to inform her how the whole family was doing, how the brothers Pinchas Chaim and Mordechai Leib were doing, and especially the youngest sister Złata.
To these inquiries the Siewierz brother again replied that "they are all already in the World of Truth, and he indeed asks her to send money for tombstones — it is surely no honour to the dead not to have a tombstone"...
The letter about the "dead" luckily reached Mr. Waksman in America, who, fearing that if his Siewierz brother-in-law wrote again about the tombstones his wife might find out, at once sent money for the tombstones...
"Heaven and earth have sworn that no secret shall be lost" — and it so happened that a female cousin of the family who lives in London made a pleasure trip to Poland and among other places visited her old home, the town of Siewierz.
When the sister Złata learned of the cousin's visit, she called on her and told her the whole story — that for 20 years now she has had no news whatsoever of her American sister. She knows only[?] of the "telephone news" that her sister-in-law received, that "the whole Waksman family perished in a fire".
The cousin, also cast down by the sad news, promised to make a special trip to the city where the family had lived and find out everything exactly.
No sooner said than done. The cousin arrived in the city where the Waksman family lives, and walking in the street she saw —
— Aunt Chaja Sura walking along!
One can easily imagine the joy and delight when the cousin passed on living greetings from her "dead" brothers and sister... Only then did the whole swindle come to the surface like oil on water; only then did it turn out that the "fine" Jew and gabbai of the Chevra Kadisha had pocketed handsome sums sent for his sister and brother, and when that was too little for him, he demanded money for tombstones...
After 20 years the "dead" brothers and sister received a letter from their sister in America, who is still not sure whether they are alive, and begs with tears that they send her a family photograph, so that she may be sure her brothers and sister are alive.
