We Will Not Let Them Starve!

("Court politics." — The rabbinate and the bakers' [?] interests. — More about the Passover campaign.)
A few weeks ago we discussed in this space the question of carrying out a broad Passover campaign in Zagłębie. We explained then why intensive activity is required in this field, why this year we must be more attentive than ever, and we came to the conclusion that Zagłębie — Jewish Zagłębie — has become terribly impoverished as never before, and therefore one must take care, and take real care — not merely to discharge a duty — of the oppressed, of the fallen, of those who a year or two ago were still counted among the givers.
Unfortunately and to our regret our appeal has remained at a dead point, and hardly anyone has cared [?] about the matter mentioned. Who cares that "respectable" families will go hungry during the Passover days? After all, they starve in silence and the street does not know about it; they raise no clamour, they do not drag themselves like the beggars from door to door and shop to shop, and what people do in silence — who cares, so long as they do not annoy or disgust the public.
Besides, who can have such "trifles" in mind when one is busy with grandiose deeds and has to conduct court politics, from which one cannot free oneself even for a single minute? Was it a trifle, then, to fill the benches in Będzin with our city fathers? Why, all of Zagłębie is preoccupied because the hunger for rabbinic posts stands at its highest level. And what it means nowadays to install a rabbi in a town is well known to everyone. This is, after all, no piece of cheap trinket-work; one has to toil at it day and night, one must scheme in the most ingenious way, and one must pray to Him whom I am not worthy to mention that He help with tripping up [rivals] in ways that would not occur to any of the opponents. Of course, with such busyness, with such intensity, one cannot tear oneself away even for one minute. One cannot leave everything lying and say that the children have been married off in joy and turn to a Passover campaign.
True, here in other towns, as for instance in nearby Częstochowa, the rabbinates together with the kehilla boards occupy themselves with organising Passover campaigns and seders for soldiers and prisoners. With us, on the other hand, the rabbinates have more important matters to settle and have, of course, no time to bother with tiresome questions.
Besides, it is after all just before Passover. One must see to it that Passover can be made out of the "bread of affliction". At such a moment one must stand on guard and protect the kashrut interests, which consist in setting fees and monopolies over what lies within their competence, where no human being may interfere.
So the bakers who want to bake matzot have been ordered that for the oven it costs so-and-so much, and on top of that each must maintain so-and-so many chief supervisors. The bakers cry out in protest: we cannot pay so much, and maintaining the staff will also cost too much, so that we will not be able to compete with the provinces, which bring in matzot at considerably cheaper prices. But the rabbinate in Będzin makes nothing of all this. They are high-handed and keep repeating one argument: what, you cannot? You cannot manage? Who tells you to bake, then? Such is the price [?] and such is the decision, and do as you like and as suits you.
The bakers run about and shout: is it not enough that all year round they are in trouble — are they not to be able to earn anything at Passover either? The rabbinate, for its part, says that there is no poor public: if it costs you more, charge more, and we will ban the outside matzot. The bakers reply that this is a meagre safeguard [?]: you will stay with your ban and we with the matzot.
Such are the dialogues that take place when it comes to getting the poor piece of matzah into the home.
Be that as it may, for this or that reason the carrying out on a broad scale of the Passover campaigns for the oppressed Jewish population of Zagłębie has been postponed — something that must under no circumstances be tolerated.
But one thing must nevertheless be stated: in all the towns of Zagłębie something has indeed begun to be done, only it is in miniature format, insignificant and far too meagre for the great hungry mass.
But we are, after all, always and in everything abnormal [?], and therefore let us precisely now, at the last minute and in an abnormal [?] way, enlarge and multiply the provision of the necessary help for the Jewish population of Zagłębie, which has been left helpless and needs society to bring it, in a respectable manner, the most necessary Passover products.
Let the situation be saved even now, while it is not too late, and let us take pity on those who are fated to go hungry within their four walls at Passover.
The Jewish spark of compassion, with which we have been so crowned, still glows, and Jewish Zagłębie will not let its impoverished brothers and sisters go hungry.
R. Let.
The Commandment of the Hour.

[Zionism — "HeChalutz Ba'al Melakha"; article.] (On the founding of "HeChalutz Ba'al Melakha" in Kielce.)

The Jewish artisan has for "long" years been fed with various promises. And then — in the end he was left "standing" before a terrible abyss. Of all those promises, alas, only smoke has remained; his situation worsens from day to day, the ground is slipping [?] from under his feet. The wave of antisemitism threatens to wash him off the surface. He still clings with all his strength in order to earn a piece of bread, and there is no longer anyone [?] to help him. Unless he stands in line before various public figures with a request for interventions — but unfortunately he has met only with disappointment.

Therefore every true Jewish heart must be deeply grateful to our heroic chalutzim, who with their gigantic efforts, their incomparable heroism, with their blood and sweat, have brought it about that the Jewish artisan should have the possibility to go to Eretz Israel, that the Jewish craftsman may attain the happy [hour] of being redeemed from the exile, be privileged to complete liberation, to a free life and on secure ground.

Eretz Israel at the present moment needs qualified craftsmen, and of these there is surely no lack here in Poland — but unfortunately most of them are unemployed; while in Eretz Israel unqualified people have taken up the work.

The Jewish artisan has at last obtained his own organisation, "HeChalutz Ba'al Melakha". There he has a broad field of work; he can become a mighty force in the world Zionist movement.

"HeChalutz Ba'al Melakha" must take an honourable place in the collections for the Zionist funds, the "Keren Kayemet" and the "Keren Hayesod"; it must sell a significant number of shekels and conduct successful cultural work through Hebrew courses and systematic lectures, which embrace all kinds of fields of Zionist life in particular and of Jewish life in general.

Regrettably there are, unfortunately, still artisans' functionaries who try to stop up the minds of the neglected and unfortunate Jewish craftsman and try to hinder him from going his way of self-liberation.

But the Jewish artisan has found his way and will no longer let himself be misled, for he has a great historic task before him. He has joined the ranks of the builders of Zion, he has thrown himself with all his enthusiasm into the whole complex of Eretz Israel's construction problems, and he is advancing with sure steps toward his goal.

He is certain that the number of certificates for artisan-chalutzim will be steadily increased with every schedule, and the artisan family will form a mighty force both in Eretz Israel and in the Diaspora.

Now, as we stand before the 19th Zionist Congress, the Jewish artisan must say his word. He will distribute tens of thousands of shekels and send a strong representation to the Congress, where he will hopefully play a dominant role, and his representatives will there describe the dreadful, catastrophic situation of their comrades in the Diaspora.

Therefore a duty lies upon the Jewish artisans to join "HeChalutz Ba'al Melakha" en masse, so that they may at last take the great step for their own good and for the good of our people and land.
A Beggar (Monologue)

[Literature — monologue.] By Peretz Hirschbein.
(Monologue)

"What, why are you looking at me like that? You believe? Of course not, what I'm telling you, ha-ha-ha! Of course — a lie, that people believe! If I were to paint you a fair in the sky now — you would surely believe it; but when I take and tear out my heart and lay it before your eyes — you look at me and don't believe.
That is all because a man does not take stock of how he lives in the world. When I go and tell you how I live on Wednesday and die on Thursday, how I am born again on Friday and die a strange [violent] death on the Sabbath — you rub your eyes and don't believe...
Turning one's head with a woman, ha-ha-ha — clever people call it love! Poets have talked the fools into believing that love dwells in heaven and comes down to people only when a young man and a girl turn each other's heads. And what do I say to that, do you want to know? I say that a man in himself is a living creature. If he turns his head with a woman — is he then a dead lion? Why precisely a dead lion? Why not a dead pig? That I really don't know; maybe it's a bit of foolish pride, ha-ha-ha. —
For how did I become what you are looking at now, I mean a beggar? Why do you look at me — don't you take me for a beggar? A beggar is a beggar! It makes no difference what he begs for, the devil take it... Of course I beg now, let me be heard out[?] — otherwise I would have croaked, to all the black years!
You understand, I said that whatever one begs for — it's all the same. Here I have already overstepped the measure a little, because it depends how and who throws something into the beggar's hand; such a face the beggar himself has. I have already done everything and tried everything to be a decent beggar; at first I thought: I'll go about ragged, overgrown and neglected — then, when I stretch out my hand, they will notice me at once and have pity. And that is indeed true — they did give more willingly. But the look[?] laid [me] into the ground.. The giver looked at me with a twisted face — you might as well go die a strange death! I had a habit of holding out a greasy and torn sky, ha-ha-ha. —
You see, I have already talked you into a fair in the sky.
You want to know how a man takes and becomes a beggar when nobody forces him? Then you're a fool if that's what you think! I made up my mind that I would not marry; I made up my mind — there, you understand me, lies the trouble.. I had a craving to be cleverer than the whole world — that's where the trouble is stuck. 'I give to you — you pay me'... that's what I said to her. What, you want to know to whom I said it? Why, for all the black years, should you buy yourself a husband, that is to say, for a whole life — when you can cuddle with him to your heart's content and let him go? What, is that crazy? Love is cleverer, you think? Woe and alas to what is already stuck in love itself!
I ask you, how much must a fool pay with his head before he understands that he is a fool? How many times did I have to fall in before I understood that there is no love left in the world? Ten times? I had enough with once! Once I loved and got my legs chopped off.. I was born, grew grey and old — oh, my friend, now I look like a beggar, since I even begged from her..
What comes of it? I laugh with lizards [i.e., a bitter laugh], I myself make fun of myself, I myself shout that there is no love in the world — and I myself was burnt up by love! Burnt to coal...
Oh, my friend, I don't want to cause you any pain... Don't look at the tears that I... it's from weakness. I know it isn't fitting for a man to cry; I know I am a sinner when I go and talk like this, saying that a man needs not just one love — but hundreds, thousands!.. I only want to shout myself down, to talk myself into believing that I am already dead, ha-ha-ha!
But does a dead man suffer like this? Is there then a hell on earth? No, on earth there is love, and it itself is paradise and hell! And precisely because I had only one love, one and no more, and precisely because that one love did not want to know me — therefore. I was left lying with chopped-off legs..
Now, my friend, I come to the main point: a beggar I did indeed become. A man needs to eat sometimes too; earn — I didn't earn, I knocked about outdoors, had nothing to hire a bed with, so that I'd have somewhere to lay down my sick head, ha-ha-ha...! Ragged, shabby[?], overgrown and unwashed; by a street corner [róg] I took my stand, turned up my collar, covered my forehead with my hair; a fine snow kept pouring and pouring... Well, who do you think threw the first grosz into my hat? She, love, ha-ha-ha...
Well, what happened? What should happen? I croaked, that's what! Paid with my head; died, out of the market, and an end of that man!...
For when a man's hands and feet go limp, when a man's heart stops and a choking creeps right into his throat — because she, love, recognised me..
Oh, my friend, when one dies such a strange death, does one ever come back to life? Dead — is dead!... Only, when a man dies — they bury him and he is out of the market. But a beggar, when a man remains in the world, oh, my friend, it is a thousand times worse for him than for a dead man..."
Thousands of Jews Fled to Paris — and Now They Are Being Driven Out of There

[France — expulsion of Jewish immigrants; article from Paris.] There is a Polish-Jewish saying that a Litvak [Lithuanian Jew] never dies. Either he steals, and then he dies a "Sibirnik" (they send him to Siberia), or he converts, and then he dies an apostate. And if he neither steals nor converts, he simply goes off to Jerusalem, and then he dies a "Yerushalmi" (a Jerusalem Jew).
The same saying can now be applied to the thousands of immigrant Jews who are now being driven out of France. It is clear that they are not driven out as Jews: if they are Polish citizens, they are driven out as Poles; Romanian ones — as Romanians; German ones — as Germans; and Russian immigrants — as Russians. And if they have the "luck" of being without any passport at all, then they are sent out simply as stateless foreigners.
"If that were really so," a Polish Jew told me, "it really wouldn't bother me. The misfortune is that in the country to which they send me back, I am received as a Jew. Here, in France, I am a Pole; but there, in my old home, I immediately become a Jew again." And here lies precisely the tragedy of thousands of foreign Jews who, after a few years of rest, must once again take up the wanderer's staff and march on through the world.
But these people are not yet the most unfortunate; after all, they have a passport and can hope that at the first opportunity they will leave again for somewhere. Worse off are those who have no passport.
One fine morning such a person is summoned to the police and given a blue slip, which means that he is being told to leave the country amicably. If he does not comply, he is summoned again and given a white slip, which means: if you do not leave, you will be brought to the border by force.
A few years ago it used to end with a trip there and back. A French police agent would take such a person and escort him to the Belgian border. There the police agent would help him slip across the border illegally, give him the necessary advice and tricks for fooling the Belgian official, and the expellee would indeed, with the help of the French detective, get across the border safely. A few days later he would already be travelling back to Paris escorted by a Belgian detective, who knew exactly all the tricks for slipping across the French border, and under his supervision the emigrant would arrive in Paris. I knew Jews who made such trips there and back 27 times, at the expense of both states, the French and the Belgian. Today it is different: today, if you come back, you are put in prison, and you sit there until you are sick of it, and then you switch to a Belgian jail. In France a bill is now pending that will punish such expelled stateless persons who come back with deportation to New Guinea [sic], somewhere not far from "Devil's Island", where Captain Dreyfus was deported.
You can imagine the situation of such a German, Russian, Polish or Romanian Jew without a passport, running around Paris like a wounded animal with the white slip in his pocket.
You will ask: why are these people sent out? Don't ask. A secret denunciation by a neighbour is enough; it is enough that he is caught working without the right to do so; it is enough that a taxi runs him over — and he is already a foreigner obstructing traffic in the street; it is enough that misfortune leads him by chance to a place where a political demonstration is taking place; it is enough that he is a few francs short for the rent. In a word, there is no lack of reasons, and it is enough that, when looking over the list of foreigners, the police official concerned feels a stab in his side at your name, or is reminded of his mother-in-law.
Begging does not help, and protesting does not either, because nowadays the whole of society is against you.
If restrictions are introduced against naturalised foreigners, if naturalised persons are deprived of the right to obtain a government post for ten consecutive years, if there is a move to forbid naturalised foreign lawyers to appear in court and doctors to practise, what can a stranger say — and one without a passport at that?
The misfortune is all the greater because most immigrant Jews have not grasped the quite peculiar trait of French bureaucracy.
In France there is no law that is always carried out immediately. There are hundreds of thousands of laws and ordinances there, some dating from before the Great Revolution, which sleep peacefully in the old law books in the archive. Often the ministers themselves do not know of their existence. But when they need them, they take them out of hiding and suddenly enforce them with full severity.
Thousands of Jews sat in Paris for ten and fifteen years, as carefree as at their father's in the vineyard, and kept praising French freedom:
"Ah, what a precious country! Do what you like, you don't have to register or deregister, nobody bothers you. They let you live."
And the Jews did not get naturalised, although there were times when it was very easy to become a French citizen. They had children, raised them in French schools, bought houses, did business, and did not know that somewhere in a ministry a slaughterer's knife was lying ready for them that could slaughter them within 24 hours. Now the great outcry has broken out: suddenly they are being deprived of the right to work. Now there is a move to take away from them the right to trade and even the right to work at home.
On top of this comes the misfortune of the Jews' lack of organisation. The Polish Jews keep to themselves, the Russian Jews — to themselves, the German Jews have shunned the hated "Ost-Juden" [Eastern European Jews], and now there is not even any central organisation at all to defend the unfortunates. As soon as the disaster broke out, dozens of deputations and intercessors from all sorts of societies set off to the most prominent personalities of French society. But these, with the best will in the world, claim that they do not know who really represents the Jewish emigration. A prominent French scholar complained not long ago to an acquaintance of mine that he was already sick of the storm of deputations: they come knocking at his doors, each one comes with a different version, and he does not know which of them is really entitled to speak in the name of the Jewish emigration as a whole. The French Jews keep their distance; they thank God that for the time being the Jews are being sent out under foreign names — Poles, Russians — and not under the general name "Jew", because then they too would not be sure of their own position.
And finally they are told:
"Who is expelling Jews? We also expel genuine Poles; we do not ask foreigners about their nationality at all. Better keep quiet and do not raise the Jewish question; the time is not a favourable one; here and there people are already starting to talk about Jews in general. For the time being it is the monarchists together with the real fascists who are doing it — who knows what tomorrow may bring!"
And the danger is great.
Whoever has seen the recent demonstrations of the students against their foreign colleagues can expect anything. These demonstrations ran counter to every notion of common sense — the very common sense on which the French have so prided themselves as a national trait.
Just imagine: over a few years France has taken in more than 40 billion from foreign travellers; in France thousands of students from every corner of the world study, leaving millions in France and carrying French culture and language home with them. Only rarely does one of the foreign students stay in France. And should anyone wish to, in recent years such laws have been in force as make it simply impossible for a foreigner who has graduated as a doctor in France to obtain the right to practise here. And yet the students staged stormy demonstrations and even beat up several of their foreign colleagues. And this at a time when the whole press is complaining that the tourists have stopped coming and that there is a real danger of economic ruin for a whole series of business enterprises.
To go cursing and beating foreign students at such a time is sheer madness, and yet they did it. What, then, can one expect from such people with regard to Jews, once the fascists sense that Jew-hatred is a good means of inciting the masses? Then they will do it with all their energy — and such a movement already exists and is secretly supported by Hitler. It is no accident that precisely in recent weeks Streicher's "Stürmer" has appeared at the newspaper kiosks of the student quarter in the most prominent place, and I myself have seen how many students buy it. In a word, the storm is approaching, and people are getting ready to meet it and to defend themselves against it.
"France was the last hope," a Jew who was forced to go back to Poland told me on the train. "Now nothing is left for me but to go begging from door to door in Poland."
Tragedies upon tragedies.
When a Nation Buys Itself Free of Its Sins (On the Maimonides Celebrations in Spain)

[Feuilleton — Jewry and the Maimonides jubilee; Spain.] The Jewish people has taken hold of Maimonides.
Wherever one goes and wherever one stands — Rambam. In Spain, in Warsaw, in Tel Aviv and in New York there is Rambam-ing for all one is worth.
In his whole life and in all the centuries since his death, Maimonides never received as much fame as now.
What more do you need? Even my neighbour, who deals in herring and has a son who is a doctor, even he has caught the Rambam bug, and it gives him, poor man, no rest.
The other day he dropped in on me at home looking embarrassed and asked me:
— Tell me, please, who is this Rambam? I keep reading whole stories about him in the newspaper and I can't make out who, when and what. I even asked my son the doctor. He is even a learned young man — I mean my son the doctor — but when it comes to the fine print, it's a day of woe. And one can't hold it against him either, because it's perhaps fifteen years already since he became bar mitzvah — what am I saying, fifteen? Almost sixteen already. Yes, in May it will be [?] sixteen years since he put on tefillin, and in 16 years one can forget a lot of things. Yesterday I again saw in the newspaper that they are writing about the Rambam. So I ask my son the doctor once more: „Sewek, who was the Rambam?“ And he answers me, just like that, off into the air, that he knows who Max Baer is, but who this Rambam is, that he doesn't know.
In short, we had to explain to our neighbour everything the Rambam did for the Jewish faith. Then we told him about Maimonides the philosopher and the physician. My neighbour kept shaking his head the whole time and blinking his eyes, and it seemed to us that we were tormenting a poor Jew for nothing and in vain. When we had finished, he speaks up:
— So it means the Rambam was a sportsman... Then my son the doctor was right after all, he said so straight away...
* * *
Last week the great festival was celebrated in Spain. After five hundred years the land of the Inquisition officially celebrated a Jewish festival, and in Córdoba, where Maimonides was born, Hebrew and Yiddish speeches were heard from a public platform.
How quickly the world changes nowadays.
Only five years ago the writer of these lines was in Córdoba and wandered through the quiet streets of the town on a rainy Sunday at dawn, looking for a Jew. Not even for a cure could I find a single Jew there, and I was very [?] sad.
But suddenly a miracle happened: the hired guide, whom we had asked to take us among Jews, after a few minutes' thought confessed to us that he was a Jew, and what's more, the only Jew in town. There are no more! [?] His name was Kahn, but in Córdoba it occurred to nobody that Kahn is a Jewish name, and he was, of course, taken for a good gentile.
And when we heard that our guide was a Jew, our eyes lit up and we wanted right there on the spot to find out where he came from, but so much joy was not destined for us.
Señor Kahn at once drove us in the droshky to Maimonides Street (which still existed then; now the name of the street has been changed), and when we saw with our own eyes the sign with the inscription „Maimonides“, our eyes lit up once more and we pointed out to our guide that he had told a lie: he is not the o-n-l-y Jew in Córdoba — here is another Jew — Maimonides...
The town of Córdoba suddenly became more beautiful in our eyes. Such a living monument of the Jewishness of old in Spain as this little sign with the name „Maimonides“ we did not find in any other city. The synagogues that still stand in Spain from those times when Jews lived there are cold, dead walls that nobody looks at. The chance Jewish tourist casts a glance at them and moves on; the Spaniard does not even know what the synagogues signify. He only knows that the building is a national museum which the government wants to preserve, believing that the Spanish people wants to live with the past and boast before the world of an ancient culture — no new culture is being created here.
And that is why we say that the Maimonides lane, narrow and muddy, was nevertheless the most living symbol of the Jewishness of old in the land of the Inquisition. People used to address letters to the residents of Maimonides Street. The word Maimonides was written and pronounced by Spaniards hundreds of thousands of times.
Now, on the 800th birthday of the great Jewish spirit, Spain has at least a little bought itself free of its great sins, which it committed against the Jewish people; and not only my neighbour's son, the doctor, but the whole Spanish people has recognised that Maimonides was the greatest scholar Spain has produced.
Z. H. Rubinsztajn.
We Will Not Let Ourselves Be Turned into Pariahs!

In Jewish economic circles the question of intensifying the boycott action against German goods has lately been raised again. The all-Polish conference of the provincial „Committees to Fight the Persecution of Jews in Germany“, which took place in Warsaw on the 10th of March of this year, clearly showed the moods that now prevail among the Jewish population of Poland. The majority of the delegates sincerely gave expression to the serious feeling of responsibility for the great historic tasks that face Polish Jewry, as the most numerous Jewish community in Europe.
The whole world is watching the great struggle that Jewry in all parts of the world is waging against Nazi barbarism. The consistent carrying-out of the boycott must show the world to what extent we are capable of defending our rights and our dignity; the world must find out whether we are fit to put up resistance to the enemy, or let ourselves be trampled by anyone. A struggle is going on of humanitarianism and culture against dark medieval acts of violence, which are applied to loyal and defenceless citizens.
To all this has lately been added the „famous“ Kwellen[?]-law, which places the Jews in Germany literally outside the framework of the generally binding law, turning them into pariahs.
It is clear to everyone that the boycott is the only effective weapon! Jewry must defend itself economically against those who want to exterminate us. Important world economists admit that the boycott has contributed much to shrinking the German economy. German financiers too have openly[?] declared the same.
Even on the basis of the official publications of the German government one can see that German exports are constantly diminishing.
In the territory of the United States, where the boycott is conducted energetically and consistently, the exchange of goods between America and Germany has reached the following state:
In the year 1933 the import of German goods amounted to RM 245.852,000, whereas the export to Germany — RM 482.772,000, — balance RM 236,920,000.
The import of German goods in the first half of 1934 amounts to RM 84.788.000. The export to Germany in the first half of 1934 amounts to RM 244,940,000 — negative balance 160,152,000.
During the time of the boycott the export of English goods has risen considerably.
The report on German foreign trade shows a negative balance (45.5) during January. There is no doubt whatsoever that the main cause of the constant[?] shrinking of German exports is the anti-Hitlerite economic action, which is being conducted throughout the world against the Nazi regime. This fact forces the German press to reflect seriously on the situation that has arisen. Some German newspapers claim that because of the boycott Germany has had to limit imports to the very most necessary extent.
It must be said that the important role in the boycott movement is played by American Jewry, which shows much courage, devotion and self-sacrifice. There the boycott is carried out with the strictest exactitude. This even induced the Berlin Nazi leader Julius Lippert to appeal „to the American people“ to stop the boycott of German goods. The answer came from the American Anti-Nazi League, to which Jews and Christians belong, as well as from the American Jewish Congress. The answer points out the whole hypocrisy and shamelessness of the said „appeal“. Among other things the answer says: „The boycott against Nazi Germany is not an economic one. It is a revolt of freedom-loving humanity against those who have enslaved the German people. We will not let our anger be sold for money, not today and not at any time; today it is in Germany, tomorrow it may be another country with a similar regime“.
This is a proud answer of noble people, who react with dignity[?] to the persecutions that the defenceless population in Germany constantly has to endure.
Polish Jewry too has not lagged behind in this respect. Here too a planned boycott action is being conducted, whose aim is to eliminate German imports into Poland. The balance of the 2-year boycott movement has brought no bad results at all. The necessity of boycotting German goods is already deeply rooted in the popular consciousness. But we must conduct the boycott action with more courage and perseverance; all forces must be activated against the Nazi savageries, because only the economic boycott will sober the Nazi people up from their racist madness.
If there is anywhere a conscienceless Jewish merchant or consumer who allows himself to break the boycott of German products[?], he must absolutely be regarded as a traitor, as one who shamelessly mocks the most vital (literally: „bloodiest“) Jewish interests. Jewish society must turn away from such a person with contempt, and as a wrongdoer he must be placed[?] entirely outside the camp.
Let the world be convinced that Jewish honour and Jewish blood are not fair game, that we still have enough self-respect to defend our human existence. We will not let ourselves be turned into pariahs!

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Metzora)

[Oneg Shabbat — weekly Torah portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Metzora
The portion.
—o—
a) "He shall be brought unto the priest" (14:2)
Plagues (nega'im) come because of the sin of evil speech (lashon hara) (Chullin 140 [?]).
So the leper was shown that only the priest can purify him, by his word. With plagues everything depends on the priest's word. The leper does not become pure until the priest says "pure", and he does not become impure until the priest says "impure". This shows the leper what weight and value a person's word has, for the slanderer thinks to himself: oh, I just babbled something there.. In fact a person's word has a whole stature: it purifies and it defiles.
The Maggid of Dubno.
—o—
b) "Then shall the priest command to take for him that is to be cleansed two birds" (ibid., 4)
"Because plagues come for evil speech, which is idle chatter, therefore his purification requires birds, which chatter constantly with a twittering voice." Rashi.
But why must he take two birds? Why not two pieces of [?]?
Because the Jerusalem Talmud says in Berakhot chapter 1: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says: had I been at Mount Sinai at the giving of the Torah, I would have asked that man be created with two mouths, one to speak words of Torah and one for idle talk.
And therefore the leper brings two birds for his two kinds of evil speech: his evil speech in words of Torah and his evil speech in idle talk... Imrei Chen.
• • •
A Masorah [a scriptural word-pattern]:
"At the mouth of two (witnesses)"
"According to the Torah."
"According to the words"
"By their mouth shall every controversy and every plague be."
"At the mouth of two" — a person ought to have had two mouths, one "according to the Torah" — to speak Torah with it, and one "according to the words" — to speak idle talk with it.
But if a person sins so much with one mouth — how much more would he have sinned had he had two mouths?... "By their mouth" — had he two mouths, there would be "every controversy and every plague"... Bechirat Avraham.
• • •
When we stand to pray the Shmoneh Esreh we say: "O Lord, open Thou my lips" — God, open my mouth. For all the follies and gossip we do not need God to open our mouths — we open them ourselves... Only when it comes to prayer do we become helpless and ask God to open our mouths...
Ya'arot Devash.
• • •
That is why the leper brings birds, for he says to himself: what have I done, after all? I said a few words in front of a handful of people — is that already gossip? So he is shown birds: "a bird of the air shall carry the voice". The birds are already spreading the evil speech that was uttered in the innermost chambers... Leket Amarim.
—o—
c) "And I put the plague of leprosy in a house of the land of your possession" (ibid., 34)
"It is good tidings for them that the plagues come upon them, etc." Rashi.
So what are the good tidings in plagues coming upon the houses?
Because it proves that we are so bound to the Land of Israel and the Land of Israel to us, that our sins call forth plagues upon the houses... Kol Yaakov.
• • •
Once Jewish houses were stricken with plague so that the treasures of the Amorites might be found through it: "Because the Amorites hid treasures of gold in the walls of their houses during all forty years that Israel was in the wilderness, and through the plague he demolishes the house and finds them." Today Jewish houses become stricken, struck with plagues, because they have found Amorite treasures — because they have grown rich, obtained a gentile post, a little gentile culture... Kinyanei Kedem.
————
That is why a leper is brought to the priest: for a leper, a slanderer, sows discord between people — so he is brought to the priest, who is a lover of peace and a pursuer of peace. Korban He'ani.
• • •
"Whoever speaks evil speech transgresses the five books of the Torah"
Why is it not simply said: "Whoever speaks evil speech transgresses the whole Torah", but rather explicitly: "transgresses the five books of the Torah"?
Because every one of the five books speaks of evil speech.
In Genesis — the story of the serpent and Eve.
In Exodus — about Dathan and Abiram.
In Leviticus — it says: "Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people."
In Numbers — the story of Miriam is told, who spoke evil of Moses and became leprous.
In Deuteronomy — it says: "Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour in secret" (this is interpreted as evil speech, that is, striking one's fellow behind his back).
Therefore the wording is precise: "Whoever speaks evil speech transgresses the five books of the Torah", since in every book the sin of evil speech is stated explicitly. Minchat Belulah.
In Thy Blood Live...

By Avraham Ale.
(Reflections).
... In Israel — a people on whose tablets the abhorrence of blood is engraved, whose entire [?] Sinaitic legislation is a living condemnation of bloodshed, and whose destiny was a struggle of ideas, a spiritual battle between heaven and earth, a battle of angels — yet whose fate willed precisely that blood should be the banner of its national drama and the leitmotif of its epic.
... Once a struggle lasted until the break of dawn, in which our grandfather [Jacob] very nearly lost the sciatic sinew, and wrestling out an "Israel" our historical road has remained thirsty for our sinful [?] blood ever after... and for "men" — for further wrestlings...
* * *
It is characteristic: the first sign of redemption, the first means of punishment with which they sought to frighten the Egyptian king, was: blood!...
And as the first time, so at the most decisive time blood once again became the symbol for the Jew.
To smear with blood — the doorposts were commanded as signs, so that the destroyer should have no power over them [?].
And once again the Jewish fate was sealed with blood — Jew, your sign is blood!...
* * *
... "And when I passed by thee, and saw thee polluted in thine own blood, I said unto thee: In thy blood live"... In "bedamayikh" — sometimes "dmama" [silence] and sometimes "dam" [blood].
Therefore the Jewish fate swings on the scales.
Jewish victims fall in stoic silence — like ripe golden ears of grain in the field, and the "holy little tailors" of Tah ve-Tat [1648–49] die of fright in mute coldness in the [—] [?] — their heads for the gleaming Haidamak scythes of Chmielnicki and the stomachs of Shylocks:
"Flesh with blood!"
And they suffocate in the underground caves and casemates before the [terror] [?] of Torquemada's Inquisition, Marranos, and direct silent prayers to go with heads held high to the auto-da-fé, taking up the struggle passively [?] with Shema Yisrael — and the scale tips to "dmama".
And again, when the people goes in blood under the [—] [?] sword of sadistic Petliura men, an individual [?] rises and with a pistol in hand ends "[—]" [?] the struggle — the scale strikes "dam".
Either way it remains: in thy blood live.. in thy blood live...
* * *
Times pass, history strides with giant steps, and like straw [—] [?] on the [—] [?] of nations, and the Jewish diaspora [?] has acclimatised itself quickly enough to strike roots — again a secret [—] [?] rises on the Jewish horizon! Blood!
Philip Krantz tells us that in the 14th–16th centuries cannibalism was still practised [?] in the heart of Europe (Paris)... but the Jews cannot be left clean without any blemish — a plague is revealed in the shape of the blood libel, a Damascus ritual trial surfaces in the year 1840, a Tiszaeszlár trial is staged in 1882, and then a Vilna affair and then a Beilis drama.
— In thy blood live... the Jewish fate is sealed with blood!...
* * *
The Jewish people bathes in its own blood (Kishinev 1903, Hebron 1923 [sic; = 1929]) — the greatest curse for a people! But... in thy blood live...
Therefore the Jewish fate swings on the scales — sometimes with "dmama", sometimes with "dam" — through blood libels and pogroms, through acts of forced conversion and expulsions, and remarkably: precisely the people whose Ten Commandments call for abhorrence of blood strides along the hard road of exile accompanied by blood, Jewish blood that boils with oriental heat.
From every historical night of Egypt Jewish blood threads its way (the cheapest for [—] [?] nations [—] [?]...) like a red thread through our heroic Jewish history, and casts a light: Jew, your sign is: blood!
— In thy blood live.. in thy blood live...

A gripping tragic novel of a prodigy (ilui). (30
But more than anyone, Chanele suffered. From the day Moshele was driven out of the yeshiva, her eyes had not stopped shedding tears. Everything in her wept because of the shame that had been brought upon her Moshele. On the contrary, he shouted in anger that he would put Moshele under a cherem [ban].
It was pitiful to look at Chanele, who went about as if without a head and did not know what to do — whether to run and beg that they not persecute her only, unfortunate son.
And once, on Friday at candle-lighting, when Chanele was saying the Sabbath techine and weeping bitterly, Moshele came up to her and asked her why she was crying.
"How should I not cry, my child!" Chanele answers him. "How should I not cry, when we have already been punished!"
"It isn't true, Mameniu, we have not been punished, and if there really[?] are people who persecute me, it is not their fault. They are rather to be pitied, because they are blind. Don't cry, Mameniu, do it for my sake; don't forget that it is already Sabbath and one must not be sad."
"But Moshele, what shall we do now? It is a disgrace and a shame. People point their fingers at us. If you were a good child and had pity on your mother, you would..."
"Mother!" Moshele groaned. "You too talk like that? Have you forgotten the words you said to me as we came out of the Warsaw beth din? Did you not say then that we would go and prove to the world that we are innocent? Did you not say that we would go and seek the truth? Mother! How can I live and not think of what you yourself showed me! It was you who told me to seek the truth, and I am doing it. With all my body and soul I will fight until I prove my point. I must prove the truth, and if not — then I do not want to live in the world."
The door opens and in comes R' Shloyme, the shammes of the yeshiva.
"Gut Shabbes," he says, and goes up to Chanele.
"You need something else from the shop?" Chanele asks him.
"No, I came to tell you that R' Leibl summons you to him tomorrow, right after Havdalah, about an important matter."
"Me?" asks Chanele.
"Yes, you, and for God's sake don't forget to come right after Havdalah, so that I shouldn't have to come for you a second time," he instructed, and left the house.
All Friday night and the whole Sabbath Chanele kept thinking about R' Leibl summoning her. Her heart told her it was for no good. And perhaps — a thought ran through her — he is calling her about Moshele? After all, she had begged him so much, pleaded for him so much and wept; it could be that his anger had subsided and he would take Moshele back into the yeshiva. She could no longer wait for the minute when the first stars would appear in the sky, when the candles would be lit for Maariv in the beth midrash. She was impatient the whole day and could not find a place for herself, and as soon as people began going to Maariv, Chanele was already over at R' Leibl's, waiting in the kitchen until he would come back from the beth midrash.
For a long time she sat and waited, and at last she heard R' Leibl coming in.
"I am here, holy Rebbe," she says, and shuffles out of the kitchen into the room.
"I called you, Chane," he says, "and I want to give you to understand that your Moshele has entirely left the straight path. Whole days and nights he lies in the woods with the teacher, who has brought things[?] so far that he is no longer to be endured; and not enough that he himself crawls along evil ways, he drags other young men along with him. Therefore I called you and want to warn you that you, as his mother, should keep him away from these follies; you should see to it that you influence him to throw away his foolish philosophies. If he does not obey you and does not stop his tricks, then you should[?] know that I will stop at nothing and will carry out the sentence upon him."
Chanele stood trembling the whole time. With every stamp of his foot she felt as if a piece of her heart were being torn out inside her. With her head sunk to the ground she stood and heard it all out; she was very much afraid of R' Leibl, and so, seeing him now so agitated, she began to fear him even more — that he might, God forbid, still do something to her Moshele.
"Rebbe," Chanele groans out, "have pity on me and on my child and take him back into the yeshiva. You will see, Rebbe, that he will obey you and throw away the follies; he is still so young."
"True, if only he had obeyed, he would have become a great man in Israel; he has, no evil eye, a good head, but what can one do when he has begun to walk on evil ways."
"Rebbe!" Chanele let out a cry. "Have pity on me, I am after all a wretched [literally 'dark'] widow."
Into the room runs Moshele, who had been standing in the kitchen.
"Mameniu," he runs up to Chanele, "come home, don't be afraid."
"Show respect, you troubler of Israel!" shouts R' Leibl. "If you don't throw away your tricks, you will suffer a black defeat; I will put you under the cherem!" — and he strikes the table with his fist, which knocks over the candlestick with the candle, and the room goes dark.
A woman's scream is heard, and the heavy thud of a body falling to the floor.

Humour and satire. Compiled by Amotzlo.
Shabbat HaGadol.

[“Der Kokh-Lefl” — satirical poem; Passover, Passover-flour relief, the kehillas, the economic crisis.]
How big the chametz once used to be,
they burned it, after all, in flames,
and today — a delight... it's clean... it's bright[?]...
there's nothing at all to clear away...
They've koshered us, they've scoured us,
they've driven the chametz out of us...
thanks to the komornik [bailiff] and the sekwestrator [tax distrainer]
hardly an olive's worth is left...
How well off are the little Jews of Zagłębie,
now they may dance for joy!
No one needs to think or ponder about Passover,
everyone will receive his kimcha [Passover flour relief]..
The kehillas have assigned four złoty apiece,
with that one can do great things...
if not for potatoes, matzah and eggs,
it is surely enough for charoset...
And if there's still among us an “earner”[?],
say [with] a horse to Upper Silesia,-
he'll be able to get there
a dry little bone of maror...
Graf Kali.
Chatskele Kolboynik's Sermon for Shabbat HaGadol

[Humour and satire — "Der Kokh-Lefl".] (The whole speech is printed in a deliberately mangled, phonetically spelt popular dialect; the translation gives the sense, and words whose reading or meaning is uncertain are marked [?].)
Fellow Jews! How do I look after the flu, when one has had something [?] done to me... Nothing?
Oh, listen, Jews: when I had the flu — I had a swollen throat and a "skipke" [fever?] like fire — all the aristocrats, money they don't send to Zhimne [?], but if one of them happens to fall ill, they send him down to Zhimne [?] alley.
You think I'm already completely well? May I fall ill! I got out of bed, because I had to take part [?] in the Passover campaign; straight from bed I ran to the kehilla, one day [?], to the office [?] of the president, about the Passover campaign for our impoverished Jews.
I went straight down to the president, Reb Lozer [R. Elazar Rubinlicht, president of the Będzin kehilla], and said as follows:
— Reb Lozer, what will my impoverished Jews do [?]?
The president stroked his beard and asked me:
— What is your name?
— Chatskele, Chatskele Kolboynik ["kolboynik" — one who meddles in everything] is my name; in Zhimne [?] that's what they call me. I am the representative of all the Zhimne [?] Jews and of the "Bikikhine" [?] too. I have come to register them for the Passover campaign.
The president heard me out and at the end said:
— It must be a gabbe (meaning a gabbai) or a president of an association who comes.
So I got angry [?] and said as follows:
— Reb Lozer, stop banging the kettle [= talking nonsense]! I understand all these matters; I am neither a gabbai nor the president of an association; I have come to register the Podzamcze Jews in Batsha [?].
You think Reb Lozer got scared? Do you know [?] what the rebbe [?] did? He pressed a button, in came a sturdy young fellow and gave me a "trimaske" [shove?] down the stairs — a "mitime" [?] should come to the kehilla together with the aristocrats.
A curse on the kehilla — may it get [?] ... [?]. One really has to make one's own Passover campaign. I am already getting down to work [literally: "to the tools"].
Meanwhile, I also wish you a good Shabbes Hagodl, and be well.
Politics of the Week

[Humour and satire — "Der Kokh-Lefl".] It is already almost the eve of Passover, and still no war is to be heard of.
Oh, a little war, a little war — how badly we diplomats need a little war.
A whole winter we diplomats did everything that is at all needed to bring about a war, and — nothing; it turns out that we are no good at the job of kindling a war.
Our diplomatic "lack of sense" [pun on "common sense"] tells us that there simply cannot be a better opportunity for a war than now, so what does one do, after all, for a scuffle to break out — a little war?
Simple people, perhaps you know what to do?..
—o—
A conversation between Shabbat HaGadol and Short Friday.
Short Friday: Panie [Mr.] Shabbat HaGadol, do you at least know that tomorrow is Shabbat HaGadol?
Shabbat HaGadol: Yes, I know. It's my Shabbat.
Short Friday: To whom are you marrying off your daughter?
Shabbat HaGadol: To a glazier.
Short Friday: Is that a good trade?
Shabbat HaGadol: As long as there are Endeks [members of the antisemitic National Democracy, notorious for smashing Jewish windows] here, glazing is a golden trade.
Short Friday: Don't you know of some good business?
Shabbat HaGadol: There is a nice little business; you don't need much money, only one drawback — it is a bit too far away.
Short Friday: Never mind, where is it?
Shabbat HaGadol: The Chinese Eastern Railway. The Bolsheviks will hand it over to you for half for nothing.
A Stormy Meeting of the Kehilla Council

[Będzin — kehilla.] On Monday evening a meeting of the kehilla council took place. Even though the agenda contained so innocent an item as approving the report on the kehilla's activity in the past year, the meeting nevertheless had a stormy character; there were such „heated“ moments that it seemed inkwells were about to fly...
The meeting is chaired by the vice-president Mr. G. Landner, who in his criticism (printed „criterium“) points out to the kehilla administration that 90 per cent of the budget is spent on the religious functionaries and kehilla officials and barely 10 per cent on public purposes.
The Agudah councillors Schönberg, Rygski and Efraim Klejman submit a declaration that the meeting held on the 6th[?] of February is not valid, because there was no quorum.
The chairman Mr. Landner states that 9 councillors took part in that meeting, and since the council consists of only 17 members, the meeting is valid.
Councillor Herszlewicz criticises the administration because the family of the late rabbi was paid the entire debt, a sum of nearly 7.000 zł. If the kehilla can pay such a sum at once, then all kehilla employees should enjoy the same privilege and have their claims on the kehilla paid out.
The president Mr. Rubinlicht explains that the rabbi's debt, which was paid with long-term promissory notes, cannot be regarded as a privilege; rather, the kehilla fulfilled a moral obligation towards the rabbi's family, which is deep in debt.
Mr. Landner takes the floor on the question, not satisfied with Mr. Rubinlicht's answer. In this case — says Mr. L. — the rabbi's family was favoured. Mr. L. also criticises the kehilla's act of revenge against Mr. Berysz Fuks, who was assessed a kehilla tax (etat) of 50 zł (in previous years only 5 zł). These methods — cries Mr. Landner — lead us back to the Middle Ages; it is already reaching the point where a „donkey's burial“ will be introduced in the kehilla...
Interjection by board member (dozór) Hampel: the revenge was carried out on your colleague's proposal, because Fuks helped the former[?] cantor Żupowicz to place attachments (liens) on the budget.
On this question speak: Rubinlicht, Herszlewicz and Manela. The last condemns the act of revenge. „I dissociate myself — cries Mr. M. — from those[?] who lent a hand to the revenge.“ Finally Mr. M. appeals that the energy used in the kehilla's behind-the-scenes politics should rather be applied to the Kimcha [de-Pischa] campaign.
After the council accepts the activity report, the meeting is closed.
—o—
[Będzin — Municipal Board; notice.]
The Municipal Board of Będzin
hereby announces that as of 1 April 1935 the office of the Water-Supply and Sewerage Works of the City of Będzin has been moved from the premises at 3 Małachowskiego St. to 2 Sączewska St., 2nd floor.
The Boycott Campaign against the Talmud Torah

[Będzin — Talmud Torah.] Everyone knows that year in, year out, shmura flour is sold at the Talmud Torah, thanks to which the melamdim (teachers), who go hungry all year, receive at least a few gulden for Passover.
This year, however, a boycott campaign is being waged against this flour. The reason is supposed to be that the notices about the shmura flour are signed only by „the Rabbinate here“ (ha-rabanut de-po), and the word „Rav“ is not mentioned...
The boycott was proclaimed by the „sharp“ (zealous) young Gerer Hasidim known by the name „the 9-ers“. These „9-ers“ (no doubt also „out of respect for the Torah“...) have broken a 40-year-old tradition and brought in flour from outside[?], in order to harm the Talmud Torah.
The only wonder is that the Rabbinate, which forbids outside shmura and machine matzot, remains indifferent when a campaign is being waged whose aim is to undermine the existence of an institution where 400 poor children are brought up?
— Why are you silent?
Protest of the National Board Members against the Kehilla President

[Będzin — kehilla.] As is known, a meeting of the kehilla board took place last Wednesday. At the meeting it was decided by 5 votes to 4 to engage the shochet Rybka of Maków. Because the kehilla president decided the matter with his vote, the board members (dozory) Manela, Niemark, Tenenberg and Hampel submitted a written protest against the kehilla president.
The protest states that the president, Mr. Rubinlicht, by this vote harmed the interests of the local Jewish population.
The next day Mr. Tenenberg sent a letter in which he declares that he withdraws his signature from the protest.
Lodging in the Poorhouse, Meals in People's Homes and... 8000 zł in the P.K.O.

[Będzin — local life.] The other day, when Mr. Bonhart[?] was at the post office, he saw a well-known beggar paying in at the post office a deposit of 750 zł into the P.K.O. (Postal Savings Bank).
On Friday towards evening the same man came into the Amshinover shtibl, where he asked that someone take him home for Shabbat. The lot fell, as it happens, on Mr. Bonhart, who invited the guest to his home for Shabbat.
At the „tish“ (Sabbath table) Mr. B. had a conversation with the guest, during which the latter admitted that he has collected a bit of money from his „clients“ in the Zagłębie district, who favour him with larger donations, and in return he gives them blessings...
Pledge Campaign for the Free-Loan Fund

[Będzin — charity.] As every year, this year too the administration of the Gemilut Chesed (free-loan) fund has proclaimed a nedarim (pledge) campaign, which will take place during the days of Passover.
The pledge campaign is intended for the benefit of the Gemilut Chesed fund, which supports hundreds of merchants and craftsmen with interest-free loans.
An Inquiry from the Olkusz Kehilla: When Will the Maimonides Celebration Take Place in Będzin

[Będzin — kehilla.] The other day the kehilla administration received an inquiry from the kehilla administration in Olkusz as to when the local kehilla will celebrate the birthday of Maimonides (the Rambam).
— Apparently the Olkusz board members (dozory) are not aware that the Będzin kehilla administration busies itself with engaging cantors, shochtim and rabbis, and not with such „nonsense“ as arranging a Rambam celebration...
Cantor Żupowicz Leads the Passover Prayers at the „Mizrachi“

[Będzin — cantorial.] The administration of the „Mizrachi“ synagogue has engaged the former[?] cantor Ozer Menachem Żupowicz to lead the festival prayers in the above-mentioned synagogue.
Cantor Żupowicz will pray accompanied by an enlarged choir
Reb Yehoshua David, of Blessed Memory

[Będzin — Obituary.] An old cedar has fallen: Reb Yehoshua David, of blessed memory, has died. This is not the place to appraise the rare virtues and good qualities of the deceased; it is a loss that cannot be restored — it will never come back. Such a type of Jew, who was far from the world of falsehood, far from the political machinations and swindles that have taken root by now[?] even in the rabbinic courts. Reb Yehoshua David knew only that the world stands on three things: on the Torah, on divine service and on deeds of loving-kindness. From early morning until late at night his mouth never ceased from study, and besides he was a lovable person, the great humble man and a rare simple, guileless soul.
———
Many hundreds of people from the Hasidic world took part in the funeral, which took place on Sunday afternoon.
In front of the Ger shtibl short eulogies were delivered by the dayanim Friedberg and Lipszyc. The deceased was then brought into the beit midrash, where hakafot were made with him.
At the cemetery a short eulogy was given by Reb Mendel Lewin, son of the Będzin Rabbi, of saintly memory.
Sosnowiec: Matzos from Out of Town and... Chuppah Poles

[Sosnowiec — Community, rabbinate, kashrut.] Since the appointed commissarial council of the kehilla took over the government, certain functions have been taken away from the unofficial rabbis in our town, and all the kashrut "concessions" have been handed over to Rabbi Szwarc.
As the festival of Passover approached, an ordinance was issued by the kehilla's commissarial council that only Rabbi Szwarc may kasher ovens. The ordinance aroused strong agitation in the nationalist circles that group themselves around Rabbi Hager, and in response the "Mizrachi" bought a large consignment of matzos from out of town, in order to compete with the bakers who had been "kashered" by Rabbi Szwarc.
The Mizrachi's action caused alarm among the bakers, who decided to turn to the "Mizrachi" with a request that the matzo struggle be withdrawn.
In this connection, delegations of the bakers' guild and the journeyman bakers intervened with the Mizrachi's administration, which, realising that the matzo campaign could ruin dozens of Jewish families, withdrew the decision to bring matzos from out of town.
Besides this, actions are also taking place against the "chuppah concession", which has likewise been handed over exclusively to Rabbi Szwarc.
The first "revolutionary" step was taken by a well-known Hasidic Jew who did not want Rabbi Szwarc as officiant (mesader kiddushin) at his daughter's wedding, and when the rabbi therefore refused to give the chuppah, they took 4 poles and a tablecloth, and as the song goes:
— "In a quarter of an hour there's a chuppah"...
Other in-laws have already followed this example, and, as people say, every society or organisation is to "manufacture" its own chuppah poles...
From the Artisans' Association

[Sosnowiec — Artisans.] Last Sunday a conference of all the guild elders (cech starszowie) was held at the premises of the Artisans' Association, with the participation of the councillors of the Chamber of Crafts, Messrs. Director Manor, Szyluszek[?], Goldsztajn and Kilsztok[?]. The chairman, Mr. Langer, opened the conference. In his address of welcome he explained the tasks of the conference and said that the board of the Artisans' Association, as the representative of the Jewish artisans, intends by means of the conference to acquaint the Polish artisans' representatives with the work of the Jewish association on behalf of the artisan class, and also to point out the wrongs done to the Jewish craftsmen in many respects, as in the question of issuing certificates of acquired rights: inspections are carried out among the Jewish artisans without the participation of Jewish guild representatives. As a result, the outcome of such an inspection mostly turns out to the detriment of the Jewish craftsman; many Jewish artisans are refused artisan cards, and thereby they lose their right to independent work. Then chairman Langer spoke on the question of examining older Jewish craftsmen, because the methods applied in the examinations are tendentious, since one should ask only professional questions or hold a practical examination, but not ask whether the craftsman knows the Polish language, history and geography.
Director Manor thanked the Artisans' Association for its initiative, which leads to cooperation with the Polish artisans, and declared that in Poland all artisans, without distinction of nationality and faith, have equal rights, and there are no restrictions whatsoever regarding the Jewish artisans.
After the speeches of Messrs. Councillor Szyluszek and Goldsztajn, Secretary Baum reported on the questions: acquired rights, dispensations and qualification examinations, the participation of artisans in the appeals[?] commission, etc.[?]. After a short speech by Mr. Silberschlag, chairman Langer closed the conference.

[Sosnowiec — Culture, charity.] This evening a recitation evening by the famous German actor Kurt Katsch will take place at the local municipal theatre; he will recite a series of works by European and Jewish classics.
The proceeds go to the summer colony of the "TOZ" society.
It is to be hoped that the evening will be well attended and will help "TOZ" obtain the desired income.

Life in Kielce

[Kielce — page header.]
Friday, 9 Nisan 5695.
Friday, 12 April 1935.
Danger That a Thousand Poor Jewish Families Will Be Left Without Matzot for Passover!

[Kielce — kehilla, Passover flour relief.]
As we have already written, the kehilla turned to the well-to-do payers of the kehilla tax ("etat") asking them to give an advance ("a conto") on this year's etat. This etat income was to be used for the kimcha [Passover flour] campaign, for which nearly five thousand Jewish souls are waiting.
To our greatest regret, very few etat-payers responded to the kehilla's request. The greater part, among them quite well-to-do Jews, do not want to give a penny, and the fact that a thousand poor families will, God forbid, be left without matzot for Passover — does not bother them.
Despite the exceptionally energetic and devoted work of the kehilla presidents Piotrkowski and Goldman, it is almost certain that this year's kimcha campaign will not end with any great success.
To blame for this scandalous indifference to Jewish need are mostly the upstart war-profiteers, who have frozen hearts and do not want to listen to the great cry of woe of our lonely and unfortunate brothers and sisters, who will celebrate our festival of freedom, Passover, in a heavy and embittered mood and with broken hearts.
To his shame, the name should also be mentioned of an upstart war-profiteer, Mr. Ts., who this year bought himself a large house in Kielce and paid cash, as is reported, over eighty thousand złoty, and did not want to give a penny to the kimcha campaign. It was not a donation that the kehilla leaders asked of him, only an advance on the obligatory etat for the year 1935 — and even that this miser did not want to give. The same was done by several other gentlemen, whose names we shall yet publish.
But let our Kielce Jewish citizens, who are known everywhere as compassionate and good, devoted Jews, not take an example from these few misers, but, while there is still time, take an interest in the fate of the thousand poor Jewish families in Kielce who, as said, are threatened with being left without matzot for Passover!
It is late, Passover is already here, and all of us together must help the unfortunate families!
Robbery Attack by "Polite" Bandits on Jewish Merchants

[Kielce region — crime.]
This week several armed bandits attacked, in a forest beyond Zwoleń (Kielce voivodeship), several Jewish merchants who were travelling with the carter Yekl Bernsztajn. After terrorizing the travelling merchants, they robbed from the carter Bernsztajn 20 zł and from his wife 160 zł and various belongings, whereas from the rest of the travellers the bandits robbed nothing.
Having taken the money, the bandits took off their hats, "politely" took leave of their clients and went back into the forest. The police are searching for the bandits.
Festive Opening of the Zionist District Conference in Kielce

[Kielce — Zionism; local news.]
The district conference of the General Zionists in the Kielce voivodeship takes place on Monday, the third day of Chol HaMoed Passover.
The festive opening takes place in the hall of the Teatr Polski, Monday, at 11 in the morning. The further proceedings of the conference will take place in the hall of the Zionist Club.
On behalf of the Zionist Central Committee the following gentlemen will take part in the gathering: Dr. Higres[?], editor Moshe Kleinbaum, Eng. Landsztak, Yechiel Frenkel and the head of the aliyah department at the C.C., secretary Kaminer.
From the information that the organizing committee has received so far, it can be seen that over 100 delegates from about 50 towns of the Kielce voivodeship will take part in the conference, about 100 out-of-town guests and others.
The Zionist district conference will thus be transformed into a great Zionist demonstration.
—o—
Łacki-Bertoldi in Kielce
At the last meeting of the local Keren Hayesod committee it was decided to proclaim this year's Keren Hayesod campaign on 4 May.
The campaign will be proclaimed by Łacki-Bertoldi and by the well-known Zionist activist M. Białopolski.
The Keren Hayesod committee is already making all the necessary preparations for the opening of the new campaign.
—o—
Heavy Rains in the Kielce Voivodeship
For several weeks rains have been falling continuously in various areas of the Kielce voivodeship, because of which the pre-holiday season suffers very much. No danger of flooding threatens.
—o—
Arrest and Heavy Fines for Not Registering Children
We once again draw the attention of our esteemed readers to the fact that the Kielce magistrate has extended the deadline for carrying out the marriage and birth registrations until 15 May of this year. After this deadline those who have neglected the registrations will be punished with unconditional arrest of up to 3 months and in addition with heavy fines.
A Dog Drags a Woman's Hand with Manicured Nails Around the Street

[Kielce — city, police.]
This week 2 boys noticed how a dog was dragging around a human hand at Bodzentyńska 68. The neighbours of the said street reported it to the police, who began an energetic investigation, at the same time taking the hand to the police commissariat. Various versions soon spread in the town, among others that the hand belonged to a woman who had been seen that same evening walking with two suspicious persons, by whom this woman was supposed to have been murdered. The police therefore searched in various places in the said house, as well as in the big heap of rubbish, and found nothing.
After a longer investigation it was finally established that the dog had dragged the hand out of a heap of rubbish at Bodzentyńska 68, and that it had been amputated on 23 March of this year in the municipal hospital from the worker at the local "Kadzielnia", Bolesław Giczylski[?], and the hand had been thrown into the rubbish by the hospital staff together with various dirty bandages.
Kielce Relief Committee in Toronto Sent 1,500 Dollars of Passover Aid for Kielce Jews

[Kielce — relief and charity; Passover.] On a mission of the Kielce Relief Committee in Toronto, the Zionist activist Mr. Mordechai Wajcblum of Ottawa stayed in Kielce this week; he distributed about 1,500 dollars which the said committee had sent for the poor Jews of Kielce — of this, 1,000 dollars from American relatives, and about 500 dollars Mr. Wajcblum distributed to transient paupers (orchei-porchei).
Warsaw Engineer Takes Over the Kielce Factory “Marmur”

[Kielce — industry and labour.] The “Marmur” factory in Kielce, which had lately been in an exceptionally difficult financial situation and remained owing its workers over 20 thousand złoty, has been taken over by the engineer Jan Weber of Warsaw. The factory has resumed work and employs 300 workers.
Deputy Madeyski to Become Kielce Voivode

[Kielce — administration and state.] The Polish press reports that in political circles in Warsaw it is spoken of as a certain fact that Deputy Madeyski will shortly be nominated Kielce voivode in place of Dr. Dziadosz, who is [serving as] voivode in Kielce.
District Inspector Kowalik in Zagłębie

Young Jewish Man Dies Suddenly at the Sosnowiec Investigation Office

[Sosnowiec — police.] In Sosnowiec the 31-year-old Abraham Landau of Częstochowa, owner of a belt [?] ("pasy") factory, was arrested in the street.
At the investigation office the arrested man declared that he was from Warsaw, but one of the secret agents present declared that Landau was a resident of Częstochowa.

What's New in Upper Silesia? — From Jewish Cultural and Social Life in Katowice

[Upper Silesia — Katowice, Zionism and culture.]
Zionist mass meeting
On Monday evening an impressive Zionist mass meeting took place in the "Powstańców" hall, with the participation of the well-known scholar and gifted speaker Dr. Alszwanger.
On the handsomely decorated platform the seats of the presidium were taken by Messrs. Dr. Rapaport, the chairman; Dr. Alszwanger; Dr. Brauging [?], president of the Katowice "B'nai B'rith"; and Finkelstein of Kraków.
After the opening by the chairman Dr. Rapaport, Mr. Finkelstein spoke about the rapid development of Eretz Israel and about the need to steer the building process in the proper direction.
Then Dr. Alszwanger began his well-constructed lecture on "The future of the Jewish people".
The lecturer explained scientifically, in very popular language, the great moral significance of the people for the individual — the protection that his cultural belonging to his people gives the Jew — pointing out that the German Jews, in their present spiritual collapse, cannot find any consolation in the works of Goethe and Schiller, as our grandfathers found it at a critical time in our old holy books. As characteristic of our situation in the world the speaker recalled a conversation with an Italian Jew, and this is what the Jew said: "that in spite of our being Jews, we are nevertheless tolerated and even esteemed". But — exclaimed Dr. Alszwanger — how much humiliation lies in the words "in spite of". We must bring it about that people do not say "in spite of", but "because I am a Jew I am esteemed".
The speaker declared that the Jewish people is now creating in Eretz Israel its third work after the Bible and the Talmud, and called on everyone to help revive the old-new Jewish home.
The numerous audience, made up of all strata of Katowice Jewish society, warmly applauded the speaker for his original ideas.
Lecture by Łacki-Bertoldi and Dr. Sack
The League for Labour Palestine organised in the "Powstańców" hall a Palestine meeting on the 15th anniversary of the death of Joseph Trumpeldor and his comrades.
After Mr. Boim explained the purpose of the meeting, Mr. Łacki-Bertoldi began his lengthy and enthusiastic lecture about the great fallen heroes of Tel Hai, who created the synthesis of labour and heroism, winged by the great idea of building Eretz Israel on healthy national and social foundations.
After depicting the positive and negative sides of the Yishuv that is building itself up, the speaker appealed for contributions to the campaign to build up Tel Hai and thereby erect a worthy monument to the dreamers of the Jewish renaissance.
Dr. Sack too spoke in a warm tone about Trumpeldor, who is unfortunately exploited and falsely understood as a mere militarist by a certain Zionist trend; the speaker said that the Zionist workers are beginning to create a great constructive work with the building up of Galilee, and thereby honour the fallen fighters not only with the yearly march to the common grave at Tel Hai.
A. R. W. Y.
