[Opinion — the boycott of Nazi Germany; Zagłębie and Upper Silesia.]
The free trade with Germany. — To the attention of our anti-Hitler committees.
When Hitlerism began to rage and the bestial instincts were poured out upon our brothers in the German hell, Jewish circles were constantly debating in what way world Jewry should react to the barbaric deeds. Various projects and concepts were then put forward, and one of them was that first of all one should stop trading with Hitler-Germany; above all, every contact, every dealing with the barbarians should be broken off.
Our hot-headed youth, the „kzekoylber“ [?], thought that with this the bird had been caught and the hare shot. They calculated that, since Germany lives mainly from exports and Jewry throughout the world has a large share in them, salvation would come that way. They adopted resolutions: as long as our brothers in Germany are not treated equally with all other citizens, so long will Germany be cut off for every Jew.
Our more conscious elements, those who looked at all this more clearly and more profoundly, those who made a precise reckoning, understood that Germany would not be frightened by it and that they would hardly lose [?] anything by our resolutions. And this is also understandable, because after all we are weak as a straw against a state, however strong we may want to be with our modest forces. The resolution itself — not to trade with Germany, not to set foot on her soil — bore a rather demonstrative character. Not buying in Germany sounded more like a protest than economic pressure.
But what have we gained [?] What has time shown us? We have felt that in our unity lies hidden a great, unbelievable strength. True, we must never overestimate our forces, because that is a great failing on our side, but we must not underestimate our abilities either.
Statistics have shown us that, although Germany legendarily cheapened her export articles, in such a way that the government created a special fund to subsidise them, it has nevertheless reached the point where exports have been reduced to the maximum, and in Germany's collapse a very great role is played by the fact that they are stuck with their articles and have no possibility of exporting.
It is enough for us that Germany's trade balance shows a deficit from last year which [amounts to] 2 million marks.
We did not expect this gain. True, the Polish Jews have the smallest share in the merits; America, Holland and Switzerland distinguished themselves more, where our brothers there have great merits. But be that as it may, we can be proud that we, with our modest forces, were able to exert pressure on Hitler-Germany. And it is interesting that the pressure has reached such a height that again and again [?] disguised travelling salesmen appear, who want to obtain by cunning ways orders for their firms, offering at the same time the most brilliant conditions.
The Germans are clever and refined, and although [?] they know that not everywhere do the domestic articles stand at the same level as theirs, they are nevertheless afraid to trust and to let other brands take root [?], even when these are lower in quality than theirs.
We do not know how it is elsewhere, but here with us in Zagłębie and Upper Silesia people have become very susceptible [?] to these convenient [?] conditions, and with a light conscience they look for a permission both to trade with them and to visit them.
Earlier, it is true, people were very ashamed, and they traded with Germany just as with contraband goods. Of course, rarely did any of the responsible merchants and Jews want to lay a hand on a German article; still, a few individuals were found who fulfilled their „duty“ secretly.
But all this was at the very beginning, when Hitlerism began to rage, when the wound was still fresh, when Jewish blood was being shed incessantly and when the cries reached [?] up to the heart of heaven.
Since that time, however, two years have passed, and although things have not become better in Germany, people have got used to the troubles. They have become indifferent to the inhuman tortures, and they no longer stop to think when it comes to making a deal with a German firm.
So it is told that our brethren the Children of Israel have begun with great relish to do business with Hitler-Germany. All sorts of Jews do business, respectable and not respectable, pious and free-thinking, and nobody, God forbid, is ashamed, as used to be the case once. People do not take into account at all that conscience does not agree with reason, and they act as is healthier for the pocket.
Is there any reaction to this among us? True, there are anti-Hitler committees whose task should be to react as sharply as possible to impermissible phenomena concerning trade with Hitler-Germany; unfortunately they have already cooled off and deal with the questions only superficially, as they say, to fulfil the obligation; otherwise they would surely not have allowed this open free trade.
We were sure that the holiday and Chol HaMoed days would be used among us for propaganda to strengthen the boycott against Hitler-Germany. As it turns out, however, nobody even gave it a thought. It will be enough to tell that the Jews of Zagłębie do not even know that Zagłębie was represented at the anti-Hitler conference which took place a few weeks ago in Warsaw. Apparently our delegates did not even feel any need to give a report on what the general activity in the country looks like and what prospects are being prepared for the future.
Such a way of acting on the part of the committees is absolutely out of place. After all, they were not created in order to stifle [?] the activity, but on the contrary, to strengthen and awaken the obligation both as a Jew and as a cultured human being.
A resolution must be adopted once and for all that world Jewry is against those Jews who sell off our most vital [lit. bloodiest] interests for the first and best „little deal“ with Hitler-Germany. Such Jews — even if they be the very top of society — must be removed from the Jewish community. One must tell them quite openly and boldly that their place is outside the camp: one must not greet them, not stretch out a hand to them, not associate with them in society. Let them know that they are the refuse of the Jewish community, since our sufferings do not hurt them and they do not want to listen to the Jewish sighs.
With disgust and abhorrence we must turn away from these sold souls, for whom apart from money nothing exists.
A sacred duty lies upon our anti-Hitler committees to renew and strengthen the responsible work imposed on them and not to allow the terrible lawlessness of the trade with present-day Germany, which leads to the stage of legal deal-making; at the same time all those who go against the most vital interests of world Jewry must be unmasked.
R. Let.
Kiss-Business.

A terrible decree is approaching the young folk, and just in time for spring.
The Polish newspapers and some organisations of Polish women have launched a campaign against... kissing.
This does not mean, God forbid, that one should not kiss at all. It is hard to believe that a women's organisation could be found, even one of old grannies, that would agree to such a ban[?]. It is only about not kissing hands, against the „całuję rączki“ [„I kiss your little hands“, the Polish courtesy phrase].
There is a philosophical justification for this: every person is allotted in advance how many kisses he is to give and receive in his life. If one kisses hands, one therefore robs[?] other areas of the kiss.
There is also a hygienic standpoint: some ladies' little hands would[?] gladly forgo the pleasure of a nose and a mug finding rest on them.
There is a further, comic standpoint: the „całuję rączki“ often takes comic forms; it is enough to catch a glimpse of who kisses whom and how.
On the Jewish street a sort of kiss-„shmegdrikism“[?] has simply developed. Young yeshiva lads, even ones in Jewish caps, also think that with a kiss on the hand they are saving their whole „progress“.
Strategists would[?] even be in favour of preserving the kiss method. The hand-kiss helps many young men out of all sorts of embarrassments. Many a man expresses with a kiss what he cannot say with his lips.
At any rate, the anti-kiss campaign is already in full swing, and anti-hand-kiss leagues have already been formed in various towns.
The Jewish hand-kiss-ware youth is in danger.
It is possible that in Zagłębie the „koła kobiet“ [women's circles] will not join the anti-kiss league, and then Zagłębie will be saved.
Girls and women who have long been trying to get rid of uninvited hand-kissers, however, already have a brilliant way out of the situation. They have the choice of pulling back the little hand, or of not letting it be lifted up and answering:
— „Dziękuję“ [thank you], I belong to the anti-kiss league.
A. Szwarcer.
Counting (Sefirah)...

For thousands of years Jews have been obliged to fulfil the commandment of sefirah, of counting; apparently, as soon as the Jews became a people, they began to count. Already in the wilderness Moses our Teacher counted the Jews, and later they also counted the half-shekel — so many heads, so many shekels, that is: wherever there is a Jew, there must be counting.
Since then we have kept on counting without stop. We counted (paid) poll tax, cattle tax, contribution tax, and just counted and counted.
It is well known, after all, that the greatest payers (counters) are Jews. We count out money for „obrotowe“ [turnover tax], „dochodowe“ [income tax], „szyldowe“ [signboard tax], „drogowe“ [road tax], „wasserowe“[?] [water tax?], „kryzysowe“ [crisis tax], and since we are Jews, we also pay „etatowe“, „kahalowe“[?] [kehilla tax], and so on in order and in order.
So it has gone on for hundreds and perhaps thousands of years. We lived only by virtue of having counted into the state treasury of all the kings and princes, under whose grace, thanks to this counting, we were allowed to live.
But a time came when there is no money left[?], there is nothing more to count; yet we are Jews after all, so we must go on counting, and if not money, then at least other troubles — „and ye shall count for yourselves“. We must keep on counting without stop.
Now I have a little slip which I put before those Jews who can no longer count any money, so that they may nevertheless fulfil the commandment of sefirah.
Count, Reb Yudl, how many livelihoods have lately been torn out of Jewish hands, while we have been left on the „meat bench“[?].
Count how many parties there are[?] on the Jewish street. It seems that in this counting you will exceed the measure of the sefirah, in which you need only count to 50. Our parties you will have to count much further; and when you have finished counting the parties, start counting again how many factions each party has — and I promise you that you will grow tired with counting.
Count how many Zionist funds there are[?] today on the Jewish street, and tell them that this is the reason none of them has any success.
Count how many Jewish officials are[?] employed in the state offices, municipal institutions and also in the sick funds; and if you are counting anyway, be so kind as to count on this occasion how many Jewish workers are employed by our Jewish-national manufacturers, who preach from the public platforms about a Jewish productive life as the only conclusion for our future life.
Count how many Jewish intellectuals cannot and will not read any Jewish newspaper or a Jewish book; count how many Jewish educated young ladies know anything about our classics and how many go to a Jewish lecture or to the Jewish theatre. On the other hand you may count how many of them go to the dance halls, card clubs or to the Polish „szmonces“ [cabaret jokes].
Count how much electric light is used up in the kehilla during the council sessions, where only nonsense is talked and the real matter is never reached; and count (a stenographer specially engaged for the purpose could best do it) how many words each „dozór“[?] [board member] or parnas lets out of his mouth at such a session — words that stick like peas to the wall.
Count how many societies, associations and institutions we have in town, and count straight away how many flower days each society holds in the course of the year.
Count — on the contrary, try to count even one cultural institution that we have in our town.
Count our speakers, „Kokhlefls“ [busybodies], noise-makers, who grow like mushrooms after rain and who „chop the teakettle“ [chatter] at the various meetings and academies that they arrange.
Count the signatures the Revisionists collected for the petition, and them a ...[?]; count the individual petitions that arrived at the Polish Foreign Ministry and also to the English king, for I fear that if you do not count them, no one else will count them either...
Count the queue of those who this year, poor souls, came for „kimcha“ [Passover flour relief], and you will have a notion of our great poverty, which has spread wide across the Jewish street.
Count, little brother, how many evictions will be carried out with the coming of the summer months, and count straight away the families who will be left homeless.
Count how many Jews and communal workers[?] break the boycott and go on trading with murderous Germany — and nevertheless it does them no harm; they continue to stand at the head of Jewish society and demand honours.
Count the bit of small change gambled away in the clubs that pass themselves off as cultural and language institutions.
Count how many denunciations by the Jews of Dąbrowa, by those who come „for the sake of Heaven“, are lying with the prosecutor and the examining magistrate.
Count how many „dozors“ and parnasim of the Będzin kehilla are still left who have not yet been infected with bribery „for the sake of a shochet“...
Count the Jewish words spoken at the sessions held so far of the kehilla commissioners' council in Sosnowiec.
Count how many Jews — supposedly zealous Gerer young men, who speak only in the name of strengthening the faith — broke the communal ordinance and bought shmura flour elsewhere, in order to harm the Talmud Torah.
Count, Reb Yudl — your whole life you keep on counting, with you everything is sefirah; and that is why it is clear why the days of the sefirah are days of mourning and gloom, when one never stops counting!...
Our whole life in exile consists of counting and counting — of sefirah..
Samal.
Remarks

[Article — politics, antisemitism and peace.] By Sz. Rotenberg.

The Lwów version.
A short while ago the Endeks [Endecja, the Polish nationalists] in the "Ladoer" [sic; probably Łódź] city council showed a model of how their theories ought to be carried out in reality. Without any diplomatic tricks, but with open, cynical impudence, they adopted a whole series of anti-Jewish resolutions which in no respect fall short of the Hitlerite extermination methods in Nazi-land.
None of us ever had any illusions regarding the "humanitarian" methods that the Endeks will apply in solving the Jewish question in Poland. We know very well that with them it is called a "holy" war of extermination in the spirit of "thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth", in which they use the old Jesuit motto: "the end sanctifies the means".
But precisely because of that open, zoological hatred of Jews, the gentlemen of the Camp of Great Poland [Obóz Wielkiej Polski] are less dangerous than our so-called BB [BBWR, the government bloc] protectors, according to the well-known saying: "God protect me from my friends; from my enemies I will protect myself."
What the tactics of our "protectors" look like they showed most clearly in the Lwów city council.
For many years the Jewish community of Lwów received from the local city council a subsidy for its relief fund amounting to 180 thousand gulden [colloquial for złoty], which in time was pressed down to 110 thousand gulden; recently, with the help of the BB votes, even the reduced sum was struck out entirely.
What is characteristic here is the motive these people give. They claim that they want to give Jews equal rights with Christians, and the magistrate [municipality] will take care of all the poor without distinction of faith.
But how such "caring" for the Jewish poor will look in practice is not hard to imagine. We feel too strongly the "tender" and "fatherly" hands of our "providers" to have any trust in them in so delicate a matter as weighing out[?] the right proportion in dividing relief between the Jewish and non-Jewish population.
Equal rights — a magic word — we too wish for it with all our hearts. But it must happen in every sphere of everyday life. And first of all one would have to tear down the Chinese wall that bars Jews' access to state and municipal posts, to the various work positions and sources of livelihood. Here, however, they begin to introduce "equal rights" by striking out the last relief items for the poorest of the poor. And it is truly hard to classify which is worse: the Endek Gleichschaltung or the Sanacja "equal rights"!

"Vox populi".
Throughout all of human history the spiritual and temporal rulers have always swindled with the names: God and People. Mutual fratricidal slaughters, rivers of human blood, "goys"[?] [perhaps a misprint for "shveys" — sweat], suffering and pain, are to this day the result of all kinds of political gangsters.
The 3 words "God wills it" [Deus vult] of Pope Urban the Second were enough for the First Crusade to begin and for the world to be turned, over generations, into a slaughterhouse of human flesh.
In his sadly famous palace speech just before the World War, Kaiser Wilhelm cried out with pathos that his voice is the voice of the people. That was meant to say that the people demand the war through his mouth.
In roughly the same way all the other "God-anointed" emperors, kings, sultans, tsars and the remaining satraps delivered their bellicose inflammatory speeches. And since there were never any great differences of opinion between the spiritual and the temporal rulers, a cunning synthesis was combined of "vox populi, vox dei" (the voice of the people is God's voice), and the business was made kosher before God and men.
Had not a handful of diplomats decided the fate of the nations, but rather a true popular vote (not after the fashion of Hitler and his like), the world would surely now have had an entirely different spiritual, moral and economic face.
A classic example:
At a time when a mad armaments race is going on, when billions are swallowed up by various sea and air fleets, poison and death gases, the English government circles have carried out a survey among the millions of voters on the most topical political problems.
Although the survey is not yet finished and so far about 6 million people have answered, one can already form a clear idea of the real demands of the masses.
70 percent of the voters declared for adopting sanctions for breaking the peace, 94 percent for general disarmament, 94,5 percent for prohibiting private arms production and arms trade, and 97,5 percent that England must remain in the League of Nations.
That is the true mood, which prevails not only in England but among the masses all over the world, whose slogan is[?]: "Bread and work".
War and political adventures are the business of the various "Führers" and "Duces", who lead the masses astray into an abyss of the most terrible physical and moral ruin.
Jews Will Respond!

[Poland — Investment Loan.] We are being called upon, together with all the citizens of Poland, to subscribe to the so-called Investment Loan. And at the present time this is a patriotic matter of great importance. In a time of economic crises and political difficulties it is still a great piece of luck for the Polish citizen that the government has succeeded over the last few years in keeping its own currency and the balance of trade firm. Thanks to this we avoid severe cataclysms and can think about providing for at least our minimal needs.
We Jews in particular, who do not live from secure government posts but from trade and handicraft and the free professions, must feel the importance of this very stability and help, for our part, to maintain and strengthen it.
At every puff of a little breeze we Jews feel as though we were living at the top of a ship's mast; therefore we are interested in the winds blowing as seldom and as weakly as possible.
And when we were called upon two years ago to the National Loan, we subscribed to it beyond our means. Now we must subscribe to the Investment Loan, which is meant to combat unemployment in the country and to carry out various investments that are important for the security of the country and for the progress of our civilisation.
Jews will again respond with all the impetus and fire of our readiness to sacrifice in matters that concern the state in general and our own well-being in particular.
True, the holiday just past emptied our pockets, because we had to provide for ourselves and for our poor, and besides we had, incidentally, a whole week of complete rest because of the double holiday — our own (Passover) and our neighbours' (Easter).
But with our Jewish trust and optimism and heightened energy we go on anyway with the struggle for our existence. And since we are used anyway to dividing every groschen we earn in two — half for ourselves and half for the community — we will now add a few more drops of optimism and energetic effort — for the state, and indirectly for ourselves!
Our old, just, never-answered grievances about the equivalent [?] (what we receive in return) may well be reawakened. Especially where public works are concerned, we may remind [the authorities] of the Jewish unemployed and of our equal right to benefit from state work. And our representatives, both in the Sejm and in the city councils, will certainly not miss any opportunity to remind the proper circles of our right and of their duty.
But at the same time we must remember that one of the pillars on which our just demands rest is our loyalty to the state and our constant readiness to help it in its need — from which no claim or counter-claim, no account we have with the government, ever releases us.
The Investment Loan, incidentally, can be covered by half with the National Loan. In a certain sense this creates a relationship of "this one benefits and that one loses nothing", because the bonds of the National Loan, which yield quite a good return, are after all registered [bonds] and lie in the safes like stones. The government, however, will be able to turn them into money. Thus the citizen in fact has to pay only half of the subscribed sum, and that too in small monthly instalments. There is no doubt that this circumstance will make the subscription stronger still.
The plan of this loan is put together very favourably. Every holder of a bond receives not only his interest but also the chance of winning quite substantial sums, even half a million złoty at one stroke.
But the greatest gain is the investment itself — the creation of new sources of livelihood for tens of thousands of unemployed, and public works that are useful in themselves too.
Jews are being called — and they will respond with full readiness and generosity.
P. K.
Heard and Seen

[Będzin — feuilleton „Heard and Seen“; May Day and the united front; Yiddish in Jewish institutions.]
By Ben Amotz.
„Because of Palestine“...
It was not fated — a young man belonging to a left-wing grouping complains to me — that the Jewish and Polish proletariat should demonstrate together on the 1st of May, under one banner; it was not fated.
And do you at least know who is to blame? Who caused the united proletarian front not to come about?
— Who? we ask curiously, who is to blame?
— The one to blame is... Palestine.
And the young fellow, weeping crocodile tears over the destruction of the shattered proletarian unity, explains why the „misfortune“ happened.
We — the Jewish workers' organisations — were invited this year to the conferences called by the P.P.S. [Polish Socialist Party], in order to create a united front for the 1st of May demonstration.
Along came the Right Poale Zion and declared their „ani ma'amin“ [credo] in the „world revolution“ in general and in Palestine in particular.
— What, Palestine?! — the delegates of the „secular mashkes“ [?] began to protest — how can one permit such a scandal, that while Kalman the boot-maker is demonstrating, the word Palestine should be heard? Can such a thing be?
Well, well — a passionate discussion indeed developed over this „treyf word“, until the Right Poale Zion gave up a series of slogans and demanded no more than the following slogans:
— „Long live a socialist Palestine“ and „Long live the Histadrut“.
One would think that even the „Tse'irei Agudat Yisrael“ would have agreed to such „innocent“ slogans... But the Jewish „friends“ of Palestine proved according to the Shulchan Arukh that these slogans too are as treyf as pork, because, firstly, no social revolution at all has taken place in Palestine, and secondly, the word Histadrut gives off some strange Zionist smell... And so one cannot agree.
And the Polish delegates could by no means understand why the „Żydki“ [little Jews] squabble and cannot get along among themselves over such a „drobnostka“ [trifle], over a slogan that does not even concern Palestine... It is after all — said the non-Jewish delegates — a „sprawa rodzinna“, a family matter, so why are you getting so heated?
And there was something else the non-Jewish socialists could not understand: why — they asked — do we not come out against your demonstrating with Palestine slogans, while you Żydki fight so that the word Palestine, God forbid, should not be mentioned? Which „naród“ [nation] has such an element that hates its own land?... This, comrades, is a „naród dziwny“ [strange nation]...
The „third verse“ [the arbiter] also intervened and, for the sake of peace, proposed that to the slogan about a socialist Palestine there be added:
— „A government of workers and peasants“...
The proposers argued that with this amendment everyone would be made kosher who wants to bring a „bright tomorrow“ to the broad Jewish masses and toilers („horepashnikes“), since the word workers also applies to the Arabs, and there are peasants in Palestine too. And the government? There is a hekhsher [kosher certificate] for that too: towards the Revisionists the Histadrut behaves like a strong government...
All these arguments, however, were rejected by our „leftists“; the upshot was that the united front was not created, every group made „Shabbes for itself“ [printed „mitzakh“ [?]], and all of it happened only — „because of Palestine“...
Bravo, Mr. Doctor!
I find myself in the office of a Jewish economic institution, of a small-traders' association, and see:
a Jewish market trader, a plain everyday Jew, is conducting a conversation with the Jewish office clerk (biuralistka); it goes without saying that the conversation is conducted in Polish — that is, after all, a well-known thing. From the Jewish girls employed in the Jewish institutions you will not, God forbid, hear a single Yiddish word; she, the Jewish official, surely cannot compromise herself before a Moshe or a Zeinvel by speaking the mother tongue with him — she would thereby degrade her name as an „inteligentna panna“ [educated young lady]... And it is truly pitiful to watch how Itche Meir the bagel-seller breaks his teeth, gestures with his hands, nods his head — just so that the Jewish „urzędniczka“ [clerk], who has to write the appeal to the Treasury (Skarb) for him, should understand him and write in the „petition“ (prośba [?]) that „his wife has died, the children are ill, and he, the taxpayer (płatnik), is on festering [?] wounds [?].“
— „Czy pan coś zalega?“ [„Are you in arrears with anything, sir?“] — asks the appeal-writer.
Itche Meir, the taxpayer, is dumbfounded by the question. „But I told her the children are lying sick, so why does she want to know whether I too have been lying?“... [pun: Polish zalegać, „to be in arrears“, heard as Yiddish „ligen“, to lie]
———
Later I found myself at the general meeting of „TOZ“ [Society for the Protection of the Health of the Jews]. The audience — doctors only, the cream of the Jewish intelligentsia, people brought up on the Polish language, on Polish culture.
And among them there is a great „chutzpanik“ — Dr. Liberman they call him — who takes his place on the speakers' platform and delivers the report of „TOZ“
— in the Yiddish language...
After the meeting I ask him: Mr. Doctor, where do you get such „audacity“ [?], to speak the mother tongue before such a diploma-holding audience? How do you look in the eyes of your fellow doctors? What opinion will they express about you? Moreover, you may, God forbid, lose your livelihood, because our Jews have no confidence in a doctor who speaks Yiddish...
— Your „arguments“ do not convince me, answers the doctor; by this — says the Dr. — I wanted to emphasise that in a Jewish institution, before a Jewish audience, one must speak Yiddish!
— Bravo, Mr. Doctor!
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Kedoshim)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Kedoshim
The Portion.
—o—
a) "Ye shall be holy" (19:2)
The Sages fixed the criterion of a holy man in a person's attitude to money. "And why did they call R. Menachem ben Sumai the son of holy men? — Because he did not look at the image on a coin" (Pesachim 104a). Whoever hates money is holy. Therefore it is said at "Ye shall be holy": "Ye shall fear every man his mother and his father, and keep my sabbaths", because if you honour your old father and old mother and are not particular about the money it costs you (and about honouring a father the Gemara says: "How far does honouring father and mother go? — Even if he takes a purse of dinars and throws it into the sea, he must not shame him"), and if you keep the Sabbath without looking at the loss of money — by that: ye shall be holy... Never can you preserve your holiness as then, when it comes to losing money... Or Yaakov.
—o—
b) "Thou shalt leave them for the poor and the stranger" (ibid., 10)
We do not find that a blessing is said over leket, shikhecha and pe'ah [the gleanings, forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field]. Just as we do not find that a blessing is said over charity. Why is that really so?
Because for the most part the commandment is not for the sake of Heaven: a person gives charity because he must, on account of the people around him..
And in Berakhot 38 the Gemara says that a thing over which no blessing is made belongs to God. Only after a blessing does a person acquire it.
Therefore it is said: "Unto Thee, O Lord, belongeth righteousness [tzedakah]" — charity belongs to You, God, we do not acquire it, we say no blessing, because — "but unto us confusion of face": all the charity we give is mostly out of shame, out of embarrassment before others..
"And it shall be righteousness [tzedakah] unto us" — then the charity will be ours, then we may say a blessing over it — "if we observe to do all this commandment before the Lord our God, as He hath commanded us" — when we perform the commandment of charity for its own sake, not because of people... Imrei Shefer.
*
Chesed usually means grace, a favour. But chesed sometimes also means disgrace ("it is a shameful thing [chesed]"). To do a kindness is indeed an honour, but for the one who must come to depend on kindness, it is, poor man, a disgrace.. So the very same word means honour for one and disgrace for the other... HaKetav VeHaKabbalah.
*
Of charity it is said: "Greater is he who causes others to do than he who does."
The doer gives money, the one who causes him gives words: he must persuade the doer and talk him round, and "a word is worth a sela, silence two" — silence is dearer than money. And so talking a person round is dearer than money... Zikhron Chaim.
—o—
c) "In righteousness shalt thou judge thy neighbour. Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people. Neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour" (ibid., 15—16)
In a certain town there was a rabbi who was not qualified to issue rulings, and the local Torah scholars fought against him, shouting that he must not occupy a post he had not grown up to.
Once this "rabbi" went up onto the bimah, appealed to his opponents[?] and called out to the scholars: where has "Thou shalt not go as a talebearer among thy people" gone, and "Neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour"? Why do you persecute me and spread gossip against me?
One of the scholars answered him:
Before the warnings "Thou shalt not go as a talebearer" and "Neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour" there is the warning "In righteousness shalt thou judge thy neighbour". If you are no judge, if you are not fit to issue rulings — the following warnings do not apply... because a leader of the community is different from a private individual. His corruption is the corruption of the public, and therefore one must not keep silent about him even privately[?]...
Imrei Chen.
—o—
d) "Ye shall not steal" (ibid., 11)
The Zohar says in one place that in heavenly matters, in learning, one may indeed "steal" another's question and the like.. That is what the verse says: "I the Lord change not [lo shaniti]" — I, God, have changed the "not" of ("thou shalt not steal"): I permitted sometimes to steal after all. "Therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed [lo khlitem]" — you have permitted it to yourselves and wiped out the "not" entirely; there is no "not" at all in "ye shall not steal"... Iggeret HaShalom.
—o—
e) "A just hin shall ye have" (ibid., 36)
The Gemara expounds it: "Your yes [hen] shall be just and your no shall be just", that you should keep your promise; and therefore there is added "I am the Lord which brought you out of the land of Egypt", because sometimes a person rules leniently for himself: towards so-and-so I need not keep my word, he sinned against me. Therefore God said "I am the Lord which brought you out of the land of Egypt": you too were not worthy in Egypt that I should redeem you, that I should keep My promise of redemption, for you had sinned against Me — and yet I kept My word... Or Torah.
—o—
f) "Sanctify yourselves" (20:7)
The reason for this verse is simply to show that a Jew's sanctifying himself must be done in simplicity, without tricks, without making a noise about it... Dover Shalom.

Converts in Russia. (3)

[History — Jewish converts in Tsarist Russia; series, part three.]
By Saul Ginsburg.

Menshikov wanted to turn the free Cossacks there into his serfs, and he tried to carry this out with the help of Polkovnik [Colonel] Skornyakov-Pisarev, who had been charged with carrying out Peter's order concerning Pochep. In the year 1722 Shafirov reported to the Tsar about the illegal acts being committed there. Skornyakov-Pisarev was handed over to the court, and nothing came of Menshikov's plan. With this Shafirov roused against himself both Menshikov and the Ober-Procurator of the Senate, Skornyakov-Pisarev, a brother of the accused polkovnik. Besides them Shafirov had still other influential opponents: Chancellor Golovkin was always afraid that the other would push him out of his office. Osterman, who also served in the Collegium of Foreign Affairs, strove to take over Shafirov's post, etc. [?]. The two [?] sought to settle accounts with him.

Soon they got a suitable opportunity. In the Senate Shafirov made [?] an illegal decision about paying his brother an official's salary for several months, which was not due to him. Menshikov and his followers immediately made use of this, lodged a protest, and the matter was brought before the Emperor. To this was added yet another new affair: that Shafirov, while administering the post, had committed various illegalities, had grabbed state money, used to withhold the revenues, and the like. During the hearing of this matter in the Senate in October 1722 Shafirov quarrelled with Menshikov; they told each other the coarsest words, and Shafirov behaved particularly insolently in this. The Senate session had to be stopped. This was immediately reported to the Emperor, and he appointed a special commission of 10 senators to investigate all the accusations and pass judgement on him. Menshikov worked on the Tsar through the Empress Catherine, who, as is known, had earlier been Menshikov's servant-girl and mistress. It was in his house that Peter first saw her, fell in love with her and married her.

Menshikov's intrigue was successful. Apart from the fact that Shafirov had disgraced the honour of the Senate with his conduct, the Emperor was especially angered that he had grabbed state money. In this respect Shafirov was in fact far from an exception. Almost all of Peter's associates were bribe-takers ["khabarniks"]; they looked upon state money as if it were their own, and in general held that as soon as one sits [?] at the state bowl, one must ladle with as large a spoon as possible. Menshikov particularly distinguished himself in this; he had countless lawsuits against him over bribes and other such things, but because he was the Tsar's favourite he always came out clean.

At the beginning of 1723 the senators' commission in Moscow delivered its verdict. Shafirov was unanimously sentenced to be stripped of all his titles, offices and orders, all his property — and to the death penalty. Emperor Peter forgot everything he owed to Shafirov and confirmed the verdict. The execution was set for 15 February. A day earlier the following announcement was published throughout Moscow: "According to the verdict of the court, on Friday the 15th of February, in the Kremlin, on the square beside the Senate, the execution of a certain highly placed person is to be carried out. Therefore His Imperial Majesty has ordered this to be proclaimed in Moscow with the beating of a drum, so that all may know of it and come there in the morning to see the execution (death sentence).

On 15 February 1723 Shafirov was brought on a simple wooden sledge to the designated square. He was led out onto the scaffold, his hands were bound and he was laid down. The executioner, dressed in a red shirt, with an axe in his hand, was already standing beside him, waiting for a sign to chop off his head. At that very minute the Cabinet Secretary Makarov declared in the Emperor's name that Peter had consented to commute the death penalty to lifelong exile to Siberia. This was the only thing that the Empress Catherine — who had realised that Menshikov's intrigue had gone too far — was able to obtain from her husband. But the terror of death and the shame on the scaffold Shafirov had to endure. Trembling, half dead, Shafirov was led off to the Senate in order to record the Emperor's order and carry out the necessary formalities.

In all Russian government institutions, until the February Revolution of the year 1917, there stood on the table in the session hall the so-called "Zertsalo" [mirror] — a gilded frame with Peter the First's order of 27 [?] January 1724. This order demands that all strictly maintain order at the sessions in the government institutions, and the severest measures are prescribed against anyone who shows obstinacy against the orders. According to the court's verdict Shafirov was sent off to Siberia, but he managed to arrange that he be permitted to remain in Novgorod. Without any means he lived there, under strict guard, until Peter's death, with his household, on 33 kopecks which were handed out to him daily.

Emperor Peter died on 28 January 1725, and before his death he did not manage to designate who would take the throne after him. With the help of the Guards, Menshikov proclaimed the widow Catherine I Empress. Then, at the demand of the aristocratic party, she had to pardon Shafirov.

He was called back from Novgorod to Petersburg (which by then had already become the new capital), got back his titles of honour and became president of the Ministry of Commerce, but Menshikov had still not forgotten his hatred of him. Osterman too, who had meanwhile become Vice-Chancellor in Shafirov's place, was afraid that the other might undermine him; so they dispatched him to Arkhangelsk to organise the local fishery [?] business there.

The Bastard (33)

[Serialized novel — "The Bastard"; installment 33, chapter 5.]
Edw. S. Geliszkowski [?].
A suspenseful tragic novel of an illui (a prodigy).

"Have pity on your young mother," he said to him, "have pity on your young years."
With a sad face, with eyes dried out from tears, Chanele sat by the window and from time to time only let out [?] a heavy sigh.
Beside her stood Moshele, who, pressing her head to his heart, begged her not to cry.
"Do it, Moshele, do it," says Reb Dovidl, "have pity on everyone."
"Rebbe," Moshele groans out in a choked voice, "Rebbe, what shall I do? What do you want me to do? Tear my heart out of me, smash my mind and my brain out of my head, take from me the power of right thinking, put out my eyes so that I may not see the light of truth and justice — then perhaps I will renounce the truth. Rebbe, if you knew what weighs upon my heart, if you knew why I have spent whole days and nights seeking to cleanse mamzerim, I am sure that you would place yourself entirely on my side and would agree with me. I suffer very much and will suffer still more because of my stubbornness, as you call it, but I will not renounce it."
For a while Moshele remains silent and then begins again:
"You will drive me out of the shtetl together with my sick, tormented mother, but I will not renounce my idea until my strength abandons me."
"Moshele, my child, have pity on yourself," weeps Chanele.
"Mameniu, my dearest, how am I to act, how am I to live? I cannot do otherwise. I cannot."

Chapter 5.
Moshele again took up his everyday occupation, seeking the truth with double energy. So as not to be disturbed by those around him, who were keeping an eye on him, he went off to the little wood behind the town and studied books of Kabbalah.
"Who are you?" he suddenly hears a woman's voice.
When he raised his head he saw before him the countess of the shtetl sitting on a horse, and like an embarrassed girl he stood before the countess with his head sunk to the ground.
"Do you know me?" she asks him, jumping down from the horse.
"Yes," he says, raising his head, "I know that you are the gracious countess of this shtetl."
"Do you also know my family name?"
"Yes, Countess, Maruszecka is your family name."
"And what is your name?"
"Mine?" he asks, surprised that the countess is interested in knowing his name.
"Yes, yours."
"My name is Mojżesz [printed 'Mayoshes'?]."
"Rawen [?]," she breaks in.
"Yes, Rawen," he remains astonished that the countess knows his family name.
"I have heard a great deal about you lately and I am very glad that I have met you here. Do you come here to the forest often?"
"Yes, gracious Countess, very often, almost every day."
"And what do you do here?"
"I study."
"The book you are holding in your hand is surely a book of the Talmud."
"No, gracious Countess, it is not Talmud; it is a book of our holy mystical teaching."
"You speak quite good Polish; you are surely not from our parts?"
"No, I was born in the heart of Poland, in Knin [?]."
For a while it became quiet. Countess Maruszecka feels that with every glance of the young man she becomes as if hypnotised; she feels that he who stands here beside her with lowered eyes has in this short time won her heart. "Veni, vidi, vi[ci]" — came, saw and conquered — she quotes a saying of Caesar. In one moment she felt that this modest young man in his long black frock-coat ["shlits-rekl"] has within him so great a power that it makes her weak and overcome. Far higher does he stand in her eyes than the gentlemen who come to her at the castle in their dressed-up [?] and starched dinner jackets ["smokings"]. As the gentlemen dance around her like monkeys, longing for a smile of hers, for a kind word of hers — how happy she would be if this young man danced around her as they do, if he longed as they do for a smile of hers. But as it seems [?], it will not come to her so easily. Some hidden pride is kept within him, and she reads it in his face. The blood does not boil [?] in him; rather, he is far from desiring the tendernesses of a woman; a bud not yet opened is he, in which a piece of sweet life is hidden. No, it will not come easily to her to enjoy that sweet splendour of his. For no man has she yet felt such desire and ardour as for this young man, whom she has known no longer than an hour, and yet he has made such an impression on her that something burns and scalds [?] in all her limbs. He is as beautiful as an angel — she cries out in her thoughts — and has such noble feelings, and just such a one they want to put under a cherem, to shut out of society; and a ray of hope runs past her, a hope that she will be able to be with him and by him. Yes, she will take him to herself when he is cast out by his brethren.
"I have heard," she says, "that a cherem is to be proclaimed against you, that you will no longer be able to be found in Jewish society; is that true?..."
Moshele raises his eyes and looks at her in surprise.
"Is it so? Say, don't be ashamed; I heard about it long ago, and knowing why they want to put you under a cherem, I declare to you that you have won my greatest esteem; I will be proud that I came to know such a man with noble feelings, who is ready to fight for the justice of human beings. Here is my hand, let me become your friend," she says, stretching out to him her delicate, white, velvet little hand.
Moshele becomes as if confused; he does not know what he should do. Never yet in his life had he touched a woman's hand, never yet in his life had he felt a woman's limb in his hand, and here in one moment he was put before a great trial. He does not know what to do. Not take her hand? He knows that it will be a great insult to the countess. Take her hand? He knows that this is a certain sin... And there is no time to ponder; he would like to run away from here, and yet... Not knowing how it came about, he feels his hand in the velvet-white little hand of the countess; something runs from the hand through his whole body, a kind of warmth such as he had never felt before... "I remain your friend," he hears her say to him, and at the same time he feels the breath of her mouth. So fragrant, so warm it is, and he gives a shudder.
"Will you be here tomorrow too?" she asks him. "Come here tomorrow too at the same hour; I will be here too. We will talk, walk through the forest — come tomorrow. Will you come?" she says, and passes her hand over his face.
Two glances meet. They look into each other's eyes; both are silent with their mouths, but their eyes speak instead. Moshele's eyes say that yes, he will come tomorrow at the same hour, at the same time.
She pulls her hand away from his face, quickly and deftly leaps onto her horse, and soon Moshele is covered with the dust left by the horse's hooves; and just as everything was fogged by the dust, so too everything was fogged in his eyes.
As one confused, as in a dream, he remained standing and gazed before him until the silhouette of the countess had vanished. And suddenly he gives a start, as if he had woken from a dream. With his hands he rubs his eyes and does not believe that all this really happened. No, it was a dream. He tears himself from his place and wants to go away, when he sees at his feet a white silk lady's handkerchief. Impulsively he bends down and snatches up the handkerchief, from which such pleasant scents waft. He puts it to his nostrils and draws the scent into himself. And he runs from the place where the beautiful countess appeared to him. He runs, without looking around, home.
The whole day he goes about like a madman. He does not hear what is said to him. Nor does he ask how Reb Dovidl is; nothing concerns him, nothing does he want to know; he begins to long for the morrow, when he will meet the countess again.
And the next day, already very early, a while before the agreed time, he was already standing at the same place waiting for her. And again she came and again she vanished until the following morning, and so for several days in a row.

“The Cooking Ladle” — May.

“Der Kokh-Lefl” (The Cooking Ladle)
Humour and satire. Compiled by Amutslo.

May.
(Isru-khag thoughts of a Zagłębie merchant.)

May has come,
Welcome!
May refreshes —
psh psh psh,
May revives —
and I am delighted!
I am already a year past thirty
and still I cannot grasp
how a person goes into raptures
over a little hill, over a valley,
over a sky,
over a little flower,
and other such nonsense!
And when the sun pours out its rays
one must already fall on one's knees!
And when little flowers give off scent
one must already leap into the air!
And when a little stream winds along
one must already lose one's mind!
And when the grass is already turning green —
so what of it[?]!
May — a fine thing for my granny[?]!
I'll make a living out of it!...
Let us not fool ourselves:
a piece of cheviot, worsted,
has more substance;
there is something to put on,
there is something to wear...
And the rest is “labus”[?], weaknesses;
it isn't worth
whatever lives on the earth...
And in general, and in general,
what good is measuring poetry
when in one's head there buzz and spin
protested bills.
And in general — woe to the poet,
what is he babbling, what is he crumbling —
bah! if only he would at least raise
the price of “manufaktur” [textiles].
— — — — —
Kibitser.
Sefirah Philosophy.

— When does a miser count willingly?
— At the Sefirah [the counting of the Omer].
———
— Why don't women count [the Omer]?
— Because women count when they are about to get married.
Another version:
— Because women often forget the count.
———
— Why is it precisely Jews who count?
— Because Jews have to know how to count.
———
— Why may one not hold a wedding during the Sefirah period?
— Because once you hold a wedding, there is nothing left to count.
———
— Why does Shavuot come precisely when one stops counting the Sefirah?
— Because when there is nothing more to count, everything turns green before your eyes.
Knaporber.

A Psalm-Song for the President.

Our dear president of the Sosnowiec kehilla —
may it not be to his discredit, God forbid —
sits in his kehilla post
as if made to measure!...
Upon my life, they evidently took enough pains,
as they say...
and managed to lay[?] the choice...
upon a man of such stature[?],
who has all-round[?]: “wise and elderly and of fitting appearance”,
as is proper...
and made him king from Sosnowiec to Pogoń and back,
v-r“l and v-r-u“k [abbreviations, meaning unclear]. —
But, as our president himself says,
I mean —
in one of his “witty” articles —
he pours them out, poor fellow, whole cycles of them... —
“Never mind”,
so then, Sosnowiec was destined to have a vessel
“whose hand is mighty in Torah”.
He swims in the sea of the Talmud without fear,
and — by way of reproof, on the Sabbath[?] of portion Metzora,
reviews the foundations of the Torah,
just as he conversed with the pupils in halakha and aggada
and established that “in general they study there with diligence” —
one need only introduce the reforms that the times demand;
and — may I see consolation —
how great he is also in journalism and other worldly matters;
as the poet Bomsheshenokher[?] Kalman says:
one only needs to have where — writing alone is nothing!
But let me not slander — one mustn't!
He copies out “let all who are hungry come and eat —
whence would it come?”,
and sometimes, softly, “to the discontented, a heart” —
it is like a wafer in honey, or like a Piekarski torte;
besides that he is versed in the laws of R' Yaakov the Payer —
when one talks, a man is capable of anything!...

— And so, let us end with a good word:
long live our president R' Dov!
R' Leybele.
From Będzin Artisans' Life

[Będzin — artisans, organizations.]
At the branch of the Central Artisans' Union (Kołłątaja 45) a report meeting took place.
The meeting is opened by the chairman of the association, Mr. H. L. Goldsztajn, who invites to the presidium Messrs. Bursztyn, Arnowy [?], Polasz and others. Mr. Goldsztajn reports on the sad situation of the craftsmen in the present season, particularly of those who work for the shops, where the wage is so low that it is impossible to exist.
Mr. Goldsztajn proposes to turn to the Ministry through the mediation of the Chamber of Crafts with the following demands: 1) that a tariff for work be established. 2) that every shop-owner be obliged to conclude agreements with his craftsmen. 3) that the shop-owners bear obligations towards their craftsmen just as every employer towards his workers, 4) since the rent is not in proportion to the earnings of the craftsmen, it should be reduced by 40 per cent, 5) that an “ubezpieczalnia” [social-insurance fund] be created specially for artisans' workshops, which will reduce the expenses and consequently reduce the payment for the registered journeymen, and the surplus money could be used for loans for artisans.
Mr. Goldsztajn announces that in the year 1935 journeymen can more easily sit for examinations, and that for those who wish to sit for master's examinations a special preparatory course will be arranged; that apprentice boys or apprentice girls may be kept only by those who hold a master's diploma, and one must conclude agreements with them and send them to the continuation school.
The resolutions are adopted unanimously.
After a longer discussion, in which Messrs. Moshe Kajzer [?], Dawid Lustiger, Szwajcer, Abramowicz, Leśnicki and others took part, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted: 1) all Jewish artisans in Będzin are called upon to group themselves in the branch of the Central Artisans' Union, in order thereby to create one powerful artisans' organization which shall be able to serve the interests of the Jewish artisans in Będzin, and 2) all artisans are called upon to subscribe to the Investment Loan.
Then circulars are read out: from the Central office, that those who sell their own products at markets need no special patent [trade licence], and those who have already bought such a patent should apply to the association, where they will receive the appropriate information.
Doctor Accused of Leaving a Piece of Gauze in the Lung During an Operation

[Sosnowiec — court, medicine.]
Some time ago Dr. Koszybowicz [?] treated a certain Zofia Chegawa [?], whom he declared to be ill in the lungs and who must by all means be operated on.
Dr. Koszybowicz performed the operation, but after leaving the hospital the patient felt worse every day, on account of which she turned to the above-mentioned doctor.
After treating her the doctor declared to her that he saw signs of consumption in her, and advised her to travel immediately to Bystra, to a sanatorium.
In the course of time a wound [?] opened on the patient, who was staying in the sanatorium, in which a large piece of gauze was found that had already rotted. After the removal of the gauze the woman became entirely well within a short time.
Then she brought a lawsuit against Dr. Koszybowicz, accusing him of having left a piece of gauze during the operation, and demanded from him 10,000 zł. compensation.
The trial, which took place at the Sosnowiec District Court, caused a great sensation in medical circles.
As experts the doctors Trawiński, Zacharski and Oszyński [?] were called, who declared that leaving a piece of gauze during an operation is an impossible thing.
On the basis of this declaration the court dismissed the patient's claim.

[Będzin — Zionism, youth movements.]

Early in the morning the branches from the surrounding towns belonging to the Zagłębie district (galil) arrived. With the singing of “HaTikva” the conference was closed in a very elevated mood.

A 23-Year-Old Jewish Young Man Hanged Himself

[Sosnowiec — tragedy, suicide.]
The local resident Bernstein [Barnsztajn] went with his household to Żarki for the second [final] days of Passover and left as guard of [?] his apartment his cousin, the 23-year-old Israel Tenenbaum.
On Sunday evening Mr. Bernstein came back, but he found the apartment locked. Having waited several hours and Tenenbaum not coming, Mr. B. went off to sleep at a relative's.
The next morning, when Bernstein again found the apartment locked, the matter became suspicious to him and he forced open the door. When Mr. B. went into the third room he saw a terrible sight: from the ceiling above the stove Tenenbaum was hanging on a new rope, in whom there were already no signs of life.
As the neighbours relate, the suicide was seen for the last time on Saturday at about 7 in the evening. At that hour he was in the attic, where he probably wanted to commit the suicide.
The suicide left a letter, in which he asks that no one be blamed for his terrible deed.

Life in Kielce — Our Duty to the Land of Israel

[Kielce — Zionism, Keren Hayesod campaign; article.] (On the Keren Hayesod campaign in Kielce.)
Tomorrow, Saturday night, Jewish Kielce will welcome the ambassadors of the Jewish state on its way, the emissaries of redemption, the famous Zionist activists Dr. A. S. Juris (Land of Israel) and Yaakov Białopolski, who will rouse and encourage the great Jewish public in Kielce to go on forging the golden chain for the land of our past, present and future — the Land of Israel!
The two distinguished guests mentioned come to us at a time of an extraordinarily bitter crisis, at a time when the Jewish people stands broken by despair and hopelessness — at such a time, through the proclamation of the Keren Hayesod campaign in our town, the distinguished emissaries of the “Keren Hayesod” will call on and remind the Jews of Kielce that the people of Israel lives (am Yisrael chai), that we are a people with hopes and duties, that a beautiful, bright, free life awaits us.
And although we are struggling for our day-to-day existence, we will, as until now, continue to fulfil our civic Jewish duty towards our homeland, the Land of Israel; we will double our contributions to the “Keren Hayesod” and also help our emissaries in their holy work.
The Land of Israel is the only hope and comfort in the anxious present, and it brings us the tidings of our bright future and is the only rescue from all our troubles and sufferings.
Blessed therefore be every hand that stretches out its help to the creation and building of our grandiose edifice.
We welcome the start of the Keren Hayesod campaign in Kielce and we are sure that Jewish Kielce will know how to make use of the distinguished guests and to help bring it about that the work is crowned with the greatest success!
We greet the dear guests with the traditional “Baruchim haba'im” (Welcome)!
Ch. Zielony.
The Proclamation of the Keren Hayesod Campaign in Kielce

[Kielce — Zionism, Keren Hayesod campaign.] Today, Friday, the delegates of the Keren Hayesod Directorate in Poland, the well-known Zionist activists Dr. A. S. Juris and Y. Białopolski, arrive in Kielce; they will proclaim this year's Keren Hayesod campaign in our town.
The Keren Hayesod campaign will be proclaimed at a festive academy (gala meeting), to be held at the Teatr Polski tomorrow, Saturday night. At this academy the distinguished emissaries of the Keren Hayesod will appear with lectures on the subject: “How we are building the Land of Israel”.

Today, at 9 o'clock in the evening, a large consultation of all Zionist activists will take place at the Zionist club. Messrs. Dr. A. S. Juris and Y. Białopolski will take part in the consultation.
• • •
On Saturday, at 11 o'clock in the evening, a tea evening in honour of the distinguished guests will take place at the Zionist club, organised by the Zionist women's organisation “WIZO”.
• • •
As we are informed, the most respected Zionist activists of our town, as well as ordinary nationally-minded Jews, have joined the Keren Hayesod work.
There is therefore no doubt whatsoever that this year's Keren Hayesod campaign will be concluded with a surprising success.
Resolutions of the Zionist District Conference.

[Kielce — Zionism.] The second session of the Zionist district conference took place, as already reported in our paper, at the Zionist club and was chaired by Mr. Frenkel.
At the session Mr. Kaminer reported on aliyah and hachshara and on the situation in the organisation, and Mr. Frenkel — on the Zionist victims [those who had died].
At this session a number of deceased Zionists were also honoured by rising, among them the deceased Zionists of the Kielce voivodeship: Prof. Moszkatblit (Radom), Szlomo Ajzenberg (Szydłowiec) and Alte Fuks (Opoczno [?]).
The third session was opened by Laznik[?] Rotsztejn (Opatów). At this session Mr. M. Langer of Warsaw delivered a lengthy lecture on the youth movement in the organisation.
Afterwards the general debate on the lectures given took place. Over 30 delegates from various towns and townlets took part in the debate, at the same time giving reports on their branches.
The fourth session was chaired by Dr. Kirszenbaum (Staszów). At this session Editor Kleinbaum, in his masterly 2-hour speech, answered all opponents, rejecting the claims of some delegates against the Central Committee that it deliberately does not want to join the World Union, and that the C.C.'s representatives at the Palestine Office take no interest in the aliyah affairs of the Zionist activists.
„Our heart — exclaims Editor Kleinbaum — grows sicker and weaker from day to day because of the cries of pain of our comrades, whom we want to help and cannot.“
Then the chairman of the permanent commission, Mr. Ch. Wielany[?], read out the various resolutions, which were adopted unanimously.
Among the resolutions there is also a vote of confidence in the Zionist Executive, in the C.C., in Deputy Icchak Grünbaum, in comrades Kleinbaum and Kaminer, a resolution on joining the World Union, etc.
Editor Wielany delivers a speech of greeting in honour of the departure for Palestine of the deserving Zionist activist Mr. Jechiel Frenkel and wishes him, in the name of the gathering, many, many more years of fruitful work for the good of our people and land.
An inspired closing speech is delivered by Mr. Kaminer, who at the same time congratulates Mr. Frenkel on his departure for Palestine and proposes inscribing Mr. Frenkel in the Golden Book of the K.K.L. [Jewish National Fund]. The proposal is received by all delegates with ovations in honour of Mr. Frenkel.
Mr. Frenkel thanks them for the honour and dedicates a few warm words to the delegates and to the Kielce comrades.
„…for organising the conference.]“
At 6 o'clock in the morning the conference was closed in an elevated mood to the strains of „Hatikvah“.
May Day celebration of the League for Labour Palestine.

[Kielce — labour movement.] The League for Labour Palestine received, for the first time in Kielce, a permit to hold the May Day celebration in the open air. The League (Right „Poale Zion“, „Hitachdut“, „HaPoel“, „HaOved“, „Frayhayt“, „HeChalutz“, Kibbutz Borochov, among them butchers[?] and other trade unions), numbering several hundred persons, marched in closed ranks through the Jewish streets, singing the „Internationale“, the „Shvue“ [the Oath], „Hatikvah“ and other Hebrew songs.
After the street procession a large academy [assembly] took place in the „Uciecha“ cinema, at which speeches on current affairs were delivered.
The May Day celebration of the other, non-Jewish parties also passed off quietly.
A woman dies of a heart attack while seeing her children off to Palestine.

[Kielce — tragedy.] This Monday, at 4 o'clock in the afternoon, a certain Abraham Lewenberg left Kielce for Palestine with his family. His mother-in-law, Ejdl Wrycka[?], 53 years old, came from Chmielnik to bid him farewell. After taking leave of her daughter, son-in-law and grandchildren, Mrs. Wrycka, right after the train departed, suffered a severe heart attack at the railway station, and a few hours later she died in the municipal hospital.
From the Torah va-Avodah movement in Kielce.

[Kielce — Mizrachi.] Last Saturday night the annual general meeting of the „Torah va-Avodah“ movement took place in the hall of the Mizrachi „Beit-Am“.
The meeting was opened by Mr. J. Rapaport, who at the same time gave a report on the activity of the „Torah va-Avodah“ work during the last half-year. The financial report, as well as a report on hachshara and aliyah, was given by Mr. P. Harszyk[?]. Mr. S. Liberman reported on the work for the „Keren Kayemet“ and the „Keren HeChalutz HaMizrachi“.
After the discussion, in which a member of the „Torah va-Avodah“ council in Poland, Mr. Gothart, also took part, it was unanimously decided to begin energetic shekel work.
The meeting was closed with the singing of „Hatikvah“.
Festive prayer in honour of the 3rd of May. —o— The 12th L.O.P.P. Week in Kielce.

[Kielce — state holidays.] Today, Friday, at 10 o'clock in the morning, a festive prayer in honour of the Constitution of the 3rd of May will take place in the municipal synagogue, with the participation of representatives of the local military, administrative and municipal authorities, as well as representatives of all Jewish institutions and pupils of all Jewish schools.
—o—
[Kielce — municipal.] The 12th L.O.P.P. [Air and Anti-Gas Defence League] Week in Kielce.
This Monday, under the chairmanship of Starosta Mr. Porembalski[?], the first organising meeting concerning the forthcoming 12th L.O.P.P. Week, which begins on the 12th of this month, took place in the hall of the city council.
A committee of the most prominent Jewish and non-Jewish citizens of our town was elected. The committee has already set to work.
Don't forget the deadline of 15 May! —o— Constituent meeting of the Shekel Commission.

[Kielce — public notices.] We remind our esteemed readers once again that on 15 May of this year the deadline for completing the marriage and birth records expires. After the said deadline the severest penalty will be applied against those who have not completed the records — up to 3 months' unconditional arrest and up to 1000 zł. fine.
—o—
[Kielce — Zionism.] Constituent meeting of the Shekel Commission.
Last week the constituent meeting of the Shekel Commission took place. Mr. J. M. Ajzenberg (General Zionists) was elected chairman; vice-chairman — Mr. Jechiel Grazer[?] (Mizrachi), secretary — Mr. Trąmpczyński[?] (League), and treasurer — Mr. Hojzler[?] (Hitachdut).
The office of the Shekel Commission operates in the premises of the Keren Kayemet (Wesoła 28).

Young Jewish man perishes in the flames.
On Wednesday night a fire broke out in Berish Hochberger's shop in Zawiercie. When the fire had already engulfed the dwelling, the 23-year-old young man ran inside, wanting to save something more. But he could no longer get out and perished in the flames.
The town is plunged in deep mourning.
—o—
Proposal that merchants with 2nd-category patents be required to keep commercial books.
On Tuesday evening a large meeting took place in the premises of the Merchants' and Industrialists' Association in Sosnowiec, with the participation of the director of the Chamber of Commerce, senior official (starszy referent) Szykański, the head (naczelnik) of the tax office and several officials.
The chairman, Mr. Safer, opened the well-attended meeting with a greeting to the guests and gave the floor to senior official Mgr. Szykański, who in his 3-hour lecture discussed the law on the latest tax amnesty, the proposals to change the patent [—], and the proposal that merchants who do not have a turnover of 100 thousand zł. but hold patents of the second category should also be required to keep commercial books.
—o—
Money sought in the Sosnowiec Talmud Torah.
In the night from Monday to Tuesday thieves got through a window into the premises of the Sosnowiec Talmud Torah, where they broke open all the locks of the drawers and of the Holy Ark, presumably looking for money.
In revenge they threw the sacred ornaments of the Torah scrolls out of the Holy Ark.
—o—
Membership drive of „Malbish Arumim“.
The board of the „Malbish Arumim“ society in Będzin is setting about a drive to recruit new members and at the same time to increase the monthly pledges. It is therefore to be hoped that the Jewish population of Będzin will know how to appreciate the institution's many years of merit and will help it, so that it may have the means to continue its deeds.
—o—
Catastrophe with a lorry.
Yesterday afternoon, on the road to Czeladź, a catastrophe occurred involving a lorry of the „Gambrinus“ brewery.
The catastrophe happened in the following circumstances: a Christian boy was walking in the middle of the road. The driver, wanting to avoid the boy, crashed at speed into a telephone pole. The result was fatal[?]. The boy was seriously injured, the telegraph pole and a tree were broken, and the car was badly smashed.

Jewish Boy Drowns While Trying to Save His Christian Friend. Tragic Incident in Zawiercie

[Zawiercie — tragedy.] Zawiercie is under the heavy impression of the terrible accident that happened last Monday, in which 2 young lives perished.
On that day, in the morning, 4-year-old Lejzer Liber went off together with his 5-year-old Christian friend Henryk Karcz for a "walk" outside the town.
Passing the unfenced stream of the "Zawiercie" factory, they felt like picking the little flowers that grow on the bank of the stream.
At a certain moment Karcz fell into the stream and began to drown. When Liber saw this, he stretched out his little hands to save his friend, and he too fell in.
When several hours had passed and the children had not come back, people began to search for them until they came upon the traces of the accident, but it was already too late: both children were already dead.
When the terrible news spread through the town, hundreds of people gathered at the spot where the accident had happened; the wailing of the parents and relatives reached the heart of heaven.
A Young Jewish Researcher on His World Journey Has Come to Zagłębie

[Zagłębie — science and culture.] On his way to Vilna the young scholar Dr. Michał Adler, member and correspondent of the International Anthropological Institute in Paris, has come to Zagłębie.
Dr. Adler now comes from a series of towns in Poland where, on his initiative, organising groups have been formed for creating the world-wide Jewish Anthropological-Ethnological Society.
The society's plan provides for the creation of a centre with branches in all the larger Jewish communities in the world, support for expeditions and research work, the publication of a special journal in Yiddish, Hebrew and other languages, and the founding of a special professional publishing house[?].
The society is also to set itself the task of founding a special anthropological-ethnological central institute with all necessary facilities such as a laboratory, museum, library, etc.
Dr. Adler has also come to Zagłębie in order to interest the Jewish public and cultural institutions in this very important task.
In the lectures Dr. Adler will give, he will convey lively greetings[?] about the life, creativity and history of the Jews in Peru, Argentina, Colombia and other South American countries, where he recently spent a long time.
From Artisan Life in Będzin

[Będzin — artisans; taxes.] On Saturday, 2 May of this year, a meeting took place under the chairmanship of the president [of the association] Mr. H. L. Goldsztajn, with the participation of the President [mayor] Mr. Eng. Ruszczkowski[?] and Advocate Wilberszak[?], devoted to the investment loan, the tax amnesty and the situation of the artisans.
Mr. Eng. Ruszczkowski and the chairman Mr. H. L. Goldsztajn spoke about the significance of the investment loan, and it was resolved that the artisans gathered in the premises of the Artisans' Association on 4 May 1935, 350 in number, decided that every artisan who has any possibility at all must subscribe to the investment loan.
Advocate Wilberszak reported on the tax amnesty and explained to those assembled, precisely and diligently, which taxes are remitted wholly or partly and who is entitled to benefit from the reliefs.
Finally the chairman Mr. H. L. Goldsztajn informed those present that every member may apply to the secretariat with his tax receipts, where with the help of the advocate everyone will be advised about his possible tax reliefs, and that appeals may be submitted only until 15 May.
— On Sunday, 5 May, under the chairmanship of the guild elder Mr. L. L. Brama and with the participation of delegates from Sosnowiec and councillors of the Chamber of Crafts, a meeting of tinsmiths, locksmiths, blacksmiths, goldsmiths and watchmakers took place.
Mr. Brama described the difficult situation of the artisans, and especially of the trades affiliated with the metal guild.
After the councillors Golsztajn and Kilstok, Rotensztajn (Sosnowiec), A. D. Balimowski[?] and others had also spoken, it was resolved to convene a joint conference of the Jewish and Christian councillors of the Chamber of Crafts, at which the demands of Jewish artisanry are to be put forward.
— Next Saturday at 4 p.m. a meeting will be held about the new tax reliefs.
Brawler Shot Dead in Olkusz

[Olkusz — crime.] In honour of the 3rd of May an academy (ceremonial assembly) took place in the hall of the Olkusz fire brigade. Among the audience was 25-year-old Henryk Jakubowski (a Christian) from Sławków, who started a row. When a policeman led Jakubowski off to the police station, he put up fierce resistance and threw himself at the policeman. The policeman then drew his revolver, which suddenly went off, and a bullet struck Jakubowski in the heart. Half an hour later he died.
What's new in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — news.]
Maimonides celebration.
On the initiative of the Jewish community in Tarnowskie Góry, a Maimonides celebration took place in the synagogue. It opened with an introductory speech by the community chairman, Mr. Aleksander Kahn, who gave a short biography of the great Jewish thinker. After the chief cantor Mr. Singalewski sang the appropriate chapters of Psalms with the choir, the rabbi Dr. Rubiner delivered a lecture on the subject "Maimonides as a Philosopher".
At the end Mr. Wachsner played several solo numbers, and with that the academy was closed.
Katowice Jewish community opens a Hebrew school.
On the 15th of this month a school for Judaic studies, with Hebrew as the language of instruction, will be opened in Katowice on the initiative of the community board.
The curriculum is: Hebrew, Bible (Tanakh), Mishnah, Aggadah, Jewish history and the geography of Palestine.
Boys and girls aged 7 to 9 will be admitted to the first class.
At the same time special courses will be opened for boys and girls aged 9 to 15.
Porter of the German consulate a member of a gang of bandits.
These days the Katowice police arrested the gang of bandits which on 15 April carried out a robbery in Siemianowice on the 75-year-old Mrs. Kołczowa [?].
The porter of the German Consulate General in Katowice also belonged to the gang.
A theft from the customs office.
In Gołkowice, Rybnik district, 61 kilos of tar were stolen from the warehouse of the customs office.
Hitlerite books and maps confiscated.
By order of the Upper Silesian voivode, a whole series of Hitlerite books and maps was confiscated in Katowice; among others, Hitler's "Mein Kampf" was confiscated, a book about Schlageter's activity in Upper Silesia, and two maps on which the borders between Poland and Germany were drawn differently than in the Treaty of Versailles.
President of the International Chamber of Commerce in Katowice.
These days the president of the International Chamber of Commerce, Fentener-Kissingen [sic; Fentener van Vlissingen], stayed in Katowice, in the company of the Polish ambassador in Paris, Mr. Stebelski [sic], and the secretary general of the International Chamber of Commerce, Mr. Vasseur.
The distinguished guests visited several industrial works in Upper Silesia.
In honour of the 3rd of May
a festive prayer was held in the Katowice synagogue. A speech on the topic of the day was delivered by the rabbi Dr. Vogelmann.
Bandits shoot a merchant dead and rob several thousand marks.
On Friday night, when the merchant P. Berber in Gleiwitz was sitting in his flat counting money, several armed bandits came in, shot Berber dead without any reason and then robbed several thousand German marks.
Railway cashier sentenced to a year in prison.
In the dock of the Katowice court sat the former [?] railway assistant Niewiedział, who had squandered (embezzled) a sum of 33 thousand zł.
Niewiedział was sentenced to one year in prison.
Lwów chief cantor on trial at the Katowice synagogue.
The community board in Katowice has invited the chief cantor of Lwów, Mr. Schrager, to lead the prayers in the synagogue on the festival of Shavuot as a trial.
Elections to the Agudah board postponed.
Last Sunday the "Agudah" in Katowice held a meeting at which a new board was to be elected.
But because of the proposal to elect to the board those members who some time ago took an active part in the Agudist movement, the elections were postponed by two weeks.
Dispute between the butchers and the ne'emanim (kashrut supervisors).
Recently an economic dispute broke out in Katowice between the butchers and the ne'emanim. The dispute consists in the butchers wanting to reduce the ne'emanim's pensions [stipends] to 150 zł. a month (until now 250 zł.).
Conference of the rabbis of the Upper Silesian communities.
On Sunday a conference of the rabbis of the Upper Silesian communities took place in Katowice. At the conference the question of creating an association of the above-mentioned rabbis was debated.
To the Jewish population of Zagłębie. On the new film repertoire of German production

[Zagłębie — boycott of Germany.]
A notice has appeared in the Polish press that the Warsaw cinematographic joint-stock company is releasing onto the market in the coming season the following films, produced in Germany:
"Czardasfürstin" with Marta Eggerth, "Walzerkrieg" with Renate Müller and Willy Fritsch, "Gold" with Hans Albers and Brigitte Helm, "Flüchtlinge" with Hans Albers and Käthe [von] Nagy, "The Secret of the Woronzeff Family" [sic] with Brigitte Helm, "Turandot" with Käthe Nagy and Willy Fritsch, "The Mission of Jan Darg" [sic; Joan of Arc — "Das Mädchen Johanna"] with Angela Salloker, "Amphitryon" with Willy Fritsch and Adele [?] Sandrock, "Zigeunerbaron" with Adolf Wohlbrück, "Mach mich glücklich" with Else Elster and Harald Paulsen, "Ich liebe alle Frauen" with Jan Kiepura and Inge List.
We point out that the said cinematographic company is a branch office of the Berlin film concern "Ufa", which is subject to the anti-Hitler boycott.
The present situation of the Jews in Germany compels us to sharpen the boycott action on all fronts. The Jewish public is therefore warned on no account to visit the cinemas that show the films listed above.
