The Art of Matches and Gymnastics — After the Events with "Hakoach" in Sosnowiec; the Need for Reforms

[Sosnowiec — sport; article.]
There is a Jewish proverb that everything that is "too much" is no good: it is not good, for instance, when something is too good, just as it is worse when something is too bad; too intensive is no good, and too diligent is no great virtue either.
Why has this come up? Because of our youth. Some years ago people looked around and realised that the coming generation could not be raised under the same conditions and on the same foundations as we[?], the older generation; they began to found gymnastic institutions whose task was to raise people with straight shoulders and healthy chests, who would be hardened and able to endure any climate. But when we start doing something, we do not know how to do just enough, and we always think it is not yet perfect beyond perfect — so people were not content with gymnastic exercises and the Turnen movement, but went further and threw themselves into football matches, on which the greatest weight is placed, and the intensity reaches the highest degree. So much so that every minute that goes to waste is a pity. Every opportunity is used, and they play with whoever they can. Nothing stops them, and no account is taken of the conditions in which we find ourselves nowadays; they keep thinking that they have not yet done enough and that the players will not be counted as first-class heroes.
It was for this match that Będzin's "Hakoach" came to us in Sosnowiec to play a return match with their non-Jewish "comrades" of "Czarni"[?]. And why fool ourselves — nowadays it is a matter of course: as soon as "Hakoach" won, they were set upon[?] by the non-Jewish spectators and hooligans, who only wait for an opportunity to throw themselves at Jews, to amuse themselves at their expense and, when possible, to go even further.
Since the match tempers have been inflamed, and in general people are afraid to go out, let alone to cross to a distant street.
And now the antisemitic pen-bandits have set to work, for one strikes the iron while it is hot. The columns of the antisemitic Zagłębie press are filled day after day with incitement against us, and every so often they have some new and fresher invention to provoke, incite and inflame against us as the guilty ones, who of course must be uprooted root and branch. The Christian young man who was wounded in the brawl they already want to make into a saint; they shower him with "flowers" and print his picture in the newspaper, which says: look at the wounded man, see what he looked like. Everything, everything[?] must be exploited to reach the desired goal.
Of course, none of this surprises us, because, truth be told, why should they not exploit this "favourable opportunity", which falls into their mouths like roast pigeons? We know perfectly well that in quiet times, when the Jewish and the Christian population live side by side quietly and peacefully[?], they look for cunning ways to stir up bitterness, if only to raise a storm — and now, when there is so much "work", should they sit[?] with folded hands as though nothing had happened? How often do we watch the black heroes simply gnash their teeth and climb smooth walls, if only to provoke antisemitic pranks, and there — as if the world had turned upside down — not a single lad wants to stir, not even for a cure. How often do we see them barking with foam on their lips and finding nothing to latch on to — so should they perhaps let this golden opportunity go unused, while they wait as for a miracle for something to happen, for something to do? Should they perhaps not exploit such a moment?
Do we not know all this here? Do we not see it? Do we not feel it at every step? Does not every one of us who has eyes open see what a situation we are in and how they look out for an opportunity to swallow us surely[?] alive?
Our living conditions are becoming too hard for one not to see it; the incitement is becoming too drastic for one not to feel it at every trace.
There is no doubt that every one of us feels how tense the situation has become for us Jews, especially in the Upper Silesian and Zagłębie corner, where we are so near to Hitler's Germany. All these black little papers are, after all, an echo from there, where they strive to popularise the very same methods.
And we? It is not enough that we do nothing to ward off the bullets that are deliberately aimed at us; we even want to push our way in where we are not wanted and without whom we can manage very well.
Why — the question arises — must our youth play matches with non-Jewish "comrades", when this becomes dangerous, when it is a matter of mortal danger? Must the Jewish inhabitants of Zagłębie be put in danger for the sake of such whims? Why risk one's life when one can manage very well without it? Who forces our youth to arrange matches with people who become dangerous both to them and to the whole Jewish community? Who forces us to make such heavy sacrifices — and for what? For whom? Is the matter worth the trouble? Is it worth risking lives for nothing and again nothing?
And since it has come to this, we would permit ourselves to tell the youth, who are so deeply absorbed in the art of matches, that God forbid nothing would have been lost if they had not been so immersed in this business at all, for they are already far too busy with "sport". And as we said above, everything that is "too much" is unhealthy, and certainly no great benefit comes of it.
And by the way, how many cripples have we already gained through this wild playing that arises during the contests? In those moments one forgets where one is in the world, and it turns into a kind of game of chance (hazard) that takes on abnormal forms — and one can certainly manage without them. We would still understand playing as a kind of pastime in a solid and decent manner, but by no means whatsoever brutally and without any decent system.
It would in general be only fair that the boards of the societies, wherever they may be, should begin to take more interest in gymnastics and rhythmic exercises; it is worth putting more weight on this, because it makes the body healthy and supple and gives the possibility of successful development, which is an enormous plus for the future of the youth.
Above all, a thorough reform of our gymnastic institutions is required; more attention and supervision are required for this problem, which is the destiny of our future.
It would be advisable in the autumn to convene a broad conference of all the associations in the whole of Poland, where the sorrows and joys of this sporting life could be heard.
These institutions are just as important for the youth as any kind of school, for they too are schools for the youth: with proper supervision they can bring great benefit, and conversely they bring enormous harm. This must be reckoned with without doubt.
For that very reason an understanding (consultation) is needed, at which proper reforms will be adopted that will regulate this sporting life which we call gymnastics.
Dr. Papuri.
Little Feuilleton. “Vayakhel-Pekudei” under One Roof...

“Vayakhel-Pekudei” [two Torah portions read together] under one roof...
My wife and my partner’s wife lived like two little doves: they wore hats from the same milliner, shoes from the same shoemaker, used the same kind of powder and rouge, were treated by the same doctor, lay in childbed in the same clinic, used the same midwife — forever together, the one wouldn’t budge without the other. That is why both of them were given the name “Vayakhel-Pekudei”, both together!...
But everything comes to an end, and this friendship too came to an end — a “bitter war” broke out!
How, and over what? — You will hear in a moment.
This year they both came up with a project: since times are bitter, let us rent a shared summer flat. One rent, one housekeeping, one maid, one lighting bill, one account at the shops, and so on.
It seems a straightforward plan; but[?] the trouble is that, besides one rent, one cart [furmanka], one housekeeping, there is also... one kitchen!
And it was precisely over the shared kitchen that the “war” broke out.
What happened? Well, listen:
The kitchen has one stove, and[?] just when my missus wants to put in a pot, my partner’s wife comes first with a pot. My missus takes out my partner’s wife’s pot and puts in her own pot. My partner’s wife sees it, takes out my missus’s pot and puts in her own. In the end the fire goes out and both pots stay raw. Well, all week long the pot-war was still a quiet one; but when Friday comes and both have to prepare for the Sabbath — then it’s “la-Yehudim” [ironic: then the real celebration starts]. My missus wants to be the first to cook the fish with the broth, and my partner’s wife also wants to be first.
My partner’s wife puts the fish-pan on the fire; my missus takes it off and puts on her own. Then[?] my partner’s wife came and did the same.
And what was the end? The end was that my partner’s wife lost her temper and said to my missus — “Chamka!” [Polish: boor, vulgar woman]...
My missus answered her: “Shmintelligentka!” [mocking inteligentka, “intellectual lady”]
My partner’s wife said: “Shut your mouth!”
My missus answered: “Don’t pull my tongue!” [don’t provoke me]
From word to word they went for each other’s hair, the manicured nails were set to work, brushes flew, rolling pins and other “weapons” — a real “war”...
When my partner and I arrived on Friday evening at our shared summer flat, we found both wives in bed with bandaged heads, with raw fish and with no dinners on the stove.
You hear; my partner and I have been running businesses together for many years now, and nothing — we get along even in big matters; while our wives made one joint business — a joint dacha — and see what came of it!
K.
The Double Nationalism. (A Talk among Ourselves)

(A talk among ourselves). By Argus.
There is an old philosophical problem over which Maimonides already toiled: the problem of “knowledge” and “free choice” — how one can[?] bind the two concepts together. Either way: if the Master of the Universe knows in advance everything that will happen, then He also knows that So-and-so will sin. And if He knows that, then man must sin and no longer has free choice, no choice at all. Why then is he punished for the sin? And if, on the other hand, one[?] says that he does deserve punishment because he had the choice not to sin — then[?] how could the Master of the Universe have known in advance how man would act later?
I am not dealing with philosophy now and will not enter the labyrinth of the intellectual combinations with which Maimonides resolves the logical contradiction. It is enough for me that as soon as mankind emerges from the phase[?] of naked wickedness and righteousness, it already had to find an answer to the hard question.
And now a fresh “heikhi timtza” [a case to be resolved] has arisen for us Jews, which we must answer. How can it be that all the Jews of the whole world should be one people, and at the same time the Jews of every country should be loyal and honest citizens of their homeland? The question is not new. Jewish ideologues racked their brains over it from the very first day, since[?] the first crack appeared in the wall of the Jewish ghetto.
After the Paris Jewish Sanhedrin, which Napoleon set up in connection with the equalisation of Jews and Frenchmen, the issue was studied, and then it was ruled that there is indeed no Jewish world politics, only a faith which, like all other faiths, may extend over various countries. The other Jews of Western Europe followed the same path: they clung to the rights they had received and in return gave up, without reservation, their Jewish-national feeling.
In Eastern Europe and in [?] Jews were given no rights, so the question was not topical for them; they were allowed to be good national Jews. And it came out as if there were two kinds of Jews: one kind belonging to a Jewish International, and a second kind belonging to no one but their own country.
A breach in this conception came some sixty-odd years ago, when Crémieux founded the “Alliance Israélite Universelle” (Kol Yisrael Haverim) in Paris to help the Jews of Damascus during the blood libel, when Moses Montefiore of London travelled to rescue those same Jews, and when later an analogous aid society [Hilfsverein] was created in Berlin.
That means, then, that there does exist some thread[?] binding the Jews of the whole world together. [—] how does that fit?
The question became even more entangled with the rise of Zionism. Jewish world nationalism was activated, and at the same time we did not want to give up a single drop of our civic rights in all the countries where we have been long-settled for hundreds and thousands of years.
Gradually a theory of “dual statehood” was worked out. Just as a national[?] state is possible, in which two peoples sit in one state with the same rights, so for one individual a “dual statehood” is also possible — that he should belong to two states.
After all, Poles and Germans and Irish and Chinese in America are patriots of two countries — all the more so Jews, who possess still other dualisms, for example: two languages.
Once upon a time people had more than one god and more than one wife; when they realised that this was no good — it is no more. But why should one not be allowed to have two fatherlands, since life forces a person to wander from one country to another and to carry in his heart the love and attachment to his old home?
Well[?], what will happen if both fatherlands wage war on each other? There is an answer to that too: primacy of the country where one lives.
This solution of the problem is always easier than the answer to the philosophical question of “knowledge” and “free choice”; but it requires a prior axiom: that people must have freedom of movement, must be able to settle in and live their lives as is most convenient for them.
For the German Jews in particular the problem is not a hard one. They can argue to Hitler: we made an exchange with your grandfathers — they gave us rights, and in return we gave up our nationalism to them; now you are taking the rights away from us, so give us back our national feeling, which lies buried with you somewhere in the old archives. The German Jews do not have the sense to argue so — so we will argue for them.
But there are Jews all over the world, and Hitler’s antisemitism is beginning to spread everywhere like an epidemic, and wherever you cast a glance, you are confronted with this very question: how so, how can you be double citizens? That is also the meaning of the Endek [Polish National Democrats’] saying: “Do Palestyny!” [“To Palestine!”].
So we must polish well the theory of bi-nationalism, which answers this blockheaded question.
The Merchant Class Is in Danger! — What Does the New Census Law Smell Of?

[Trade — the census law; article.]
The just-dissolved Sejm favoured us in its time with a law on censuses [mandatory qualifications] for trade.
True, we managed to have the decree called off to the extent that it was promised that the census law would not be put into force so soon.
Lately, however — on the initiative of the Polish Merchants' Association in Poznań [Yiddish: Poyzn] — a questionnaire on the matter has been sent out through all the chambers of commerce, and one can expect the census law to become an accomplished fact very soon.
The authors of the bill, wrapping the impurity in piety [i.e. dressing an unclean motive in a respectable cloak], say that since the level of trade here in Poland is very low, this level must be raised by requiring a certain education of the merchants.
That is the official motive.
The real motive, however, is that the Poznań merchants, and lately also the Polish merchants of Warsaw, reckon that with the census they will be able to destroy the Jewish merchant and thereby get rid of Jewish competition.
We must fight the introduction of the census with all our strength, because it will bring disaster on all trade in the country — but the one to suffer most and soonest will be the Jewish merchant.
Let us analyse each kind of the projected census.
Education census
Are the merchants in Poland really so uneducated?
All over the world the most educated part of the population are the liberal professions and higher officials, and after them come, in order, the merchants, the craftsmen and finally the peasants.
And here, too, it is exactly the same — so what is all the noise about?
And if there must be an education census after all — how high is it to be, and above all, in what manner will the examination take place and who will the examiners be?
We know of cases where at an examining board the non-Jews were given the words „tate“ [daddy], „mame“ [mummy] to write, and the Jews księżyc [moon] and książę [prince].
We also know of cases where at an examining board a craftsman was asked whether he knew about Sobieski[?] and Grunwald, to which the examinee answered: Gentlemen, I have been a baker for 15 years and this is the first time I hear that such ingredients are supposed to go into baked goods!.
Practice.
This is one of the most dangerous points for us, because the bill also applies to employees. The question arises — the Jewish merchant will be pushed out of trade thanks to the census, so with whom will a Jewish employee be able to do his practice?
Material.
This kind of census is simply an absurdity. It would only be interesting to know the opinion of the bill's authors: in what way will they fix the amount of capital that one will have to show when opening a soda-water kiosk or a needle shop.
Moral.
This census we need not fear at all. The Jewish merchant possesses just as much morality as the non-Jew; only we want to know exactly what is meant by it, and above all who will issue this certificate of morality.
The concept of morality is very elastic, and involuntarily we recall the saying of an English writer who, after three years in prison, said: as it seems to me, it is not [only] honest people who sit in prison either...
Organization.
Every merchant will have to belong to an organization. That might not have been a danger. But it is quite possible that, let us say, the Zagłębie merchants will have to belong to the Polish Merchants' Association in Warsaw, and [Warsaw][?] will not admit any Jews.
As we see, the new census law is a death blow to the Jewish merchant; but even from the general standpoint of the state it is a ruin for trade in general.
There are already branches of life here where a census has been introduced — these are the liberal professions, for instance doctors, lawyers, etc.; and in Warsaw itself are there not hundreds of members of the liberal[?] professions who do not earn even the minimum for subsistence?
In trade, too, censuses have already been introduced, for example: the Polish cooperatives, which pay lower taxes and enjoy colossal credits — and did not the state recently write off 20 million of their debts?
Or was the bus industry, where concessions were introduced, saved?
And is it a way out of the difficult situation to restructure[?] — as has already been done even without a census law — [so that] newspapers may be sold only by „Ruch“ or [—] by the L.O.P.P. [LOPP — Air and Anti-Gas Defence League]?
True, the questionnaire itself foresees that the census law will apply only to new merchants, whereas[?] the old ones will be exempt from the law; but that does not make the danger a hair smaller, for we must after all care for the fate of our children, for whom almost all other sources of livelihood are closed.
For the time being the chambers of commerce are dealing with the question, and there, under the present circumstances, the law will, in our opinion, pass.
Let us then hope that the government, whose slogan is now „Face to the village“, and which is trying to close the so very wide scissors, i.e. the difference between village and town products — will understand that for the greater part of its citizens it is precisely free competition that is desirable, thanks to which everything becomes cheaper, and not the monopolization of trade in the hands of individuals; and that the government will not allow the census law to come into force!
Moshe Szwif[?].
An Open Letter — to the appointed president of the Sosnowiec kehilla, Mr. Tenzer

[Sosnowiec — kehilla; the craftsmen's bank; open letter.] In your article "What Remains of the Halakha" you touched upon [?] the Craftsmen's Bank, and you write that the Craftsmen's Bank in Sosnowiec is in a very favourable state, thanks to a number of serious communal workers who stand at the head of this [?] bank... We too, as co-operative members, know that at the head of the bank stand the chairman of the council, Dr. Herzman, and Dr. [Prokhaks?] Dr. Kohn. I believe they are serious persons, for after all they are not the Zionist thieves.. and "reckless good-for-nothings", as you always put it about the Zionists.
Therefore allow me to ask you: why did you take the 25,000 zł. that the kehilla received for the plot of land of the Szpigel family and deposit the whole sum in the Bank Handlowy, and did not even find it necessary to put at least a small sum of 5000 zł. into a Jewish co-operative bank, where the poor craftsman and small trader gets a small loan and also a discount, whereas in the Bank Handlowy a small trader or craftsman can surely not enjoy credit so easily...
And when, 2 months ago, I put the same question to a serious member of the management — why the kehilla deposited the whole sum in the Bank Handlowy and did not find it necessary to deposit a small sum in a Jewish co-operative bank, whose president is no Zionist, God forbid, but Dr. Herzman — that person too was surprised and took the liberty of putting the same question to Dr. Herzman, who answered that he too had demanded it of his colleague Tenzer, but Tenzer dug in his heels and said "no" with a capital aleph: I want it so. Now, Mr. Tenzer: where is your fairness towards a Jewish co-operative bank? And where do your kosher little Jews sit [?]... And if you justify the bank as a serious institution, then how did you act against that very bank? Yes, Mr. Commissar, do not play a false role, and be a little more serious and consistent.
Jakub Szymon Feldman,
co-operative member of the Craftsmen's Bank in Sosnowiec.
An Old-New Matter

[Reader's letter — the newspaper and the neighbours.] In the last few days we received a letter from one of our regular readers.
The reader writes to us as follows:
"I was ashamed to come into the editorial office to tell you about what is weighing on me, so I am doing it in writing.
I have a shop; ever since the 'Zaglembier Tsaytung' has been appearing I have been a regular reader; I simply cannot do without the 'Zagl. Tsayt.'
But — believe me or not — I never get to read the newspaper that I buy; do you know why? Because of my neighbours.
My neighbours snatch it away [?] when the newspaper seller brings me the paper, before I have even managed to take a look in it; it is not seemly for me to quarrel with my neighbours — but it annoys me greatly that people want to exploit someone else's livelihood like this.
On the contrary, give me advice what to do; I begrudge the newspaper, but I can no longer bear my neighbours; even on Shabbat they come into my home, sit themselves down — and nothing; am I obliged to supply them with a newspaper every week?
Give advice, Mr. Editor [Panie redaktorze]!
Your reader M. —n."
Our Panorama.

[Zagłębie — weekly feuilleton.] By Ben Amotz.
(A kehilla that must be united. — Jewish "unity". — Prizes for praying. — "Al mikra megilla" for Eicha. — The disrupted domestic peace in the Sosnowiec "German" synagogue. — 10 members out of 13 "kahal-men".)

Zagórze must — in our opinion — be united.
In the history of the strengthening of Judaism, the deeds of the Jews of Zagórze must be written in golden letters.
No small thing, what Zagórze — which lies geographically between Dąbrowa and Sosnowiec — has accomplished in the field of strengthening religious feeling among the youth! What the "Aguda" [Agudat Israel] did not manage to do in the course of its many years of existence — it did not find the signal [?] that would awaken in today's youth the desire to pray — has been [printed "אין" for "איז"] discovered in the holy community of Zagórze, thanks to the Jewish "unity" that reigns there.
The holy community of Zagórze numbers thirty families in all. It goes without saying that such a "large" Jewish collective cannot live in peace among itself: first, for the sake of the neighbouring communities, as a moral lesson that a kahal without a quarrel looks like a rabbi without a spodik [fur hat]; and second, we do live in some sort of "democratic" age, when every schlemiel makes Shabbat for himself and no longer depends on public opinion.
And so the Zagórze kehilla indeed split apart and founded no fewer than three minyanim.
Well, even that would not have been so bad: each minyan would get its "portion", and peace upon Israel. But the trouble is that the division was not made proportionally; rather, every "shtibl" was given a "free hand"...
Well, in this field a fierce competition flared up: each minyan pays higher prices for a "head"; one is not particular whether the worshipper is a "red" or a "blue", as long as he is "a lad with a pair of trousers"...
Because of the situation that arose, one of the minyanim [printed "מניגים"] announced a prize for young worshippers: besides an honour [kibbud] on [?] Shabbat, every worshipper gets a cinema ticket...
As our correspondent reports, the gabbaim of a second minyan decided that every worshipper is to be insured with a foreign company; but how much truth there is in this report, we do not know.
All we want is for the wide Jewish world to learn of the splendid deeds of the Zagórze kehilla, where a means was invented to "trick" the youth into praying: they get cinema tickets, as long as they have prayed...
———
Famous, too, should be the minyan in Będzin that has a Torah reader [baal koreh] who this past Tisha b'Av "turned" it into Purim.
It happened unexpectedly. In a mood of Eicha the congregation prays Maariv, then sits down with the tallow candles in their hands; the "shtibl" is wrapped in Tisha b'Av mourning, and suddenly:
— The blessing "al mikra megilla"...
— What? Mad or out of your mind? — protests are heard from the worshippers — what kind of mockery are you making of the nation's destruction, eh?
— Quiet! Calm down, gentlemen! — the baal koreh cries out — I will give you to understand that for Megillat Eicha one must say the blessing "al mikra megilla"...
— On the contrary, you tell me too [?]: don't we have Purim all year round? When a "gotigirster" [?] strongman shouts in the streets: "With a mighty hand will I rule" — well, can that be possible if not on Purim?
The argument worked; the worshippers calmed down and resolved to make public [the deed of] their baal koreh, who introduced a "change of season" and over Megillat Eicha said the blessing:
— "Al mikra megilla"...
———
The head gabbai of the "German" synagogue in Sosnowiec finds himself, poor man, in great embarrassment and does not know which side to go along with.
In the Sosnowiec "German" synagogue peace and quiet always reigned; the committee fulfilled its tasks perfectly, so that there were no "victors" and no "vanquished" either. But ever since R' Bertshe went out into the kehilla dance, the "domestic peace" in the synagogue committee has been disrupted too.
The reason is simple: the first founders of the synagogue committee — by the way, people who bear the burden and allow themselves to spend with a generous hand — do not want a commissioner to be found among the worshippers, despite the fact that the commissioner has "Jewish military" behind him, which can do no more than check the sealed [plombed] poultry; but still — a commissioner...
But there are also in the synagogue committee such as the commissioner has "arranged" [?] into his kehilla carriage; they surely cannot be so brazen, so they say: our dear one, "be thou our chief"...
———
But bad off is the third side, the head gabbai: the split has hit him hard, for he sees that because of the disrupted domestic peace no one will suffer but the synagogue...
———
Fortunately the dispute in the committee of the Million Campaign in Sosnowiec has been liquidated.
As is known, a few weeks ago a meeting of the town's notables was held in Sosnowiec about collecting the quota [contingent] sum for "CEKABE" [the central interest-free loan fund].
At the meeting a committee was elected, then a presidium, as is written and customary — and, Jews, open your purses.
But the kehilla nominees [?], who are also members of the committee, felt wronged. How can it be? — they argued — we did not get a single minister's portfolio? Not one of us was elected to the presidium? The soul aches [printed "כואת"]! We will not be able to look our commissioner in the eye!
So the "wronged" ones girded their loins, stormed every session and sent ultimatums: if their honour is not restored, they will have to make use of their rebbe's power:
— "With a mighty hand will I rule over you"...
The committee members took fright at the "scare" ["straszunek"] and agreed that, so that both strongmen of the Jewish street be satisfied, two chairmen and two treasurers would be elected.. and all is firm and established.
———
The Jews of Sosnowiec may now open their purses, for "peace" has been restored in the relief committee, and there are two chairmen and two treasurers...
— "10 members and 13 kahal-men"...
Ben Amotz.
Credits for Artisans

[Poland — economy; artisans and credit.] The efforts of the Union of Chambers of Crafts to enlarge and ease the credit for artisans on the part of the Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego [National Economy Bank] have been successful. The interest rates have been reduced to 2 and a half per cent; the institutions that distribute the credits take one and a half per cent. So from 1 September 1935 the credit will cost the artisan only 4 per cent a year. The reduced rates also apply to the old credits that have not yet been repaid.
The bank has also increased the quota of discount credits from 6 300,000 zł. to 7 and a half million zł. Despite the fact that in some places the credits were not used — the bank has therefore expressed its consent that credits not used in one district may be transferred to another place where such credits are lacking.
The amount of credit each artisan can obtain has been raised as follows: in Gdynia, Bydgoszcz, Katowice and Poznań up to 4000 zł.; for all other districts — 3000 zł.
The 7 and a half million zł. that the said bank has now allocated are not a one-time sum; they will remain with the institutions that distribute the credit as a permanent artisans' credit.
Until now an artisan received the credit for 18 months; now he will be able to receive it for 30 months.
Artisans will continue to receive the credits on bills of exchange with 2 guarantors (endorsers); the bill, however, may not be issued for more than one year. The procedure will be as follows:
If an artisan receives a loan of 1200 zł., he issues a bill of 200 zł. for 3 months, a bill of 200 zł. for 6 months, a bill of 200 zł. for 9 months, and a bill for 600 zł. for one year. After the year, that 600-złoty bill will again be exchanged for 3 bills of 200 zł. each. Until now the bills had to be renewed every 3 months. The credits for artisans will continue, as hitherto, to be distributed through the K.K.O. [probably Komunalna Kasa Oszczędności, the municipal savings bank].
The credits for artisans until now were not exhausted; the procedure for obtaining these credits did not satisfy the borrowers. What was the reason for this? The first obstacle for artisans in taking these credits was the high interest, the great difficulty of renewing the bills every 3 months and of obtaining the guarantors' signatures every 3 months, the short term for which the credits were granted, and finally the difficulties made by the institutions that distributed the credit.
The new credit regulations for artisans remove the obstacles to a certain extent.
One must further hope that the distribution committees will also remove the remaining bureaucracy in selecting guarantors and securing the credits, and then the credits will be a boon to the artisans, who thirst for these credits.
Radio Corner

[Poland — radio; interview.] A conversation with the general director of Polish Radio, Mr. Roman Starzyński.
On 8 July Mr. Roman Starzyński, until now director of the cabinet of the Minister of Posts and Telegraphs, temporarily took over the post of general director of Polish Radio. In a conversation with a representative of "Antena" [the Polish Radio weekly] Director Mr. Starzyński expressed himself as follows:
The taking over of the post of general director of Polish Radio is connected with the government's policy regarding domestic radio affairs. Almost all European radio stations are in the hands of the state, and therefore this important and responsible branch of work could not remain exclusively with private initiative.
I emphasize, however, that there can be no talk here whatsoever of nationalizing (étatizing) the radio; this is only for the time being, until the general meeting, which will elect a new council and board, and until then no change of an organizational or personnel character will take place.
Polish Radio has very healthy development[?] possibilities, as the growth of subscribers [each] year[?] can show. Everyone must admit that thanks to the government factors the radio has for about a year now been becoming ever more popular — on the one hand through the improved and enriched programmes, on the other hand — through the cheapening and making it possible for broad circles to acquire the appropriate radio set. This has a very great cultural significance.
Even "Antena", both in its outward appearance and in its editorial form, which does not lag behind the best European radio papers, I also regard as a very positive phenomenon.
It is hard to find in all Poland another such institution that has a secure million[?] in revenue as Polish Radio has. But one must not forget that the expenses too are quite large, and this not only because of the programmes but also because of investment needs. Polish Radio must have its own building in order to be able to work normally. These expenses an ordinary radio budget cannot cover.
After the actual owner of Polish Radio has been determined, it will work like any ordinary joint-stock company. All this, however, will have to be set up so that the radio carries out one hundred per cent its social, cultural and educational tasks, and indeed stands in one row with the first-rank European radio stations.
Attention, Radio Hares!

[Poland — radio; law and penalties.] Listening to the radio "na gapę" [as a freeloader] carries a heavy penalty.
Who is a radio hare [Polish zając radiowy — an unlicensed listener]? Anyone who makes himself a radio set or buys one in a shop and does not report it at the nearest post office, so as thereby[?] not to pay the monthly fee.
Under Art. 28 of the Law on Posts, Telegraph and Telephone, such a thing is regarded as a serious offence, and a severe penalty threatens.
The law says: "Anyone guilty of installing or using post, telegraph and telephone installations contrary to the provisions of the law is punished with arrest of up to three months and a fine of up to three thousand złotys, or with one of these penalties. Together with the penalty, the installation may also be confiscated for the benefit of the state.
From this it can be seen that a radio hare is regarded as an offender, because by not registering his radio set and not paying the monthly fee he breaks the law, under which one is explicitly obliged to register and to pay the radio fee.
These "black listeners" are the greatest enemies of the radio, because owing to the reduced income of the radio station it cannot develop properly, and it is hindered from improving and enriching the programmes.
The democratic conduct of the head of the Tax Office (Urząd Skarbowy) in Dąbrowa, Mr. Szczenk

[Dąbrowa — tax office and taxes; a merchant's letter.]
With the departure from office of the former head of the Tax Office (Urząd Skarbowy) in Dąbrowa [Dąbrowa Górnicza], Mr. Tarnowski — after whom the merchants in general and the Jews in particular shed not a single tear (for reasons I already wrote about in their time) — the post of head (naczelnik) was taken over by Mr. Szczenk [?].
In these few words I wish to state with pleasure that the present head, Mr. Szczenk, is equal to his task, is highly cultured, is a European in the full sense of the word, and by his conduct has already, in this short time, won great sympathy and respect among the merchants of Dąbrowa, without distinction of faith or nationality.
We merchants understand quite well that taxes we must pay, and that without taxes the state could not exist; as loyal citizens we do it quite willingly. But we have the right to demand of the officials that they treat us equally with everyone, and this, unfortunately, we did not have in the time of Mr. Tarnowski. On the contrary, our feelings were often trampled underfoot, and the blood boiled in our veins when we learned how Mr. Tarnowski dealt with the petitioners when they came to ask him to spread their taxes into instalments or to postpone the dates of auctions (licytacje), etc.
Now the situation has changed. It is a pleasure to come in to the noble Mr. Szczenk: he receives the petitioner in a very courteous manner, he goes deeply into each person's situation, and if it is at all possible, he settles the matter.
It goes without saying that he cannot settle everything as the taxpayer would wish, but the refusal comes in a very cultured form, so that the taxpayer, having the fullest confidence in the head, Mr. Szczenk, leaves satisfied, interprets it for the good, and himself defends the honourable official.
I consider it my duty to convey these few words to the public, and it remains to hope that Mr. Szczenk will continue on the same path, which brings good results both for the State Treasury and for the merchants of Dąbrowa.
B. Rechnic.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Ekev)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.]
Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Ekev
The Portion.
—o—
a) "Thou shalt be blessed above all peoples" (7:14)
When you look at how other nations behave, you may well be "blessed", fortunate, because however bad you are, Jew, you are still better than they... No'am Megadim.
—o—
b) "Thou shalt not covet the silver or the gold that is on them" (ibid., 25)
Do not covet the gold and silver that the service of idols brings. Imrei Ḥen.
—o—
c) "And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee" (10:12)
Our Sages expounded from this: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven. Rashi.
Everything is in the hands of Heaven, everything depends on God, and even if you pray to Him it is not certain that He will grant your wish — except the fear of Heaven: for the fear of Heaven, if you pray, God will surely grant your wish... Rabbi Mendele of Kotzk.
—o—
d) "And to serve Him with all your heart" (7:14 [?])
What is service of the heart? It is prayer. Rashi.
In Lublin there was a preacher (maggid), R' Berish Halpern. When in the little town of Shelishtz [?] (Siedliszcze?) near Rejowiec (Lublin district) a terrible blood libel took place, the maggid took up the defence of the accused. He came out so sharply that he was arrested.
Sitting in prison, he prayed aloud, as was his custom. Once the prison warden came to him and asked him:
"Why do you shout so loudly when you pray? There are many Christians here who also say the morning prayer, and they say it so quietly."
The maggid answered him:
"Because their God is near them, He hangs on the wall of the prison cell... but our God sits so high, in heaven, so I must shout loudly..."
For this the prison warden dealt him a slap, and that same night — so they tell in Lublin — the warden suffered a stroke (apoplexy).
• • •
In Kotzk there was a young married man who complained to Rabbi Mendele that his head ached and he could not pray.
"What has a headache to do with prayer? Prayer is a service of the heart, not a service of the head..."
—o—
e) "A land whose stones are iron" (8:9)
Do not read "its stones" (avaneha) but "its builders" (boneha). Ta'anit 4a.
The builders, the builders of the Land of Israel, must be hard as iron, they may not be soft [?], and so too the builders of the people, the Torah scholars... Rabbi Yitzhak Nissenbaum.
—o—
f) "That your days may be multiplied" (11:21)
They said to Rabbi Yoḥanan: There are old men in Babylonia. He wondered and said: It is written "that your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, upon the land" — but not outside the Land. When they told him: They come early to the synagogue and stay late, he said: That is what helps them (Berakhot 8a).
Because they rose earlier than everyone to go to the synagogue, and went to bed later than everyone, they lived longer after all, had more of the days and nights, and did not sleep them away...
• • •
"The fear of the Lord prolongeth days, but the years of the wicked shall be shortened" (Ecclesiastes [sic; actually Proverbs 10:27]).
A righteous man lives longer, he makes more use of his days; "but the years of the wicked shall be shortened" — they sleep them away... Kotnot Or [?].
Adw.(?) S. Geliszkowski — The Bastard (48)

[Literature — serialised novel.] Adw.[?] S. Geliszkowski: The Bastard. A thrilling tragic novel of a prodigy (an illui). 48)

Painful, full of grief and anguish, were for her then the moments when, as though through a fog, she glimpsed Leon. As if from a tight clamp she would tear herself loose, push away, and flee from the thought that gave her no rest. A worm gnawed at her heart, and to drive it away she went every evening to the best restaurants, spending her time until the grey dawn, and coming home like a dead woman she threw herself into bed, falling asleep under the intoxication of the wines and liqueurs.
Often she would let one [printed "eyger"] of her new acquaintances accompany her home, but she would forcibly remove him from the room when he wished to stay.
Empty had her heart become: no desire for anyone, and no wish at all, except the wish to stifle the feeling for that man whom she could by no means forget.
Very hard she fought against the feeling; she understood and felt that she was deceiving herself, that somewhere there, deep in the hidden recesses of her heart, there was a great wound that would not heal so quickly.
But in spite of all this she fought the feeling gallantly and tried to tear it out by the root. And though she felt she was already tired of such a life, she did not cast it off, and every evening visited the best restaurants, made merry until the grey dawn and acquired ever more new acquaintances.
The gilded youth paid large bills for her, the most expensive wines flowed like water; nothing was too hard or too dear for them for the truly beautiful Balbina, who excited them with her hot body and shapely limbs, which kindled in them a wild fire of desire. But for that very reason she pushed them away from herself with mockery and laughter, shouting under the intoxication of the wine: "Once I loved, once I desired — and that is all; I do not want to know you any more. Waiter, wine!" — she cried, raising the goblet on high.
And her words excited them even more; still greater grew the desire for the beautiful Balbina, of whom they could by no means find out who she was and what she wanted.
There were those who followed her like a shadow, came to her house and, for a good reward, held a conversation with the maid, in order to become more closely and intimately acquainted with the mysterious Balbina; but the maid could say nothing more than that she lived alone and received no man at all.
And once — it was just before Christmas, at the same time and possibly even on the same day on which Leon received the indictment — she went as always into the great hall of the restaurant "Diana".
The hall was packed full. All the tables were occupied; there remained only the one table which was reserved for her, right by the stage. The large orchestra was playing, and it seemed as if all the guests were eating and drinking in the rhythm of the orchestra and to the sounds of the beat.
— For you, madame — the waiter came up to her and asked her what she was ordering.
— As always — came the answer.
Not far from her table sat a middle-aged gentleman of solid, handsome appearance, sketching something with a pencil in his notebook and from time to time casting his glance at Balbina.
From the very first glance one could see that this was a man who belonged to the artistic family, as was testified by his head of long grey hair and his long black cravat, and by the fact that he very quickly [printed "der gikh"] drew her portrait in profile with his pencil. And when he had finished drawing, he wrote a few words on his visiting card, called the waiter and asked him to hand it all over to Balbina.
— Please, madame, this is for you — said the waiter, handing her the visiting card and another sheet of paper.
Balbina takes the visiting card and reads:
Honoured Madame!
I am an artist. You will ascertain this from the drawing which I have enclosed. For several weeks now I have been looking for as alluring a model as you are, in order to be able to begin my sculpture in white alabaster under the title "The Woman and the Cradle-Child". And if you were to grant me the happiness and agree to appear in my masterpiece, it would be the greatest happiness for me.
P.S. I await your answer. Max Bloch.
Having read the letter through, she looked at the drawing of herself and was enchanted.
— Who gave you this? — she asks the waiter, who stood waiting for an answer.
— The gentleman who is sitting here not far from you — he answers, pointing to the artist.
She turns her head and meets his gaze.
— Your drawing is wonderful — she said to him when he had sat down at her table.
— I thank you for the compliment — he says with a bad Polish accent — I would be happy if you would not refuse my request.
— Are you not from Poland, then? — she asked him.
— No, I am from Berlin, gracious lady; do you perhaps understand German?
— Please. You may speak German.
— As already said — he began to speak in a good, rich German — I am a sculptor, and in about five months there will be held in our Berlin an exhibition of paintings and sculptures; the prize for the best work amounts to half a million marks, but the material side does not concern me. The most important thing for me is to win the first prize for my composition, and for that I need a woman such as you are. Do not take this for a compliment, gracious lady; no, it is no compliment. We artists deal only with beauties, but you are an exception. My work will represent a woman who, after a shipwreck, finds herself on the waves of the raging sea in a small boat, quieting a newborn child at her breast.
A shudder passed through her body on hearing the composition of the sculpture for which she was to pose.
— God — she cries inwardly — this is, after all, a piece of my own life; the man must be a prophet.
— Have you really found no one more suitable than me? — she asks, looking into his handsome and clever eyes.
— No, madame, my artistic instinct could lead me to no better model than you.
— Will you, then, remain in Warsaw the whole time?
— No, madame, my work must be completed in Berlin.
— That means that I would have to travel to Berlin?
— Gracious lady, I will cover all your expenses, and besides that you can receive such a large sum — half a million marks. I believe that if your family affairs allow it, then all other difficulties can be removed.
— But yes, sir, I understand, but how can I let myself travel with you God knows where? Why, you might yet sell me — she laughed with a roguish smile.
— In Berlin one does not buy women, and further than Berlin you will not travel; besides, madame, this is my proposal and my ardent wish, and no compulsion. You can, after all, take counsel with your relatives and friends; inquire in Berlin about the sculptor Max Bloch, and you will know who I am, and then you may boldly entrust your person to me.
That same night she did not close an eye, thinking about the proposal of the artist Bloch. In her mind her fantasies ran wild, and she already saw herself as the owner of a large sum of money. Oh, how happy she will be — she cries out; but soon she again feels the longing of her heart; again, as though under a thick fog, Leon's silhouette appears, and she grows sad.
— Yes — she cries out — there is nothing to deliberate; tomorrow already she will tell him that she is going with him to Berlin. It will be better for her when she leaves the city where she has suffered so much and suffers still. "Change your place, change your luck," her father always used to say. Once and for all — tear the threads with the city, and the rest time will show...
Weeping and torn was her heart when she stood at the window of the second-class carriage and watched the great Warsaw houses run away from her. She felt how her heart tore itself out into the open and did not want to travel with her; it wanted to stay here, in the great, bustling Warsaw, whither some secret magnetic force was drawing.

"Der Kokh-Lefl" ["The Cooking Ladle"] — A Bit of Dacha Delight

"Der Kokh-Lefl" ["The Cooking Ladle"]
Humour and satire. Compiled by Amotzlu.

A Bit of Dacha Delight.

When the heat waves come along
I let the town and people sweat,
I turn into a hare at once —
To the village I am drawn,
To calm my nerves a little,
To stretch out on the grass.

Gone is the taste of smoke and sulphur,
The deckchair [lezhak — leżak] is my furniture,
I enjoy repose and quiet,
I get no more receipts [kvites — kwity],
I needn't write any [tsites?],
So I really gather strength.

From creditors I'm exempt,
I heed them like the tomcat [i.e. pay them no mind],
They don't know my new address,
And in the village my account is clean,
For I really don't want to be a sucker,
And I study well the laws of gorging.

Only one thing is bad:
That it doesn't last a whole year —
It would have done people good.
I tell you, and listen to me:
Whoever thought up the dacha
Should be wished eternal life.
M. H.

The public workers grow gloomy, the sick get no help, the hens [?] and the roosters [?] are not sealed [with the kashrut seal], the magistrate evicts dozens of Jewish families, on Shabbat Nachamu the public ate treyf [?] "galaretka" [calf's-foot jelly]. [?] darkness is, after all, not nice.
So the wise men of the town gathered, the magicians [khartumim] of the "encoffined" [?] kehilla, and asked one another:
— "What is the halakha?"...
But none of the magicians found the right answer. Suddenly they heard the cantor with the beadles and the gravediggers saying a Mi She-berakh for the head of the kehilla on his departure — only then did it become clear that

In summer — when the wife is at the dacha, one cannot write plain letters, the way a husband writes to a wife.

What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: A Naive Silesian Swindled

[Head of the local section; Będzin — crime, fraud.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, ס״ז[?] / 17 Av 5695 — piątek 16 sierpnia 1935 [Friday, 16 August 1935].)
Będzin
A Naive Silesian Swindled.
At the local horse market a Silesian, a certain Friedrich, sold a horse for 80 zł. and set off on his way home.
As he came along Czeladzka Street, an elegantly dressed gentleman approached Friedrich and persuaded him to go with him to Podzamcze[?] Street, where an auction of horses was taking place.
The naive Silesian let himself be talked into it and went with the stranger. When they found themselves at the corner of Kołłątaja and Modrzejowska[?] streets, the unknown stranger bent down and picked up a small packet.
"I've found a rather large sum of money," the stranger cried out with joy, "come quickly up to Góra Zamkowa [Castle Hill], where we will share the find..."
At a certain moment someone came up to them and asked whether they had not found a packet of money which he had lost. At the same time this man began to search the pockets of Friedrich and of his companion, shouting: "Give me back my money."
Friedrich, afraid that he would be suspected of having found the "find," hurried away, but later he discovered that the proceeds for the horse had been stolen from him...
Great Meeting of the Committee to Aid Refugees from Germany

[Będzin — refugees from Germany, meetings.]
In connection with the intensified persecution of Jews in Germany, the local committee to aid the Jewish refugees organized a meeting in the "Światowid" [hall], which drew a very huge crowd; the hall was packed full.
After the speeches of Dr. Weinzieher, Wygodzki and others, appropriate resolutions were adopted.
By the way, we express a sharp protest against those who stand at the head of the committee, who did not take care that the Yiddish text on the poster about the meeting should not be written in such an ignorant "Yiddish".
Again They Are Going to Set Up a "Synagogue Committee"

[Będzin — kehilla, synagogues.]

"The Jewish kehilla of Będzin greets the conference of the Yiddish Scientific Institute and wishes it success in its work."

A Jewish woman from Poland who spent this year's season in Karlsbad left a diamond ring in a jewellery shop on the "Alte Wiese".

Sosnowiec — The Windows of the Beth Midrash in Dańdówka Smashed

[Sosnowiec — Violence against Jews.]
Sosnowiec
The windows of the beth midrash in Dańdówka smashed.
In Weiler's house in Dańdówka is the local beth midrash. On Saturday at minchah a rather large mob gathered in the courtyard, who had been incited to attack those who were in the beth midrash at the time.
When one of the gang, a known brawler [awanturnik], wanted to force his way into the beth midrash and the Jews did not let him, he smashed, in revenge, all the windows of the beth midrash.
The Jews who were inside lived through mortal terror and were afraid to go out, lest they be attacked by the incited mob.
When [seeing] the situation, Rabbi Englard of Sosnowiec, who represents the local community, was informed by telephone. Rabbi Englard intervened at the local police commissariat, from which a police detachment was soon sent out; it put the chief brawler in chains and dispersed the mob.
Around 11 at night, when order had been restored by the police, the Jews left the beth midrash.
The Ryczałt Tax for the Year 1935

[Taxes — Merchants.]
The ryczałt [lump-sum] tax for the year 1935.
We learn from reliable sources that it is already completely certain that from New Year 1936 the present system of fixing the ryczałt according to the turnover of the year 1930 will no longer be applied.
A new ryczałt system will be introduced, which will be based on newly collected material that will be gathered about each merchant separately.
Every merchant will have the possibility of renouncing the ryczałt.

A Public Activist Has Died

Robbed of His Clothes and Left Naked

Life in Kielce — Went to His Wife in Suchedniów and Ate the Sabbath Meal at the Szydłowiec Rebbe's

[Kielce — everyday life; humour.]
Life in Kielce.
(Date boxes: Friday, Parshat Ekev[?] / 17 Av 5695 — piątek 16 sierpnia 1935 [Friday, 16 August 1935].)
Went to his wife in Suchedniów and ate the Sabbath meal at the Szydłowiec Rebbe's.
Last Friday towards evening Yekil Sz. packed his luggage, took along a full suitcase[?] of dry and „wet“ things and went out to the park to wait for the bus.
From the great heat in the bus Yekil, tired from the whole day, fell asleep, and so he rode all the way past Szydłowiec.
Here Yekil came to, gave a good yawn, looked up at the sky and asked himself where he already was. Hearing from the conductor that they were already past Szydłowiec, Yekil simply felt sick and broke out in a sweat. He grabbed the suitcase[?] and started running into town. Here he already saw the lit candles in the Jewish houses, and from a neighbouring house the hymn „Lekha Dodi“ rang out festively.
Yekil stood for a while, thought and thought, and decided to go to the Szydłowiec Rebbe. Coming in to the Rebbe, he found them in the middle of Kabbalat Shabbat. The congregation looked in amazement at the strange guest with the suitcase[?] in his hand, who had come so late to travel to the Rebbe.
After the prayers Yekil told the Szydłowiec Rebbe the whole story and asked him to allow him to be his guest over the Sabbath.
The Szydłowiec Rebbe even gave him a good scolding — why does a Jew allow himself to set out from home so late? — but he took pity on him and received him as a guest, and right after the Sabbath ended (motzei Shabbat) Yekil travelled back to Kielce.
At the railway station in Kielce, getting off the train, Yekil met his wife, who had also arrived on the last train from Suchedniów to find out the reason why her husband had not come for the Sabbath. Both looked at each other like two roosters and could not get a word out.
So the two of them walked „in silence“ through the Kielce streets until they came home. Here they became very talkative, began telling each other what had happened, and in the course of it they started to quarrel; it would have become quite „homely“, but thanks to the neighbours everything passed off peacefully.
— Your[?] husband — said a neighbour woman — has, God forbid, done nothing bad at all, for instead of spending the holy Sabbath in Suchedniów, where they are not so strict about Jewishness, he preferred to spend the Sabbath at the Szydłowiec Rebbe's.. and that had its effect...
A Great Deal of Bitter Truth. For the Attention of Jewish Summer Holidaymakers.

[Society — Jews and their neighbours at the summer resorts.] At a summer resort not far from Łódź, the local hooligan rabble recently began to show off their Jew-beating tricks. Because of this the local kehilla, together with the Jewish villa occupants, decided to send a delegation to the local priest, in order to ask him to admonish his run-wild "holy flock" a little.
The priest received the delegation in a friendly manner and promised to fulfil their request. On this occasion he held a long conversation with the visitors, in which he made the following remarks:
— I am no antisemite and in general I cannot understand how a true Christian can hate people, and consequently also Jews. Yet it often[?] happens that individual Jews, by their tactless conduct, themselves draw[?] upon themselves the hatred accumulated against them among the mob.
Let us take as an example the behaviour of a part of the Jewish holidaymakers, and especially of the female holidaymakers.
Picture such a situation: in a village or small town where the summer residences are located, there live hundreds of landless and unemployed people in the most terrible conditions. They go about with their wives and children ragged and worn out, live all year round on potatoes, and a piece of white bread is[?] for many of them a real ideal.
At the same time they suddenly see Jewish women who are simply bathing in lard and honey and who appear every hour in different, many-coloured clothes.
Further: just show me one climatic resort where Jews stay that has no "dancing" [dance hall], where young people do not carouse whole days and nights and "mrudert"[?] a whole world.
You must not forget that all this together hands the antisemites a good argument for fanning anti-Jewish incitement, for stirring up the mob and for steering its embitterment and anger in the direction of "the smallest estate" — against the whole Jewish people.
Incidentally, one more aspect of the conduct of this respectable group of Jews shocks me.
The Jewish people is now living through the hardest period in its long history. The Jews in Germany, who were after all the pride of the people, have now been exposed to shame and mockery. Everywhere the Jew is robbed[?] and hunted, and his life grows ever[?] harder.
Surely the horrifying experiences of the German and other tormented Jews ought to have affected the minds of their fellow nationals in Poland; unfortunately, in the behaviour of the Jewish Lolas, Folas and Sankas [Polish pet names of Jewish women] at the summer resorts one cannot notice that they are much troubled by the fate of their brothers and sisters abroad!
———
To the priest's remarks the Jewish delegation really had nothing to answer; it is, alas, a bitter truth that one sees with one's own eyes...
The Summer Colony for Poor Jewish Children in Zalesza

[Kielce — welfare and children.] As every year, this year too the parents' committee of the poor Jewish children in the public schools (folk-schools) has set up in the village of Zalesza[?] (near Kielce) a summer colony for some thirty-odd children.
The colony is located in a splendid wooded area; the rooms are very comfortable and very hygienically arranged, and the children, who suffer want and hunger all year round, feel very well, are looked after and content, and bless every day the deed of the initiators of the colony, Messrs. B. Górski, Mrs. Szpigelglas, Prof. Tencer, headed by Mr. Cytryn, who truly works for the good of this colony beyond his strength.
It is therefore a duty of the Jewish public in Kielce to support this committee. The main duty lies with the Jewish kehilla, which must support the colony.
Plenary Session of the Electoral College. Minister Car a Candidate in the Kielce District.

[Kielce — the Sejm elections.] On Wednesday at 10 a.m., in the hall of the Kielce city council, the plenary session of the electoral college took place, to elect candidates for deputies to the Sejm from the Kielce district (Kielce—Włoszczowa).
The session, which lasted several hours, was attended by 131 electors, among them the following Jews: Rabbi Rapaport (Kielce), Doctor Lejchter, Nusynowicz, L. Rozenberg, Pinkusowicz (all from Kielce) and Zemel (Włoszczowa).
After a lengthy deliberation the following candidates were chosen by secret ballot: Minister Car, Franciszek Basak, Antoni Klimas, Henryk Chyb[?]. As deputies (substitutes): Kazimierz Ostrowski, Kazimierz Hanasowski[?], Mrs. Plenkiewicz, Leon Paszylewski[?].
Boiler Explodes in a Soda-Water Factory

[Kielce region — accident.] In Mr. Zylberberg's soda-water factory in Chęciny, while the gas was being let into the boiler, the boiler exploded, as a result of which 2 workers were seriously injured.
The cause of the explosion has not yet been established.
"Linat HaTzedek" Stops Its Medical Aid Work

[Kielce — welfare and medicine.] The institution "Linat HaTzedek", well known in Kielce for decades, stopped dispensing medical aid to poor sick people several weeks ago.
The reason for this, as the leaders of this society explain to us, is the doctors' strike and, above all, the difficult financial situation of the society.
Great Rally of Maccabi Clubs of the Kielce and Silesian Voivodeships in Częstochowa

[Sport — Maccabi.] In connection with the 20th anniversary of Jewish sport in Częstochowa, a great rally of the Maccabi clubs of the Kielce and Bielitz (Bielsko) districts of Maccabi will take place in Częstochowa on 21 and 22 September (wrzesień) of this year. Besides these two districts, many sportsmen from a number of other cities, such as Warsaw, Łódź and Kraków, will take part in the rally — several hundred persons altogether. The exact programme of the rally was fixed last week in Katowice at a joint conference of both district executives, and it promises to be very interesting and varied. Within the framework of the rally there will be championship contests within each of the two districts in a number of sports (light athletics, sports games, football, boxing), as well as a competition between the two districts. Among the most impressive parts of the rally will be the gymnastics festival (Turnfest), in which all the participants will take part.
In connection with the rally and the jubilee, the organising committee is preparing a splendid jubilee publication devoted to the Maccabi movement in general, with special attention to the activity of the Maccabi clubs of the Kielce and Bielitz districts. A number of prominent Maccabi activists from the central office and the district executives will contribute to the jubilee publication. The publication will be furnished with several dozen photographs of the Maccabi movement in the past and present.
The rally is at the same time a preparation for the all-Polish rally of the Maccabi clubs, which will take place in Warsaw in 1936.

On Sunday the collection for the Million Campaign in Poland begins in Sosnowiec

Yesterday evening a large meeting was held in the premises of the Small Traders' Association in Sosnowiec in connection with starting the drive to collect the assigned quota sum, amounting to 17.500 zł., which the town of Sosnowiec must give for the Million Campaign proclaimed throughout Poland by the CEKABE [central of Jewish interest-free loan funds].
A fairly large number of the most respected communal workers of Sosnowiec took part in the meeting, as well as the delegate of the Central Committee (C. K.), Mr. Kagan.

Let us believe that, as in all the larger Jewish communities, in Sosnowiec too the drive will be crowned with success.

The Young Composer Szpilman on Polish Radio

[Sosnowiec — culture and music.]
(Photo caption:) Wł. Szpilman, before his appearance tomorrow on Polish Radio.
The already well-known, talented pianist and composer Wł. Szpilman (son of the well-known musician Szpilman in Sosnowiec) is appearing this time on Polish Radio with a programme of his own works. He will perform his étude „The Life of the Machine“ (the first part of this concert the radio listeners already had the opportunity to hear during the broadcast „Concert of Polish Music“), as well as his latest[?] work „Pictures from the Years of Childhood“.
Szpilman is a modern composer through and through. The theme of his work is simply[?] life itself. „The Life of the Machine“ is a reflection of the machine, its rhythm and the force of labour; „The Pictures from the Years of Childhood“, on the other hand, are already another moment in life — a lovely memory of a bright past.
The critics, who regard Szpilman's works as mature, individual creations of a young composer, predict that the radio broadcast will be one of the most successful.
Wł. Szpilman has composed a great deal, which he himself has already performed on various stages with tremendous success. (Among other things he has composed: a violin concerto, a Prelude in A minor, two nocturnes, a symphonic fantasy.)
Recently Szpilman has thrown himself into Eretz-Israel motifs, he is working on them very diligently, and in a short time he will present[?] himself with his new kind of work.
Szpilman's concert takes place on Polish Radio on Saturday the 24th of this month at 4.15 p.m.

Chaim Binkowski, of Blessed Memory

[Sosnowiec — obituary.]
At the age of 69 the well-known popular communal activist Chaim Binkowski, of blessed memory, has died in Sosnowiec.
The deceased was a type of the old generation, a man of the people in the full sense of the word. Being himself a craftsman, he worked for many years with self-sacrifice in the ranks of the artisans. He was a founder of the Artisans' Association and of the Artisans' Bank, where until his last day he was a member of the board. At the last kehilla elections he was elected a parnas (councillor), and he stood close to the national (Zionist) ranks.
A great crowd from all strata of the Jewish population took part in the funeral.
At the open grave there spoke: on behalf of the Artisans' Bank — Dr. Herzman[?], and on behalf of the Association — Mr. Eksztajn.
